<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_script_include"><sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>package_private</access><active>true</active><api_name>x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator</api_name><caller_access/><client_callable>false</client_callable><description>Central transition-guard helper for the case state-machine. Provides canTransitionToOpen/canTransitionToInProgress/canTransitionToResolved/canTransitionToClosed, validateNoBacktransition, isAgentInGroup, and getOpenTaskCountForCase. Called by all Flow Designer flows, Business Rules, and UI Actions in the x_casemgmt scope. ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase ChangeCaseFileStateService. All transition rules and verbatim error messages are traced to AAP Section 0.5.5 and 0.7.4. canTransitionToResolved blocks the In Progress -> Resolved transition with the verbatim message "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case." when any child x_casemgmt_case_task has status != Closed. validateNoBacktransition blocks any -> Draft with the verbatim message "Cases cannot be returned to Draft." and Closed -> * with the verbatim message "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified." Role checks use gs.getUser().hasRole(role_name) only. Group-membership checks use GlideRecord on sys_user_grmember (read-only). Open-task counting uses GlideAggregate on x_casemgmt_case_task. Contains zero hardcoded sys_id literals in references and zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description><mobile_callable>false</mobile_callable><name>CaseTransitionValidator</name><sandbox_callable>false</sandbox_callable><script><![CDATA[var CaseTransitionValidator = Class.create();
CaseTransitionValidator.prototype = {
    /**
     * No-arg initializer. The class holds no per-instance state across
     * calls (each guard call from a flow/Business Rule/UI Action is
     * stateless), so initialize() is intentionally empty. Keeping the
     * empty initializer lets callers use the platform-canonical
     * `new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator()` instantiation pattern.
     */
    initialize: function() {
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Draft -> Open transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From  | To   | Required condition         | Failure handling          |
     *     | Draft | Open | assigned_group populated   | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * The caller (the validate_open_transition.xml subflow or a
     * before-update Business Rule) surfaces the returned {error} string
     * via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true) so the
     * blocking-error message appears on the form per AAP Section 0.7.1
     * ("Surface all blocking errors on the form").
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned
     *     (typically the platform-injected `current` GlideRecord in a
     *     before-update Business Rule, or the case record loaded by the
     *     Flow Designer subflow).
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when valid, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Required field assigned_group is empty.' }
     *     when assigned_group is null/empty/whitespace, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToOpen: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // GlideRecord.getValue() returns the column's string value or
        // null. Coerce to String defensively (some platform releases
        // return GlideElement objects instead of primitives) and trim
        // whitespace. An assigned_group that is a single space character
        // is functionally empty for the purposes of this guard.
        var assignedGroup = caseGr.getValue('assigned_group');
        if (!assignedGroup || String(assignedGroup).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Required field assigned_group is empty.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Open -> In Progress transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From | To          | Required condition                                      | Failure handling          |
     *     | Open | In Progress | assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group   | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * Both conditions are checked. If assigned_agent is unset, OR
     * assigned_group is unset, OR the assigned_agent is set but is not a
     * member of the assigned_group (verified by isAgentInGroup), the
     * transition is blocked. The single error message is intentionally
     * uniform across all three failure modes so a probing client cannot
     * distinguish which precondition failed (defense against
     * privilege-escalation reconnaissance).
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when valid, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' }
     *     when any precondition fails, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToInProgress: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // Same defensive String() coercion + trim() as canTransitionToOpen.
        var assignedAgent = caseGr.getValue('assigned_agent');
        var assignedGroup = caseGr.getValue('assigned_group');
        if (!assignedAgent || String(assignedAgent).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        if (!assignedGroup || String(assignedGroup).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        // Membership check delegated to isAgentInGroup. The sys_ids
        // passed in are RUNTIME values (read from the case record), NOT
        // hardcoded literals - this complies with AAP Section 0.7.2's
        // no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
        if (!this.isAgentInGroup(String(assignedAgent), String(assignedGroup))) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the In Progress -> Resolved transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From        | To       | Required condition                                  | Failure handling                                          |
     *     | In Progress | Resolved | All linked x_casemgmt_case_task have status=Closed | "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case."    |
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.7.4 (verbatim error message):
     *     "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case."
     *
     * The string above MUST appear character-for-character in the return
     * value when at least one child task has status != 'Closed'. The
     * caller (validate_resolved_transition.xml subflow or a future
     * before-update Business Rule) passes this message to
     * gs.addErrorMessage(), which surfaces it on the form.
     *
     * Implementation delegates to getOpenTaskCountForCase, which uses
     * GlideAggregate for an efficient COUNT(*) query rather than
     * fetching task rows. The boolean predicate (count > 0) is computed
     * here so the validator's API stays uniform.
     *
     * Semantic source-side reference: ArkCase
     * CaseFileTasksServiceImpl.java line 45-50
     * (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/
     *  java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/
     *  CaseFileTasksServiceImpl.java) delegated to a Solr
     * ChildDocumentsSearchService for a comparable count; the
     * ServiceNow target uses the platform-native GlideAggregate
     * because Solr is out of POC scope per AAP Section 0.3.2.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when zero open child tasks remain,
     *     or { ok: false, error: 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.' }
     *     when at least one child task has status != Closed, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToResolved: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // GlideRecord.getUniqueValue() returns the sys_id of the current
        // row. This sys_id is a RUNTIME value (computed by the platform
        // when the case row was inserted), NOT a hardcoded literal.
        var openCount = this.getOpenTaskCountForCase(String(caseGr.getUniqueValue()));
        if (openCount > 0) {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Resolved -> Closed transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From     | To     | Required condition                                          | Failure handling          |
     *     | Resolved | Closed | Caller has x_casemgmt_case_manager role; auto-set closed_date | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * The role check uses gs.getUser().hasRole(role_name) which accepts
     * the role's NAME ('x_casemgmt_case_manager') as a stable
     * human-readable key per AAP Section 0.7.2. This is the canonical
     * pattern for role checks in scoped applications - it does NOT
     * require a hardcoded role sys_id.
     *
     * The closed_date side-effect is NOT performed here. It is the
     * responsibility of two separate artifacts:
     *   - ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_closed_date.xml (catches
     *     direct DB updates: Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord
     *     scripts, bulk imports)
     *   - ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml (catches
     *     interactive transitions through the form/UI)
     * Defense in depth between these two writers is intentional;
     * see set_closed_date.xml's documentation for details.
     *
     * Dual-mode userId argument:
     *   - When userId is empty/null OR equals gs.getUserID() - use
     *     gs.getUser() (the current session user) - this is the
     *     standard interactive-form-update path.
     *   - When userId is non-empty AND differs from gs.getUserID() -
     *     look the user up by sys_id, then resolve the role grant with
     *     a GlideRecord query on sys_user_has_role
     *     (user=<that user> ^ role.name=x_casemgmt_case_manager).
     *     This supports scheduled flows or system-context calls that
     *     validate transitions on behalf of a specific user (e.g. "does
     *     [requested user] hold the case_manager role?").
     *     gs.getUser(user_name) is deliberately NOT used here: on this
     *     release it ignores its argument and returns the SESSION user,
     *     which silently answered with the caller's roles and let a
     *     non-manager pass this guard. See the WARNING in the method
     *     body and ../docs/PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md 9.6 E-GU.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @param {String} userId - sys_id of the user attempting the
     *     transition. Typically gs.getUserID() (the current session
     *     user); may be a different sys_id for system-context calls.
     *     If null/empty, defaults to the current session user.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when the user has the case_manager
     *     role, or { ok: false, error: 'Only case managers can close cases.' }
     *     when the role check fails, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToClosed: function(caseGr, userId) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // hasManagerRole resolves the case_manager role membership for
        // the user identified by userId. Three branches:
        //   (a) userId is provided and equals the current session user
        //       -> gs.getUser() is the most efficient path.
        //   (b) userId is provided and differs from the current user
        //       -> resolve THAT user's roles from sys_user_has_role
        //          directly. See the WARNING below: gs.getUser(userName)
        //          must NOT be used for this.
        //   (c) userId is null/empty -> default to current session user.
        //
        // WARNING - measured platform behaviour, do not "simplify" this.
        // gs.getUser(userName) IGNORES its argument on this release and
        // returns the SESSION user. Measured directly:
        //     gs.getUser('x_casemgmt_demo_agent') -> resolved_name=admin,
        //     IS_SESSION_USER=true, hasRole(case_manager)=true
        // An earlier revision of this branch called
        //     gs.getUser(userGr.getValue('user_name')).hasRole(...)
        // and therefore answered with the CALLER's roles rather than the
        // named user's, so a NON-MANAGER passed the Resolved -> Closed
        // guard and this method returned { ok: true }. That is a silent
        // bypass of the AAP Section 0.5.5 rule "Resolved -> Closed
        // requires the caller to hold x_casemgmt_case_manager", and it was
        // caught by assertion A9 of the transition-logic regression
        // harness on a clean install.
        // sys_user_has_role is the platform's own store of EFFECTIVE role
        // grants - it is maintained to include roles inherited through
        // groups and through role containment - so querying it answers
        // the question correctly for ANY user, not only the session user.
        var hasManagerRole;
        if (userId && String(userId).trim() !== '' && String(userId) === String(gs.getUserID())) {
            hasManagerRole = gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
        } else if (userId && String(userId).trim() !== '') {
            // Non-current-user context. The user is identified by the
            // RUNTIME sys_id passed in by the caller (NOT a hardcoded
            // literal), and the role is resolved by NAME, which satisfies
            // the AAP Section 0.7.2 stable-key constraint.
            var userGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
            if (userGr.get(String(userId))) {
                var grantGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role');
                grantGr.addQuery('user', userGr.getUniqueValue());
                grantGr.addQuery('role.name', 'x_casemgmt_case_manager');
                grantGr.setLimit(1);
                grantGr.query();
                hasManagerRole = grantGr.hasNext();
            } else {
                // Unknown user sys_id -> deny by default. Returning
                // false rather than throwing keeps the validator's
                // failure modes uniform (always {ok:false,error:string}).
                hasManagerRole = false;
            }
        } else {
            hasManagerRole = gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
        }
        if (!hasManagerRole) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Only case managers can close cases.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates that a status change does not violate the prohibited
     * transitions enumerated in AAP Section 0.5.5.
     *
     * Two prohibited patterns - both with VERBATIM error messages
     * per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *
     *   1. Closed -> anything (except staying Closed). Closed is the
     *      terminal state. The verbatim error message:
     *           "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified."
     *
     *   2. Any non-Draft state -> Draft. Backtransitioning to Draft is
     *      prohibited because Draft is reserved for new cases (the
     *      portal submission and dictionary default both produce Draft;
     *      no transition path returns to it). The verbatim error
     *      message:
     *           "Cases cannot be returned to Draft."
     *
     * The method is designed to be called from before-update Business
     * Rules where:
     *     previousStatus = String(previous.status)  // value BEFORE update
     *     newStatus      = String(current.status)   // proposed value
     * Flow Designer subflows can pass equivalent values via flow
     * variables.
     *
     * Edge cases handled gracefully:
     *   - Insert (previousStatus is null/empty): no transition to
     *     validate -> { ok: true }. This lets the same method be called
     *     from before-INSERT Business Rules (where previous is null)
     *     without producing false rejections.
     *   - newStatus is null/empty: no proposed value -> { ok: true }.
     *   - Closed -> Closed: not a real transition (no field change) ->
     *     { ok: true }.
     *   - Whitespace-only inputs: trimmed before comparison.
     *
     * @param {String} previousStatus - the previous status (e.g.,
     *     'Open', 'In Progress', 'Pending', 'Resolved', 'Closed', or
     *     '' on insert).
     * @param {String} newStatus - the new/proposed status. Must be one
     *     of the choice values in
     *     ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when the proposed transition is
     *     allowed, or { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' }
     *     when transitioning out of Closed, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' }
     *     when transitioning to Draft from any non-Draft state.
     */
    validateNoBacktransition: function(previousStatus, newStatus) {
        // Defensive coercion. The caller may pass GlideElement objects,
        // primitives, null, or undefined. String() of null/undefined
        // produces 'null' / 'undefined' which would otherwise compare
        // unexpectedly; the explicit ternary covers that case.
        var prev = previousStatus ? String(previousStatus).trim() : '';
        var next = newStatus ? String(newStatus).trim() : '';

        // Case 1: Closed is terminal - no transitions out.
        // The (next !== 'Closed' && next !== '') guard avoids false
        // rejections for:
        //   - Closed -> Closed (no field change; not a real transition)
        //   - Closed -> '' (proposed value is empty/cleared; not a
        //     real transition; the caller's other guards or dictionary
        //     mandatory flag will reject the empty value separately)
        if (prev === 'Closed' && next !== 'Closed' && next !== '') {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' };
        }

        // Case 2: Any non-Draft -> Draft is prohibited.
        // The (prev !== '' && prev !== 'Draft') guard avoids false
        // rejections for:
        //   - INSERT (prev is empty -> no transition to validate; the
        //     dictionary default value places new rows in Draft and
        //     this is the canonical entry point)
        //   - Draft -> Draft (no field change; harmless no-op)
        if (prev !== '' && prev !== 'Draft' && next === 'Draft') {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' };
        }

        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the transition EDGE itself: is `previousStatus ->
     * newStatus` one of the edges the state machine defines?
     *
     * WHY THIS EXISTS (the gap it closes). The canTransitionTo* methods
     * above each validate the PRECONDITION OF A TARGET STATUS - "does
     * this case satisfy what Open requires", "does it satisfy what
     * Resolved requires". None of them, and nothing else in the
     * application, checked WHERE the case was coming FROM. A single save
     * that moved a case straight from Draft to Closed therefore passed:
     * it never had to satisfy Open's assigned_group requirement, nor In
     * Progress's agent-membership requirement, nor Resolved's
     * task-closure gate, and it reached the terminal state with
     * closed_date empty (../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_closed_date.xml
     * keys on the Resolved -> Closed edge). All eight illegal
     * skip/backward edges behaved the same way.
     *
     * AAP Section 0.5.5 defines the legal edges, and AAP Section 0.7.3
     * Gate 2 requires "All state transitions enforced for both case
     * types". The adjacency list below is that matrix, read as the
     * complete set of legal edges:
     *
     *     Draft       -> Open
     *     Open        -> In Progress
     *     In Progress -> Pending      (and back)
     *     In Progress -> Resolved
     *     Pending     -> In Progress
     *     Resolved    -> Closed
     *     Closed      -> (nothing; terminal)
     *
     * This method is the SINGLE DEFINITION of that graph for the whole
     * application, so the before-update Business Rule
     * ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions.xml
     * (order 250), the Flow Designer subflows in ../flows/sub_flows/ and
     * the Custom Action ../flows/custom_actions/x_casemgmt_transition_guard_action.xml
     * all answer the question the same way.
     *
     * MESSAGE OWNERSHIP. The two PROHIBITED rows of the matrix keep
     * their verbatim AAP Section 0.7.4 wording, returned from here as
     * well as from validateNoBacktransition() above, so a caller that
     * consults only this method still surfaces the contractual text:
     *   - source Closed -> 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.'
     *   - target Draft  -> 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.'
     * Every other rejection is a skip edge, for which AAP Section 0.5.5
     * prescribes no wording (it has no row for those edges, only the
     * general Section 0.7.1 requirement that the error be surfaced on
     * the form). Those get a specific, actionable sentence that names
     * both the attempted edge and the legal next status, in the same
     * voice as the existing invalid-status message in the order-250
     * Business Rule.
     *
     * Edge cases, all resolved as { ok: true } because none is a
     * transition:
     *   - INSERT: previousStatus is null/empty. Seed data and the portal
     *     legitimately insert rows directly at Draft, and the demo data
     *     inserts rows at every status, so an insert must never be
     *     judged against the graph.
     *   - newStatus null/empty: no proposed value.
     *   - previousStatus === newStatus: a field-only save, not a
     *     transition.
     *
     * FAIL CLOSED on an unrecognised SOURCE status. If a row somehow
     * holds a status outside the six choice values, its legal successors
     * are unknown, so the move is refused rather than guessed. (An
     * unrecognised TARGET status is refused earlier, by the order-250
     * rule's own allowlist, with its own message.)
     *
     * @param {String} previousStatus - the committed status, i.e.
     *     String(previous.status) in a before-update Business Rule, or
     *     the status read from the database by a subflow.
     * @param {String} newStatus - the proposed status, i.e.
     *     String(current.status).
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when the edge is legal, otherwise
     *     { ok: false, error: <message to surface on the form> }.
     */
    validateTransitionEdge: function(previousStatus, newStatus) {
        // Defensive coercion, identical in style to
        // validateNoBacktransition above: callers may hand over
        // GlideElement objects, primitives, null or undefined.
        var prev = previousStatus ? String(previousStatus).trim() : '';
        var next = newStatus ? String(newStatus).trim() : '';

        // Not a transition - nothing to validate. See the edge-case list
        // in the doc comment for why each of these three is allowed.
        if (prev === '' || next === '' || prev === next) {
            return { ok: true };
        }

        // The two PROHIBITED rows of AAP Section 0.5.5, with their
        // VERBATIM Section 0.7.4 messages - DO NOT paraphrase. These are
        // also enforced (and normally reached first) by the order-100 and
        // order-200 Business Rules; repeating them here means this method
        // alone is a complete answer for any caller.
        if (prev === 'Closed') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' };
        }
        if (next === 'Draft') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' };
        }

        // The adjacency list is declared inside the method deliberately:
        // a function-local object cannot be mutated by a caller holding a
        // reference to this Script Include, so the graph cannot drift at
        // runtime. The keys and values are the Title Case choice values
        // from ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml, verbatim.
        var ALLOWED_NEXT = {
            'Draft': ['Open'],
            'Open': ['In Progress'],
            'In Progress': ['Pending', 'Resolved'],
            'Pending': ['In Progress'],
            'Resolved': ['Closed'],
            'Closed': []
        };

        // hasOwnProperty rather than a truthiness test: an empty array is
        // falsy-adjacent in some engines' idioms and 'Closed' maps to one
        // legitimately (though the prev === 'Closed' branch above already
        // returned). This distinguishes "known status with no successors"
        // from "status this application does not recognise".
        if (!ALLOWED_NEXT.hasOwnProperty(prev)) {
            return {
                ok: false,
                error: 'This case is in a status this application does not recognise, so its status ' +
                       'cannot be changed. Please tell your administrator.'
            };
        }

        var allowed = ALLOWED_NEXT[prev];
        if (allowed.indexOf(next) >= 0) {
            return { ok: true };
        }

        // Build the guidance half of the message from the same adjacency
        // list, so the sentence can never contradict the graph it is
        // describing. Only 'In Progress' has two successors today; the
        // join is written generically so adding a choice value to the
        // graph needs no change here.
        var guidance;
        if (allowed.length === 0) {
            guidance = prev + ' is a terminal status, so no further status change is possible.';
        } else if (allowed.length === 1) {
            guidance = 'From ' + prev + ' the only valid next status is ' + allowed[0] + '.';
        } else {
            guidance = 'From ' + prev + ' the valid next statuses are ' +
                       allowed.slice(0, allowed.length - 1).join(', ') + ' or ' +
                       allowed[allowed.length - 1] + '.';
        }

        return { ok: false, error: 'A case cannot go from ' + prev + ' to ' + next + '. ' + guidance };
    },

    /**
     * Verifies that a case already in the terminal Closed status is
     * being saved WITHOUT any change to its own columns.
     *
     * WHY THIS EXISTS. AAP Section 0.5.5 row 8 pairs the prohibition
     * "Closed -> *" with the message "Closed cases are terminal and
     * cannot be modified." - and the application honoured only the first
     * half. A status change out of Closed was refused, but a save that
     * left status alone and rewrote priority, subject, or cleared
     * assigned_agent committed silently, so the record the message calls
     * unmodifiable was in fact freely editable. This method closes that
     * gap and makes the contractual sentence, and the four in-scope
     * documents that quote it, literally true.
     *
     * WHAT IS COMPARED, AND WHY ONLY THIS. The list is exactly the
     * application's own columns: the twelve fields of AAP Section 0.5.7
     * plus pending_reason. It deliberately excludes:
     *   - every sys_* column, because sys_mod_count and sys_updated_on
     *     change on any save and comparing them would turn a genuine
     *     no-op into a rejection;
     *   - duration_to_close, which is a virtual function field computed
     *     at query time and cannot be written at all.
     *
     * THE NO-OP SAVE STAYS ALLOWED. Opening a Closed case and pressing
     * Update without editing anything changes no compared field, so this
     * method returns { ok: true } and the save proceeds as the harmless
     * no-op it is. That behaviour is asserted by the QA suite and is
     * preserved on purpose.
     *
     * IMMUTABILITY IS NOT AUTHORIZATION. This is a data-integrity guard
     * on the terminal state, not an access-control check; who may write
     * the row at all is decided by the scoped ACLs in ../acl/.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the in-flight record, i.e. the
     *     platform-injected `current` in a before-update Business Rule.
     * @param {GlideRecord} previousGr - the committed record, i.e.
     *     `previous`. REQUIRED: callers must guard for the insert case
     *     (where `previous` is null) before calling, exactly as
     *     ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed.xml does.
     *     Without a prior snapshot nothing can be verified, so a missing
     *     record is refused rather than waved through.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when no compared column changed, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' }
     *     when one did, or { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' }
     *     when either GlideRecord is absent.
     */
    validateClosedRecordUnchanged: function(caseGr, previousGr) {
        if (!caseGr || !previousGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }

        // The application's own columns, in the order AAP Section 0.5.7
        // lists them, with number first and pending_reason last.
        var GUARDED_FIELDS = [
            'number',
            'type',
            'status',
            'priority',
            'subject',
            'description',
            'opened_date',
            'closed_date',
            'assigned_group',
            'assigned_agent',
            'requester_name',
            'requester_email',
            'pending_reason'
        ];

        for (var i = 0; i < GUARDED_FIELDS.length; i++) {
            var field = GUARDED_FIELDS[i];
            // getValue() returns the raw column value as a string, or
            // null when the column is empty. Normalizing null/undefined
            // to '' is what makes "empty before, empty after" compare
            // equal instead of null !== '' rejecting a no-op save, and
            // what makes "populated -> cleared" (e.g. clearing
            // assigned_agent) compare as the change it is.
            var after = caseGr.getValue(field);
            var before = previousGr.getValue(field);
            after = (after === null || after === undefined) ? '' : String(after);
            before = (before === null || before === undefined) ? '' : String(before);
            if (after !== before) {
                // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
                return { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' };
            }
        }

        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Decides whether a state-transition UI Action button should be
     * VISIBLE on the case form to the user making the request.
     *
     * WHY THIS EXISTS (the platform limit it works around). A
     * sys_ui_action.condition is a `condition_string` column with
     * max_length 254 - a hard platform limit. Four of the six transition
     * buttons carried a condition of 264-271 characters, so the platform
     * silently truncated each one MID-EXPRESSION on import (the Resolve
     * condition ended `...isMemberOf(current.assigned_grou`). A truncated
     * condition cannot evaluate, and the platform's failure mode is to
     * FAIL OPEN with no server-log entry: Start Progress, Set Pending,
     * Resume and Resolve therefore rendered on every status for every
     * identity, including the read-only x_casemgmt_case_viewer, whose
     * form has no Update button at all. The two short conditions
     * (x_casemgmt_case_open at 76 characters and x_casemgmt_case_close at
     * 79) were unaffected by the truncation and were left inline at that
     * point. They no longer are: both now call canShowManagerAction()
     * below, because the inline form carried the post-abort defect
     * described there - it reads the status the user attempted rather
     * than the status the row holds. All six conditions are therefore
     * method calls, and none of them is close to the character limit.
     *
     * There is a second reason the condition must carry the whole guard
     * on this release: sys_ui_action has NO `roles` column here - UI
     * Action role restrictions live in the m2m table
     * sys_ui_action_role - so the <roles> element in a serialized
     * sys_ui_action payload is inert and grants no gating whatsoever.
     * The condition is the only guard the platform will honour, which is
     * exactly why it must be short enough to survive import.
     *
     * Moving the expression into this method makes each condition a
     * ~77-character call, comfortably inside the limit and immune to a
     * future edit pushing it back over.
     *
     * THE RULE, unchanged from the four original inline expressions
     * (AAP Section 0.4.1 "only those needed for state transitions
     * visible to the appropriate roles", plus the Section 0.5.6
     * "Assigned only" definition):
     *
     *     the case is in `requiredStatus`
     *     AND (
     *         the user holds x_casemgmt_case_manager
     *         OR (
     *             the user holds x_casemgmt_case_agent
     *             AND ( assigned_agent is the user
     *                   OR the user is a member of assigned_group )
     *         )
     *     )
     *
     * VISIBILITY IS NOT AUTHORIZATION. This governs only whether the
     * affordance is drawn. Every one of the six UI Actions re-checks role
     * and status server-side in its own script, the order-100/200/250
     * Business Rules re-check the transition on the write itself, and the
     * scoped ACLs decide who may write the row at all. Hiding a button
     * the user cannot use removes a misleading affordance; it is not the
     * security boundary and is not relied on as one.
     *
     * Group membership is resolved through this.isAgentInGroup(), which
     * queries sys_user_grmember, rather than through
     * gs.getUser().isMemberOf(). The two are equivalent for this purpose
     * and reusing the helper keeps one membership implementation in the
     * application. gs.getUser().hasRole() answers true for a user holding
     * `admin`, which is why an administrator continues to see each button
     * on its correct status.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record the form is showing,
     *     i.e. the platform-injected `current` in a UI Action condition.
     * @param {String} requiredStatus - the source status the button
     *     belongs to: 'Open' for Start Progress, 'In Progress' for Set
     *     Pending and Resolve, 'Pending' for Resume.
     * @return {Boolean} true when the button should render, false
     *     otherwise. Never throws: a missing record or a missing status
     *     argument returns false, so the affordance fails CLOSED - the
     *     opposite of the truncation behaviour this method replaces.
     */
    canShowAction: function(caseGr, requiredStatus) {
        if (!caseGr || !requiredStatus) {
            return false;
        }

        // EVALUATE AGAINST THE STORED ROW, NOT THE IN-MEMORY ONE.
        //
        // When a Business Rule calls setAbortAction(true), the platform
        // answers the POST with a redirect back to the same form and
        // re-renders it from the SUBMITTED values, so `current` carries the
        // status the user attempted rather than the status the row still
        // holds. UI Action conditions are evaluated during that re-render.
        // Measured on the rendered form: saving CASE9000003 (In Progress,
        // one Open child task) with status Resolved was correctly refused
        // with "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.", and
        // the returned form then dropped "Set Pending" and "Resolve" and
        // drew "Close" - the transition belonging to Resolved - on a record
        // whose stored status was still In Progress. A clean reload showed
        // In Progress and the correct two buttons, so the affordance
        // disagreed with the database for exactly as long as the refusal
        // was on screen, which is the window in which the user is deciding
        // what to do next.
        //
        // Re-reading the row makes the button set describe what is stored.
        // On an ordinary form load the two are the same record and the read
        // changes nothing; on a new record there is nothing to read and the
        // in-memory values are the only ones there are. Assignment is read
        // from the same stored row for the same reason: an uncommitted edit
        // to assigned_agent or assigned_group must not widen "Assigned
        // only" while the write that would have made it true is refused.
        var stored = this._storedRecord(caseGr);

        var wanted = String(requiredStatus).trim();
        var actual = stored.getValue('status');
        actual = (actual === null || actual === undefined) ? '' : String(actual).trim();
        if (actual === '' || actual !== wanted) {
            return false;
        }

        var user = gs.getUser();

        // Managers act on any case in the right status. hasRole() is true
        // for an admin as well, by platform design.
        if (user.hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager')) {
            return true;
        }

        // Anyone who is neither a manager nor an agent - the read-only
        // x_casemgmt_case_viewer, or a user with no application role at
        // all - gets no transition buttons.
        if (!user.hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_agent')) {
            return false;
        }

        // "Assigned only", per AAP Section 0.5.6: the agent named on the
        // case, or any member of the group the case is assigned to.
        var me = String(gs.getUserID());
        var agent = stored.getValue('assigned_agent');
        agent = (agent === null || agent === undefined) ? '' : String(agent);
        if (agent !== '' && agent === me) {
            return true;
        }

        var group = stored.getValue('assigned_group');
        group = (group === null || group === undefined) ? '' : String(group);
        if (group === '') {
            return false;
        }
        return this.isAgentInGroup(me, group);
    },

    /**
     * The manager-only variant of canShowAction().
     *
     * Two of the six transitions are reserved to x_casemgmt_case_manager
     * by AAP Section 0.5.5: Draft -> Open and Resolved -> Closed. Their
     * conditions were short enough to survive the sys_ui_action.condition
     * 254-character limit inline, so they were left as
     * `current.status == '<status>' && gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager')`
     * while the four broader ones moved into canShowAction().
     *
     * That inline form has the defect canShowAction() was changed to fix,
     * and it was still visible after that change: `current` on a
     * post-abort redisplay carries the status the user ATTEMPTED.
     * Measured on the rendered form - saving CASE9000003 (In Progress)
     * with status Resolved was refused with "All tasks must be closed
     * before resolving this case.", and the returned form drew the red
     * "Close" button, because Close's inline condition read the
     * uncommitted "Resolved". So the bar offered the Resolved -> Closed
     * transition on a record the database still had at In Progress, one
     * banner below the sentence explaining that it had not moved.
     *
     * This method is deliberately NOT canShowAction(): that one also
     * grants an assigned x_casemgmt_case_agent, which for these two
     * transitions would widen the affordance past what Section 0.5.5
     * allows. The role test here is exactly the one the inline
     * expressions carried - hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager'), true for
     * an administrator by platform design - and nothing else changes.
     *
     * VISIBILITY IS NOT AUTHORIZATION, as for canShowAction(): each UI
     * Action re-checks role and status in its own script, the Business
     * Rules re-check the transition on the write, and the scoped ACLs
     * decide who may write the row at all.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record the form is showing,
     *     i.e. the platform-injected `current`.
     * @param {String} requiredStatus - the source status the button
     *     belongs to: 'Draft' for Open, 'Resolved' for Close.
     * @return {Boolean} true when the button should render. Fails CLOSED
     *     on a missing record or status, and never throws.
     */
    canShowManagerAction: function(caseGr, requiredStatus) {
        if (!caseGr || !requiredStatus) {
            return false;
        }

        var stored = this._storedRecord(caseGr);
        var wanted = String(requiredStatus).trim();
        var actual = stored.getValue('status');
        actual = (actual === null || actual === undefined) ? '' : String(actual).trim();
        if (actual === '' || actual !== wanted) {
            return false;
        }

        return gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
    },

    /**
     * Resolve the STORED row behind an in-memory case record.
     *
     * Returns a freshly-read GlideRecord for caseGr's sys_id when one can
     * be read, and caseGr itself otherwise. Used by canShowAction() so
     * that transition affordances describe the database rather than an
     * uncommitted form; see the comment there for the measured behaviour
     * that made it necessary.
     *
     * Both fallbacks are deliberate and both fail CLOSED:
     *
     *   - A record with no sys_id is a new record that has never been
     *     written. There is nothing to re-read, and its in-memory values
     *     are the only description of it that exists.
     *
     *   - A read that returns nothing means the row is gone or the caller
     *     may not read it. Scoped GlideRecord applies the read ACLs of the
     *     running user, so for an x_casemgmt_case_agent this is precisely
     *     the unassigned case they are refused everywhere else: falling
     *     back to caseGr hands canShowAction the same values it would have
     *     used before, and its "Assigned only" test then refuses the
     *     button anyway.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_id: the identifier is read off the record passed
     * in, per AAP Section 0.7.2.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - an x_casemgmt_case record, typically
     *     the platform-injected `current`.
     * @return {GlideRecord} the stored row when readable, else caseGr.
     *     Never null, and never throws.
     */
    _storedRecord: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return caseGr;
        }

        var sysId = '';
        try {
            sysId = caseGr.getUniqueValue();
            sysId = (sysId === null || sysId === undefined) ? '' : String(sysId).trim();
        } catch (e) {
            // getUniqueValue() is defined on every GlideRecord, but this
            // method must never be the reason a form fails to render.
            gs.debug('x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator._storedRecord: could not read sys_id: ' + e);
            return caseGr;
        }

        if (sysId === '') {
            return caseGr;
        }

        var stored = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        if (stored.get(sysId)) {
            return stored;
        }
        return caseGr;
    },

    /**
     * Helper: returns true when the user is a member of the group.
     *
     * Implementation queries the OOB sys_user_grmember table, the
     * canonical group-membership join table in ServiceNow. Each
     * sys_user_grmember row links a `user` field (reference ->
     * sys_user) to a `group` field (reference -> sys_user_group); a
     * single matching row is sufficient evidence of membership.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_ids: the userSysId and groupSysId arguments are
     * RUNTIME values supplied by the caller (typically read from the
     * case record's assigned_agent / assigned_group fields). This
     * helper never embeds a literal sys_id.
     *
     * setLimit(1) is a defensive optimization. At most one membership
     * row exists per (user, group) pair, but setting an explicit limit
     * tells the database engine to short-circuit at the first hit and
     * eliminates any potential for a misconfiguration to fetch all
     * membership rows of a populous group.
     *
     * Used by:
     *   - this.canTransitionToInProgress (Open -> In Progress validation)
     *   - ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership.xml
     *     (before-update guard on the case row that re-validates
     *     membership any time assigned_agent changes)
     *
     * @param {String} userSysId - sys_id of a sys_user record. May be
     *     null, undefined, empty, or whitespace-only - all of which
     *     are treated as "not a member" without throwing.
     * @param {String} groupSysId - sys_id of a sys_user_group record.
     *     Same null/empty handling as userSysId.
     * @return {Boolean} true if at least one sys_user_grmember row
     *     links the given user to the given group; false otherwise
     *     (including when either argument is null/empty).
     */
    isAgentInGroup: function(userSysId, groupSysId) {
        if (!userSysId || !groupSysId) {
            return false;
        }
        // Normalize whitespace-only strings to empty so the GlideRecord
        // query never receives a meaningless filter value.
        var userVal = String(userSysId).trim();
        var groupVal = String(groupSysId).trim();
        if (userVal === '' || groupVal === '') {
            return false;
        }
        var memberGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember');
        memberGr.addQuery('user', userVal);
        memberGr.addQuery('group', groupVal);
        memberGr.setLimit(1);
        memberGr.query();
        return memberGr.next() ? true : false;
    },

    /**
     * Helper: returns the count of OPEN child tasks for the given
     * case (i.e., child case_task rows where status != 'Closed').
     *
     * Implementation uses GlideAggregate, which executes a SQL
     * COUNT(*) directly in the database rather than fetching task
     * rows into the application layer. This is meaningfully more
     * efficient than GlideRecord.getRowCount() for cases with many
     * tasks, and is the correct pattern for count-only checks.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_ids: the caseSysId argument is a RUNTIME value
     * supplied by the caller (typically caseGr.getUniqueValue()). This
     * helper never embeds a literal sys_id.
     *
     * The status filter uses the literal Title Case value 'Closed' -
     * this matches the choice list defined in
     * ../choices/sys_choice_case_task_status.xml (Open, In Progress,
     * Closed). ServiceNow Choice fields persist the LABEL string by
     * default, not an integer ID, so the != filter compares the
     * stored string value directly.
     *
     * Used by:
     *   - this.canTransitionToResolved (the In Progress -> Resolved
     *     gate; per AAP Section 0.5.5, the transition is allowed only
     *     when this method returns 0).
     *   - Diagnostic logging in calling flows (e.g., the
     *     validate_resolved_transition subflow may log the count
     *     when blocking the transition, although the user-facing
     *     error message is fixed verbatim per AAP Section 0.7.4).
     *
     * @param {String} caseSysId - sys_id of the parent
     *     x_casemgmt_case row. May be null, undefined, empty, or
     *     whitespace-only - all of which return 0 without throwing.
     * @return {Number} count of x_casemgmt_case_task rows where
     *     case = caseSysId AND status != 'Closed'. Returns 0 when
     *     caseSysId is invalid or no rows match.
     */
    getOpenTaskCountForCase: function(caseSysId) {
        if (!caseSysId || String(caseSysId).trim() === '') {
            return 0;
        }
        var caseVal = String(caseSysId).trim();
        // GlideAggregate constructor takes the table name. The scoped
        // table x_casemgmt_case_task is defined in
        // ../tables/x_casemgmt_case_task.xml and its `case` field is
        // the parent reference (defined in
        // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_task_case.xml).
        var agg = new GlideAggregate('x_casemgmt_case_task');
        agg.addQuery('case', caseVal);
        // 'Closed' is the literal Title Case choice value from
        // ../choices/sys_choice_case_task_status.xml. The != operator
        // selects all OPEN tasks (Open, In Progress, and any future
        // non-Closed choice values added without breaking this guard).
        agg.addQuery('status', '!=', 'Closed');
        agg.addAggregate('COUNT');
        agg.query();
        if (agg.next()) {
            // getAggregate returns a string; parseInt with radix 10 is
            // the canonical numeric coercion. The defensive isNaN check
            // covers the unlikely case where the platform returns a
            // non-numeric string for an empty result set.
            var n = parseInt(agg.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10);
            return isNaN(n) ? 0 : n;
        }
        return 0;
    },

    /**
     * Class-name marker. ServiceNow's Class.create() pattern conventionally
     * exposes a `type` property whose value matches the class name
     * (without the scope prefix). This is used by the platform's
     * introspection tooling and by some debug logging. It MUST be
     * 'CaseTransitionValidator' (NOT 'x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator')
     * - the scope prefix lives only in the <api_name> element above,
     * not in the class name itself.
     */
    type: 'CaseTransitionValidator'
};
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>1151d194bc97cb3757738dc61623599d</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>CaseTransitionValidator</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_include_1151d194bc97cb3757738dc61623599d</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 05:45:34</sys_updated_on></sys_script_include></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_728df51c3ca5e26a06896345fa3c4dd3
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Allows users with the x_casemgmt_case_agent role to write/update case_task records ONLY where the parent case has assigned_agent=current user OR assigned_group contains current user.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case_task</name><operation display_value="write">write</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var caseElement = current.getElement('case');
    if (!caseElement || caseElement.nil()) { return false; }
    var parentCase = caseElement.getRefRecord();
    if (!parentCase || !parentCase.isValidRecord()) { return false; }
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();
    if (parentCase.assigned_agent == currentUserId) { return true; }
    var groupId = parentCase.assigned_group.toString();
    if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) { return true; }
    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>728df51c3ca5e26a06896345fa3c4dd3</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case_task</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_task_write_agent_assigned</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

x_casemgmt_case_closetruefalseUI Action that transitions a Resolved case to Closed status. Visible only to x_casemgmt_case_manager users on cases with status=Resolved (per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 6 verbatim: "Resolved -> Closed: Caller has x_casemgmt_case_manager role; auto-set closed_date - Surface form-level error"). Delegates the role check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToClosed() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml). Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the existing Resolved status. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role and status. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if any guard fails (verbatim message "Only case managers can close cases." returned by the Script Include). The closed_date field is auto-populated by the cooperating ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_closed_date.xml before-update Business Rule (order=500) on the same current.update() transaction triggered by this UI Action - this UI Action sets only current.status='Closed', the BR sets current.closed_date=gs.nowDateTime(). After the transition completes, the ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed.xml before-update Business Rule (order=100) prevents any subsequent modifications to the case (per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 8 terminal-state rule). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII.new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().canShowManagerAction(current, 'Resolved')truetruefalsefalsefalsefalsedestructivefalseClose this case (case_manager role required; case must be in Resolved status). closed_date will be auto-populated. This action is TERMINAL - the case cannot be modified after closure.truefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalseClose600falsefalsefalsetruesys_ui_actionsystem2025-01-01 00:00:00global/c2988c82e1da1b3e1029196a6e0d0f9f1Close82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_ui_action_c2988c82e1da1b3e1029196a6e0d0f9fadmin2026-09-10 05:45:34x_casemgmt_case
