sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_4004168331b9b9ca07f4cbfd349e25d8
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>true</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case_party</collection><condition/><description>Before-insert and before-update on x_casemgmt_case_party: refuses any write that would store an empty mandatory case/party_type/role_label, a `case` reference that does not resolve to a live x_casemgmt_case row, an unrecognised party_type, or a person/organization pair that violates the exactly-one-of invariant AAP Section 0.5.7 states through its two Conditional rows. Closes QA finding F15 for the party table, which carried NO business rule at all - the whole polymorphic contract lived in the UI Policy, which runs in the form engine only. Measured before this rule: party_type=Person with no person returned 201; BOTH person and organization returned 201 (a row that is simultaneously a Person party and an Organization party, breaking the invariant the single-table collapse of ArkCase acm_person_assoc + acm_person_org_assoc rests on per Section 0.1.1); neither set and no party_type returned 201. The discriminator-to-column mapping is declared once as data in PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS, so all four downstream decisions derive from it. One case NORMALISES rather than refuses: when this write itself CHANGED party_type and the newly applicable reference is populated, the now-inapplicable one is cleared and logged via gs.info, because the UI Policy hides that field without clearing it and the classic form POSTs the hidden, non-disabled input verbatim - measured on the wire - so refusing would make a legitimate Organization-to-Person conversion impossible through the only internal UI AAP Section 0.4.4 provides, and the caller could not comply because the field is off their screen. An INSERT carrying both references, and an UPDATE that sets the wrong reference without touching party_type, are both still refused, so the stored row satisfies the exactly-one-of invariant on every path. The parent is resolved with plain GlideRecord, not GlideRecordSecure, so the rule tests EXISTENCE only and leaves authorization to the scoped ACLs of Section 0.5.6. Order=100; returns early on current.isActionAborted(); reproduces none of the four verbatim messages Section 0.7.4 fixes. Does not fire on delete, so the cascade rule on the case reference and the manager Delete grant are both untouched. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity</name><order>100</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Server-side backstop for AAP Section 0.5.7's MANDATORY, REFERENTIAL
    // and CONDITIONAL contracts on x_casemgmt_case_party.
    //
    // The two Conditional rows ("person required if party_type = Person",
    // "organization required if party_type = Organization") together state
    // an EXACTLY-ONE-OF invariant. Per AAP Section 0.1.1 this table is the
    // collapse of ArkCase's acm_person_assoc and acm_person_org_assoc into
    // one polymorphic table whose party_type Choice replaces JPA
    // single-table inheritance's cm_class_name discriminator - so a row that
    // is both a Person party and an Organization party has no counterpart in
    // the source model and no meaning in the target one.
    //
    // Before this rule the table carried NO business rule at all and the
    // whole contract lived in
    // ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml, a UI Policy
    // that runs in the FORM engine only. Measured as admin:
    //     POST party_type=Person, no person                -> HTTP 201
    //     POST with BOTH person and organization           -> HTTP 201
    //     POST with neither and no party_type              -> HTTP 201

    // Stop if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    // setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, not the remaining before
    // rules; the platform keeps running them and reports the pending abort
    // through current.isActionAborted().
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1 + 2. THE MANDATORY PARENT REFERENCE.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // getValue() returns the underlying sys_id String, or null when the
    // reference was never set. It is used in preference to property access
    // because it has one documented return contract across releases, and
    // because `case` is a reserved word in JavaScript so this form avoids
    // relying on the ES5 allowance for reserved words as property names.
    var parentId = current.getValue('case');
    if (parentId === null || parentId === undefined || String(parentId).trim() === '') {
        gs.addErrorMessage('Case is mandatory: a party must reference the case it belongs to.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // EXISTENCE, NOT ACCESS - plain GlideRecord, deliberately not
    // GlideRecordSecure. Access control on this table belongs to the scoped
    // ACLs of AAP Section 0.5.6 under ../acl/, which is what AAP Section
    // 0.7.3 Gate 3 measures. A read-ACL-aware lookup here would tell an
    // x_casemgmt_case_agent creating a party against a case outside their
    // "Assigned only" read scope that the CASE DOES NOT EXIST, masking the
    // ACL that actually governs the operation.
    var parentGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    if (!parentGr.get(parentId)) {
        // Worded differently from the anonymous portal lookup's verbatim
        // "No case found with that number." (owned by
        // x_casemgmt.CasePortalService, fixed by AAP Section 0.7.4): that
        // message answers an external requester searching by case NUMBER,
        // this one answers an internal caller who supplied an unresolvable
        // sys_id. Reusing it would put a portal-facing string on an
        // internal write path and duplicate another artifact's message.
        gs.addErrorMessage('The case this party references does not exist.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. role_label - the one plain MANDATORY string column on this table.
    //
    // Whitespace counts as empty: role_label IS the party table's display
    // field (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_role_label.xml carries
    // display=true), so a space-only value renders every reference to the
    // row as a blank label on the case form's Parties related list.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var roleLabel = current.getValue('role_label');
    if (roleLabel === null || roleLabel === undefined || String(roleLabel).trim() === '') {
        gs.addErrorMessage('Role Label is mandatory and cannot be empty.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4 + 5 + 6 + 7. THE POLYMORPHIC DISCRIMINATOR AND ITS EXACTLY-ONE-OF
    // INVARIANT.
    //
    // PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS is the ONE declaration of the mapping. Every
    // downstream decision derives from it: which party_type values are
    // recognised (its keys), which reference each requires (`element`),
    // which reference each forbids (the other entries' `element`), and how
    // each is named in the message (`label`, the dictionary column_label).
    // Adding a third party_type is a three-artifact change with no logic to
    // rewrite: a ../choices/ row, a ../dictionary/ reference column, one
    // entry here, plus the matching ../ui_policy/ branch.
    //
    // The two literals are the model itself: AAP Section 0.5.7 enumerates
    // exactly Person and Organization for party_type and, unlike
    // case.type ("General Inquiry, Complaint - extensible"), marks the list
    // closed. The map is not derived from sys_choice at run time because a
    // choice row declares which VALUES are selectable but says nothing
    // about which reference column each governs - the mapping would still
    // have to be declared here - and because an unrecognised discriminator
    // must be refused even where a choice row exists without its column,
    // which a sys_choice-derived allowlist would silently admit.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // `table` is the reference target each branch points at, taken from the
    // dictionary (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_person.xml ->
    // sys_user, ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_organization.xml ->
    // core_company). It is carried here so the branch that is REQUIRED for
    // the chosen party_type can have its reference resolved, not merely
    // counted as present - see the resolvability check below.
    var PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS = {
        'Person': { element: 'person', label: 'Person', table: 'sys_user' },
        'Organization': { element: 'organization', label: 'Organization', table: 'core_company' }
    };

    var partyType = current.getValue('party_type');
    if (partyType === null || partyType === undefined || String(partyType).trim() === '') {
        gs.addErrorMessage('Party Type is mandatory: choose Person or Organization.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }
    partyType = String(partyType).trim();

    // ALLOWLIST, NOT A LOOKUP MISS. Reaching this branch means the stored
    // discriminator is not one this application knows how to interpret, so
    // there is no column it can require and no column it can forbid - the
    // row's polymorphic identity is undefined and it must not be written.
    //
    // Defence in depth rather than the only defence: `party_type` carries
    // choice = 3, so the Table API silently DROPS a value outside the
    // declared list before any rule evaluates (the write answers HTTP 200
    // with the previous value retained). This branch therefore fires for a
    // value the platform did admit - a choice row added without its
    // reference column, or a value written by a path that bypasses choice
    // filtering - which is the case that matters.
    if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS, partyType)) {
        gs.addErrorMessage('Party Type must be Person or Organization.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ---- The Conditional row for this discriminator: "required if
    // party_type = <partyType>". Checked before exclusivity, so a caller who
    // supplied neither the right reference nor a coherent pair is told which
    // field to SUPPLY rather than which to remove.
    //
    // The person/organization columns are tested for PRESENCE only, never
    // read through to sys_user or core_company: the platform's own reference
    // integrity already guarantees that a non-empty reference names a live
    // row on the referenced table, and reading a global table from a scoped
    // rule would add a cross-scope dependency this contract does not need.
    var required = PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS[partyType];
    var requiredValue = current.getValue(required.element);
    if (requiredValue === null || requiredValue === undefined || String(requiredValue).trim() === '') {
        gs.addErrorMessage(required.label + ' is required when Party Type is ' + partyType + '.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 5b. THE REQUIRED BRANCH REFERENCE MUST RESOLVE.
    //
    // The check above proves the branch field is non-empty; it does not
    // prove it points at a row that exists. Measured before this block:
    //     POST {"case":"<valid>","party_type":"Person","role_label":"x",
    //           "person":"deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef"}        -> 201
    //     POST {... "party_type":"Organization",
    //           "organization":"deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef"}  -> 201
    // plus the same two as PATCH updates -> 200. Each stored an
    // unresolvable reference, producing a party that satisfies AAP Section
    // 0.5.7's exactly-one-of contract on paper while naming nobody: the
    // Person/Organization cell renders blank on the form, in the case
    // form's Parties related list and in every export, and the row cannot
    // be re-saved from its own form because a conditionally-mandatory
    // reference cannot be re-filled from a value that displays as blank.
    //
    // This closes the "referential" clause of AAP Section 0.5.7 for this
    // table, alongside the parent `case` reference already checked above.
    //
    // Only the REQUIRED branch is resolved. The other branch must be empty
    // (enforced below), and an empty value has no target to resolve.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!_referenceResolves(required.table, requiredValue)) {
        gs.addErrorMessage(required.label + ' must reference a ' +
            (partyType === 'Person' ? 'user' : 'company') + ' that exists.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ---- Did THIS write change the discriminator?
    //
    // The insert path must never be treated as a conversion, and testing
    // `previous` for null is NOT a sufficient way to establish that.
    // MEASURED on this instance: in a before-INSERT rule the platform still
    // passes a `previous` OBJECT - an initialized GlideRecord whose columns
    // are all empty - rather than null. A `!previous` guard therefore
    // evaluates false on insert, previous.getValue('party_type') returns
    // empty, empty !== the supplied party_type, and an insert carrying both
    // references would be mistaken for a conversion and silently normalised.
    // That is exactly what happened on the first revision of this rule:
    // finding F15's reproduction 4 (a both-set INSERT) came back HTTP 201
    // instead of being refused, and the regression was caught by re-running
    // all six reproductions rather than only the new conversion case.
    //
    // current.operation() is the authoritative discriminator between the two
    // paths and returns 'insert' / 'update' / 'delete'. It is probed with a
    // typeof check first so the rule degrades to the strict, refusing
    // behaviour rather than the permissive one if the method is ever
    // unavailable - a guard that fails closed.
    //
    // previousType is additionally required to be NON-EMPTY: a row whose
    // stored party_type was blank is not converting FROM anything, so there
    // is no prior statement of identity to supersede and the refusal is the
    // correct answer there too.
    //
    // This flag is what separates a genuine PARTY-TYPE CONVERSION from an
    // incoherent row, and the distinction is not academic - it was MEASURED
    // on the rendered form:
    //
    //   Changing Party Type from Organization to Person on the case_party
    //   form makes ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml
    //   set `organization` not-visible and not-mandatory. A UI Policy has no
    //   clear action, so the field keeps its stored value, its row stays in
    //   the DOM as display:none, and its submit input is hidden but NOT
    //   disabled - so the classic form POSTs the stale value verbatim.
    //   Captured from the wire:
    //       sys_original...party_type    = Organization
    //       ...party_type                = Person
    //       ...person                    = <the newly chosen user>
    //       ...organization              = <the OLD company, still sent>
    //
    //   The server therefore sees all three at once. Refusing that write
    //   would make a legitimate conversion IMPOSSIBLE through the only
    //   internal UI the AAP provides (Section 0.4.4: "provided by
    //   ServiceNow's automatic native list and form views"), and the caller
    //   could not even comply with the refusal - the field they are told to
    //   empty is not on their screen.
    //
    // So on a conversion the stale reference is NORMALISED AWAY rather than
    // rejected: it is form plumbing, not an expression of intent. The
    // discriminator the caller just changed is the authoritative statement of
    // what the row is, and clearing the column it makes inapplicable is the
    // only outcome that both honours that statement and leaves the stored row
    // satisfying the exactly-one-of invariant.
    //
    // What is NOT normalised, and stays a refusal:
    //   - an INSERT carrying both references (finding F15's reproduction 4).
    //     There is no prior discriminator to convert FROM, so "both set" is
    //     the caller's own incoherent input, not a form artifact.
    //   - an UPDATE that leaves party_type alone and sets the wrong
    //     reference. Nothing about that write says the row is changing
    //     identity, so silently discarding a value the caller deliberately
    //     supplied would hide their mistake instead of reporting it.
    var isUpdate = typeof current.operation === 'function' && current.operation() === 'update';
    var previousType = (isUpdate && previous)
        ? String(previous.getValue('party_type') || '').trim()
        : '';
    var typeChanged = previousType !== '' && previousType !== partyType;

    // ---- The exclusivity half. Walk every OTHER declared party_type: each
    // one names a reference this row must not carry. Deriving both halves
    // from the same PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS map is what keeps them from drifting
    // apart, and the loop stays correct for any number of declared
    // party_types without modification.
    for (var key in PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS) {
        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS, key) || key === partyType) {
            continue;
        }
        var spec = PARTY_TYPE_FIELDS[key];
        var value = current.getValue(spec.element);
        if (value === null || value === undefined || String(value).trim() === '') {
            continue;
        }

        if (typeChanged) {
            // Normalise: drop the reference the new discriminator makes
            // inapplicable and let the write proceed. setValue with '' clears
            // a reference column. This runs in a BEFORE rule, so the cleared
            // value is what gets persisted - no second write, no recursion.
            current.setValue(spec.element, '');

            // Logged because this is the one place the rule alters data the
            // caller sent, and an unexplained disappearance is worse than a
            // refusal. gs.info writes to the system log under the scoped
            // application; it fires only on an actual conversion, which is a
            // rare, deliberate operation, so it cannot become noise. Only
            // the record number, the field name and the two party_type values
            // are logged - never the cleared sys_id and never any
            // person/organization display value, so no identity data reaches
            // the log.
            gs.info('x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity: party ' +
                current.getValue('number') + ' converted from Party Type ' +
                previousType + ' to ' + partyType +
                '; cleared the now-inapplicable ' + spec.element + ' reference.');
            continue;
        }

        // This is the branch that refuses the both-set row finding F15
        // reproduced - a row that is simultaneously a Person party and an
        // Organization party - and the subtler partial update that sets the
        // wrong reference on an otherwise valid row without touching the
        // discriminator.
        gs.addErrorMessage(spec.label + ' must be empty when Party Type is ' + partyType + '.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    /**
     * Reports whether a supplied reference value points at a row that
     * exists, and does so WITHOUT ever converting "I am not allowed to
     * look" into "it is not there".
     *
     * That distinction is load-bearing on THIS table rather than merely
     * prudent, because one of the two branches points at an out-of-box
     * GLOBAL table: organization -> core_company. A scoped script's
     * ability to read a table outside its own scope depends on that
     * table's cross-scope access setting, and this application already
     * documents a related effect from the other direction - for the three
     * demo personas a direct read of core_company answers 404 and the
     * platform silently omits the column (see ../docs/
     * PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md, the reference-target-access
     * entry, disclosed as ADV-1). A naive `if (!gr.get(id))` here would
     * read an access restriction as a missing row and would refuse EVERY
     * Organization party carrying a perfectly valid company - converting a
     * validation improvement into a total outage of a required AAP Section
     * 0.5.7 branch. So this helper reports a missing row only when it can
     * first demonstrate that it can read the table at all.
     *
     * Plain GlideRecord is deliberate, exactly as it is for the parent
     * `case` lookup above: the question is EXISTENCE, never ACCESS.
     * GlideRecordSecure would apply the caller's read ACLs and would tell
     * an x_casemgmt_case_agent that a user or company they may not read
     * "does not exist" - false, and it would mask the ACL that actually
     * governs the operation. Access control belongs to the scoped ACLs of
     * AAP Section 0.5.6 under ../acl/.
     *
     * The sys_id argument is always the value the CALLER supplied on the
     * row being written, read at run time, so the AAP Section 0.7.2
     * no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint holds.
     *
     * @param {string} table - the reference target table name.
     * @param {string} sysId - the supplied reference value.
     * @return {boolean} true when the value is empty (presence is a
     *     separate contract, checked by the caller) or resolves, or when
     *     resolvability cannot be judged; false only when the table is
     *     demonstrably readable and the row is demonstrably absent.
     */
    function _referenceResolves(table, sysId) {
        var value = (sysId === null || sysId === undefined) ? '' : String(sysId).trim();
        if (value === '') {
            return true;
        }

        var probe = new GlideRecord(table);
        if (!probe.isValid()) {
            gs.info('x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity: cannot address ' +
                table + ' from this scope; skipped the resolvability check ' +
                'for reference value ' + value + '.');
            return true;
        }
        if (probe.get(value)) {
            return true;
        }

        var readable = new GlideRecord(table);
        readable.setLimit(1);
        readable.query();
        if (!readable.hasNext()) {
            gs.info('x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity: ' + table +
                ' returned no rows at all, so the absence of ' + value +
                ' could not be distinguished from a read restriction; ' +
                'skipped the resolvability check.');
            return true;
        }

        return false;
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>4004168331b9b9ca07f4cbfd349e25d8</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=4004168331b9b9ca07f4cbfd349e25d8"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Allows users with the x_casemgmt_case_agent role to read case_task records ONLY where the parent case has assigned_agent=current user OR assigned_group contains current user.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case_task</name><operation display_value="read">read</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var caseElement = current.getElement('case');
    if (!caseElement || caseElement.nil()) { return false; }
    var parentCase = caseElement.getRefRecord();
    if (!parentCase || !parentCase.isValidRecord()) { return false; }
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();
    if (parentCase.assigned_agent == currentUserId) { return true; }
    var groupId = parentCase.assigned_group.toString();
    if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) { return true; }
    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>1ea69bf11f64a85ddf0c7e970779fefe</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case_task</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_task_read_agent_assigned</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_8136e6a730a2da3c4c36038f572c4269
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>true</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-insert/update on x_casemgmt_case: when assigned_agent and assigned_group are both populated, validates that the agent is a member of the group via x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.isAgentInGroup(). On failure, surfaces the form-level error 'Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true). Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2: Open -> In Progress: 'assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group') and 0.5.7 (assigned_agent constraint: 'Optional; must be member of assigned_group'). Order=300 places this rule THIRD in the before-rule chain on x_casemgmt_case, after block_terminal_closed (100) and block_draft_backtransition (200) and before clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress (400) and set_closed_date (500); running after the prohibition guards is a deliberate performance optimization so we don't run the sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup on transitions that will be rejected anyway. Dual-triggered (action_insert=true AND action_update=true) because a manager (or seed script) may assign agent and group at case-creation time via a single Table API call, not just through subsequent updates. Skip conditions: (a) either agent or group is empty (b) neither field changed since previous - avoid redundant queries on non-assignment-touching updates. Defensive previous-null guard: on insert previous is null and both change-detection flags evaluate true so the membership is always validated for new rows. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types because the membership constraint applies regardless of case type. Defense in depth: validate_inprogress_transition subflow makes the same check at the workflow layer; this BR catches direct DB writes bypassing the flow. The error message wording is NOT prescribed verbatim by AAP Section 0.7.4 (which lists only four verbatim messages); the chosen wording is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own narrative wording. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals (runtime sys_id comparisons via .toString() are platform-canonical and permitted).</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membe</name><order>300</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7 (x_casemgmt_case schema row 10):
    //     "assigned_agent | Reference -> sys_user | Optional; must be
    //      member of assigned_group"
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2):
    //     | From | To          | Required condition                       | Failure handling          |
    //     | Open | In Progress | assigned_agent populated AND member of   | Surface form-level error  |
    //     |      |             | assigned_group                           |                           |
    //
    // The membership check is delegated to
    //     new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().isAgentInGroup(agentSysId, groupSysId)
    // which performs a sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup and returns a
    // plain boolean. The Script Include is the single source of truth for
    // the membership query so the same logic is reusable across this BR,
    // the validate_inprogress_transition Flow Designer subflow, ACL
    // conditions for child case_task and case_party rows, and the
    // seed-script preflight checks. Inlining a GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember')
    // query here would create a second source of truth and risk the two
    // implementations diverging on edge cases.
    //
    // Order=300 places this rule in the before-rule chain on x_casemgmt_case
    // after block_terminal_closed (order=100, blocks any edit to a Closed
    // case), block_draft_backtransition (order=200, blocks any rewind to
    // Draft) and enforce_forward_transitions (order=250, enforces the forward
    // preconditions).
    //
    // Order alone is NOT a short circuit. setAbortAction(true) cancels the
    // WRITE; the platform still runs every remaining before-update rule and
    // reports the pending abort through current.isActionAborted(). Ordering
    // therefore decides only whose message is added first. The explicit
    // abort-state guard below is what keeps this rule from adding a second
    // message to a save that an earlier rule already rejected - and the same
    // guard is present in the order-400 and order-500 rules.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: there was no direct equivalent at the JPA
    // entity layer in
    //   acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/
    //     com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java
    // CaseFile modeled assignment via an AcmParticipant collection (lines
    // 192, 336-340, 880-908) where ASSIGNEE and OWNING_GROUP participant
    // types coexisted on the case but the relational integrity between an
    // assignee and the owning group was enforced indirectly through the
    // LDAP/AD organizational structure - if a user existed in LDAP they
    // could be assigned regardless of their group membership. The
    // ServiceNow target makes this rule EXPLICIT at the data layer via
    // this BR plus the Script Include's isAgentInGroup() helper - a
    // deliberate hardening of the case assignment contract. This is a
    // TARGET-SIDE AUTHORED rule with no byte-for-byte source analog.

    // Read the assigned_agent and assigned_group sys_id values from the
    // platform-injected `current` GlideRecord. The .toString() coercion
    // normalizes the GlideElement reference field to its underlying sys_id
    // string. Without explicit coercion, the GlideElement instance auto-
    // converts in some contexts but not others (string concatenation =
    // string conversion; equality comparison via === = identity comparison;
    // method-argument passing = pass-by-value of the underlying string
    // for primitive comparisons but pass-by-reference of the GlideElement
    // wrapper for complex operations). The downstream isAgentInGroup()
    // method explicitly handles String() coercion of its arguments and
    // GlideRecord.addQuery() accepts both forms, but explicit .toString()
    // here is the platform-canonical defensive pattern and avoids any
    // wrapper-vs-primitive ambiguity downstream.
    var agent = current.assigned_agent.toString();
    var group = current.assigned_group.toString();

    // Skip if either field is empty. The AAP defines assigned_agent as
    // optional (Section 0.5.7: "Optional"); a case without an assigned
    // agent is a valid state (e.g., Draft cases, Open cases waiting for
    // agent assignment). assigned_group is mandatory only on the
    // Open transition (per dictionary mandatory_on_open=true at
    // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_assigned_group.xml) - that mandatory
    // requirement is enforced separately by the form-level mandatory flag
    // and the validate_open_transition subflow, NOT by this BR.
    // This BR's responsibility is narrow: validate the membership
    // RELATIONSHIP when both fields are present. If either field is
    // absent, the relationship cannot be validated and the rule does
    // nothing.
    if (!agent || !group) {
        return;
    }

    // Skip if neither agent nor group changed (avoid redundant queries on
    // every save, including subsequent updates that touch only other
    // fields like description, priority, or status). For a case that
    // travels through the full state-machine
    //   Draft -> Open -> In Progress -> Pending -> In Progress -> Resolved -> Closed
    // the assignment fields typically change at most twice (once when the
    // group is set on Draft -> Open, once when the agent is set on
    // Open -> In Progress). This guard ensures the BR runs the
    // sys_user_grmember query at most twice across the full lifecycle
    // rather than five times.
    //
    // On INSERT, `previous` is null (no prior state), so the ternary's
    // !previous branch evaluates true for both flags - the BR always
    // validates the membership on a brand-new row. This is the correct
    // semantic: a manager creating a case AND assigning both group and
    // agent in a single operation must have the assignment validated
    // before the row is persisted, otherwise an invalid agent-group
    // pairing could be created and only caught on the first subsequent
    // update.
    var agentChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_agent) !== agent;
    var groupChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_group) !== group;
    if (!agentChanged && !groupChanged) {
        return;
    }

    // Skip if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    // The platform continues running before-update rules after
    // setAbortAction(true) and exposes the pending abort through
    // current.isActionAborted(). Returning here keeps a rejected transition
    // (for example Closed -> * refused at order 100, or a forward
    // precondition refused at order 250) from collecting a second, unrelated
    // membership message on top of the message the user needs to read, and
    // avoids a sys_user_grmember query for a row that will never be written.
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
    // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
    // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the
    // `CaseTransitionValidator` portion is the api_name of the Script
    // Include declared in
    // ../script_includes/x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator.xml at
    // <api_name>x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator</api_name>. NO sys_id
    // literal - the resolution is by scoped class name only.
    var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();

    // Call isAgentInGroup(userSysId, groupSysId). The Script Include's
    // method (line 656 in CaseTransitionValidator.xml) returns a plain
    // boolean: true when at least one sys_user_grmember row links the
    // given user to the given group, false otherwise (including when
    // either argument is null/empty/whitespace). The boolean shape
    // (rather than the {ok, error} pair used by validateNoBacktransition
    // and the canTransitionTo* family) is intentional: isAgentInGroup is
    // a simple yes/no membership predicate reusable from contexts that
    // have no error-message surface (e.g., ACL condition expressions).
    // The form-level error string is owned by THIS BR and surfaced via
    // gs.addErrorMessage(...) below.
    if (!validator.isAgentInGroup(agent, group)) {
        // gs.addErrorMessage('...') surfaces the form-level error at the
        // top of the case form when the user attempts the save through
        // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
        // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. Per AAP Section 0.7.1:
        // "Surface all blocking errors on the form. Invalid transition
        // attempts MUST produce a blocking error message visible on the
        // form - silent failures or post-save error logs are
        // unacceptable."
        //
        // Per AAP Section 0.7.4, only four error messages are verbatim
        // (non-negotiable): "All tasks must be closed before resolving
        // this case.", "Cases cannot be returned to Draft.", "Closed
        // cases are terminal and cannot be modified.", and "No case
        // found with that number." This rule's message is NOT in that
        // list, so the wording here is target-side authored. The chosen
        // string is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own
        // narrative wording in Section 0.5.7 ("Optional; must be member
        // of assigned_group").
        gs.addErrorMessage('Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.');

        // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
        // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
        // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
        // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
        // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
        // would still update with the invalid agent-group pairing;
        // without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write would be silently
        // rejected with no visible failure and no diagnostic message
        // for the caller.
        current.setAbortAction(true);
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>8136e6a730a2da3c4c36038f572c4269</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=8136e6a730a2da3c4c36038f572c4269"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_3719a93101a32c5e06c9907fbcfa8d03
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Field-level ACL: x_casemgmt_case_manager can always write assigned_agent; x_casemgmt_case_agent can write assigned_agent only if they are the currently-assigned agent on the case. Allows agent self-reassignment without permitting case-grabbing.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case.assigned_agent</name><operation display_value="write">write</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.1: "Field-level ACL: write restricted to
    // manager and agent-assigned". Per AAP Section 0.5.6 Matrix and
    // Section 0.7.3 Gate 3 ("case_agent cannot access unassigned
    // cases"), this script must DENY by default and grant only to
    // (a) any case_manager, and (b) a case_agent who is on the case
    // under Section 0.5.6's own definition of "Assigned only".

    // Branch 1: case_manager - unconditional grant.
    // The manager is the case-management tier's delegation authority;
    // they may freely assign, reassign, or null-out the assigned_agent
    // column on any case in the scoped application.
    if (gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager')) {
        return true;
    }

    // Branch 2: a case_agent who is on the case per "Assigned only".
    //
    // AAP Section 0.5.6 defines that phrase verbatim as "cases where
    // assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current
    // user", and BOTH limbs are evaluated here against the STORED row.
    //
    // The second limb closes QA finding F6. An earlier revision granted
    // only on `current.assigned_agent == gs.getUserID()`, which is
    // evaluated against the stored value, so an assigned agent could
    // CLEAR assigned_agent (the stored value was still theirs at
    // evaluation time) but could never RE-POPULATE it (the stored value
    // was now empty, so the single limb evaluated false). Measured on
    // CASE9000003: the clear returned HTTP 200 and landed; the
    // re-populate returned HTTP 200 with the value silently discarded
    // and sys_mod_count unchanged for that column - a one-way door that
    // let an agent permanently orphan a case from their own queue,
    // recoverable only by a manager. Because the field-ACL engine strips
    // a denied value BEFORE business rules run (measured with a
    // temporary before-update probe: the denied column reported
    // changes() === false while an allowed column on the same request
    // reported changes() === true), no server-side rule can detect or
    // report that drop, so the only correct remedy is to grant the
    // legitimate write here.
    //
    // What this does NOT allow. Both limbs read the STORED row, so an
    // agent can populate assigned_agent only on a case that is already
    // theirs or already assigned to a group they belong to - exactly
    // the set Section 0.5.6 already grants them table-level read and
    // write on. A case assigned to another group, or to no group and no
    // agent, satisfies neither limb; the caller is additionally refused
    // by the table-level write ACL
    // (../acl/x_casemgmt_case_write_agent_assigned.xml), which returns
    // HTTP 403 rather than dropping the column. Grabbing a case outside
    // the agent's own assignment is therefore refused twice over.
    //
    // The comparison `current.assigned_agent == gs.getUserID()` works
    // in ServiceNow because GlideRecord reference fields auto-resolve
    // to their sys_id when compared as strings; this is the standard
    // pattern used throughout the platform's ACL conditions. The group
    // limb uses gs.getUser().isMemberOf(), the same call the two
    // table-level "Assigned only" ACLs use, so the three records agree
    // on one definition of membership.
    if (gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_agent')) {
        if (current.assigned_agent == gs.getUserID()) {
            return true;
        }
        if (current.assigned_group && !current.assigned_group.nil()) {
            var groupId = current.assigned_group.toString();
            if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) {
                return true;
            }
        }
    }

    // Default: deny. Viewers, anonymous users, and any other role
    // populations fall through to this branch. Per AAP Section 0.5.6
    // case_viewer has Write=No on every column of x_casemgmt_case;
    // this default-deny implements that mandate at the field level.
    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>3719a93101a32c5e06c9907fbcfa8d03</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case.assigned_agent</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_3719a93101a32c5e06c9907fbcfa8d03</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 05:45:34</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_c4a2b80fa17ba2a619a7e55c692945aa
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Allows users with the x_casemgmt_case_agent role to write/update case_party records ONLY where the parent case has assigned_agent=current user OR assigned_group contains current user.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case_party</name><operation display_value="write">write</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var caseElement = current.getElement('case');
    if (!caseElement || caseElement.nil()) { return false; }
    var parentCase = caseElement.getRefRecord();
    if (!parentCase || !parentCase.isValidRecord()) { return false; }
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();
    if (parentCase.assigned_agent == currentUserId) { return true; }
    var groupId = parentCase.assigned_group.toString();
    if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) { return true; }
    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>c4a2b80fa17ba2a619a7e55c692945aa</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case_party</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_party_write_agent_assigned</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_ui_policy_854295ebb4c8309eea6a52aa788ec8a9
sys_update_xml.payload:
trueparty_type=PersonPolymorphic field-rendering UI Policy on x_casemgmt_case_party for the Person branch of the party_type discriminator. Implements the ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase's @DiscriminatorColumn(cm_class_name) single-table inheritance pattern from PersonAssociation.java per AAP Section 0.4.3 ("Polymorphic association via single-table choice + UI Policy"). When party_type=Person the single sys_ui_policy_action child makes the person reference field visible and mandatory; because reverse_if_false=true, any other party_type value - including empty - reverses that action so person becomes hidden and not mandatory. This policy deliberately acts on the person field ONLY: the organization field is owned exclusively by the companion policy "Case Party Conditional Fields - Organization", so the two policies can never contend for the same field and their relative order is irrelevant. Declarative actions plus reverse_if_false give the platform a watched field (party_type, taken from the condition) so the state is re-evaluated on every change, not only at form load; on_load=true additionally applies the correct state when an existing party record is opened. run_scripts is false and both script bodies are empty - there is no imperative logic. cleared=false on the action so toggling party_type never destroys a value the user already entered. The person field is nullable at the dictionary level (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_person.xml) precisely so that its required-ness can be conditional here.truefalsefalsetrue100truefalseCase Party Conditional Fields - Person: show person and make it mandatory when party_type=Person; reverse (hide, not mandatory) for every other value including empty.sys_ui_policysystem2025-01-01 00:00:00global/854295ebb4c8309eea6a52aa788ec8a90Case Party Conditional Fields - Person: show person and make it mandatory when party_type=Person; reverse (hide, not mandatory) for every other value including empty.82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_ui_policy_854295ebb4c8309eea6a52aa788ec8a9system2025-01-01 00:00:00x_casemgmt_case_party

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_client_1575547870432ff027b60f5a5f3497be
sys_update_xml.payload:
truefalsePolymorphic discriminator hygiene for x_casemgmt_case_party (verifier finding I2). On every change of party_type the script clears the reference column the new discriminator makes inapplicable - organization when party_type becomes Person, person when it becomes Organization - so the hidden field left behind by ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml cannot post a stale sys_id. Without it the classic form submits the hidden, non-disabled input verbatim (measured: party_type=Person with both the new person and the old organization on the wire), ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity.xml correctly refuses with "Organization must be empty when Party Type is Person." plus Invalid insert, and the user cannot clear the blocking value because the field is not on their screen - a dead end on any INSERT and on any UPDATE whose discriminator round-trips back to the stored value, since the rule normalises only a genuine update-conversion. A sys_ui_policy_action cannot do this: its `cleared` flag is one-way with no reverse, it would force one policy to act on the other's field and reinstate the contention the one-field-per-policy design removes, it would fire on load and so mutate stored data on a mere open, and a policy cannot see newValue/isLoading to restrict itself to an actual change. Clears the value and the reference display text together, never touches the applicable field, and returns having changed nothing on isLoading, on an empty party_type and on any discriminator value it does not recognise. The server-side rule remains the enforcing authority for every non-form write path. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.5.7 and 0.7.2.party_typetruefalsex_casemgmt_case_party_clear_opposite_ref200sys_script_clientadmin2025-01-01 00:00:00global/1575547870432ff027b60f5a5f3497be0x_casemgmt_case_party_clear_opposite_ref82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_script_client_1575547870432ff027b60f5a5f3497beadmin2025-01-01 00:00:00x_casemgmt_case_party

No create, write, or delete privileges (deny-by-default).</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case_task</name><operation display_value="read">read</operation><script/><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>536eb8c8bcfc523db221fc9ea9b68505</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case_task</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_task_read_viewer</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_ed26b2ef9256d55de66e4c1ac7b1997e
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Table-level ACL: x_casemgmt_case_agent can read x_casemgmt_case records ONLY when assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current user (per AAP Section 0.5.6 'Assigned only'). Affects list views, form load, related lists, report rows, and dashboard aggregates - any unauthorized case row is filtered out of every read surface.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case</name><operation display_value="read">read</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();

    // INSERT PATH - the read side of QA finding F4's create path.
    //
    // ServiceNow evaluates the READ ACL per column when it renders a form,
    // including the NEW-record form, where the row has not been inserted
    // yet. On that skeleton every limb below is false - assigned_agent and
    // assigned_group are empty (and assigned_group is manager-only), and
    // sys_created_by is not stamped until the insert - so the platform
    // judged every column unreadable and rendered the agent a case form
    // with ZERO fields: no Subject, no Description, no Requester Name, no
    // Type, and g_form.getEditableFields() empty. Measured on the rendered
    // form; the application's own client script reported it verbatim as
    // "x_casemgmt_case_flush_stale_messages: bound 0 of 4 mandatory field
    // control(s); not on form or not readable: subject, status,
    // description, requester_name". The agent could only obtain a usable
    // form by submitting the blank one, absorbing "Subject is mandatory and
    // cannot be empty." + "Invalid insert" and working on the redisplay -
    // which also consumed a case number. AAP Section 0.7.4 requires cases
    // to be creatable "via both internal UI and external portal", so the
    // create grant in Section 0.5.6 has to include being able to see the
    // form one is filling in.
    //
    // This limb exposes no stored data: isNewRecord() is true only for a
    // row that does not exist yet, whose column values are exactly the
    // defaults and the caller's own keystrokes. It mirrors the identical
    // limb on the WRITE sibling
    // (../acl/x_casemgmt_case_write_agent_assigned.xml), and every
    // already-inserted record continues to be judged by the three limbs
    // below.
    if (current.isNewRecord()) {
        return true;
    }

    // AAP Section 0.5.6 "Assigned only", verbatim predicate.
    if (current.assigned_agent == currentUserId) {
        return true;
    }
    if (current.assigned_group && !current.assigned_group.nil()) {
        var groupId = current.assigned_group.toString();
        if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) {
            return true;
        }
    }

    // NO CREATOR LIMB - and this absence is deliberate. Do not re-add one.
    //
    // A revision of this ACL carried a fourth limb,
    //     if (current.sys_created_by == gs.getUserName()) return true;
    // added so that an agent who creates an UNASSIGNED case could still
    // read the row they had just authored. It was removed, because it
    // widened read access beyond the contract and the widening produced a
    // worse defect than the one it was meant to close.
    //
    // Why it is outside the contract: AAP Section 0.5.6 does not leave
    // "Assigned only" to interpretation, it DEFINES it - "cases where
    // assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current
    // user". That definition is exhaustive, and authorship is not one of
    // its two limbs. The three limbs above are the definition; a fourth is
    // a different rule wearing the same name.
    //
    // Why the widening was actively harmful, measured: READ gained the
    // creator limb but WRITE could not be given one without extending
    // Section 0.5.6's write cell the same way, so an agent-created
    // unassigned case became READABLE BUT FROZEN - it opened with zero
    // editable fields and no Update action, ordinary field PATCHes answered
    // 403, and the agent could not even self-assign out of the state. That
    // is a stranded row that looks like work in progress and can never be
    // progressed, which is strictly worse for the agent than not seeing it
    // at all.
    //
    // What the correct behaviour therefore is: an agent who supplies
    // assigned_agent = themselves at insert satisfies limb one immediately,
    // and that row is readable AND writable AND editable on its form -
    // verified. An agent who inserts with no assignment at all creates a
    // row they cannot read until a manager assigns it, and that is not a
    // defect but Section 0.5.6's matrix operating as written: Section 0.7.4
    // describes the lifecycle as cases "created, assigned, progressed ...
    // and closed", with assignment a manager act - assigned_group is
    // manager-only per ../acl/x_casemgmt_case_assigned_group_field_acl.xml.
    // The create grant remains fully usable, which is what AAP Section
    // 0.7.4 requires of it.
    //
    // The isNewRecord() limb above is a different matter and is retained:
    // it exposes no stored row at all, only the defaults and the caller's
    // own keystrokes on a form that has not been inserted yet, and without
    // it the create grant cannot be exercised through the UI because the
    // NEW form renders with zero fields.
    //
    // See ../docs/acl-matrix.md, "Assigned only - the create-path limb".

    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>ed26b2ef9256d55de66e4c1ac7b1997e</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_ed26b2ef9256d55de66e4c1ac7b1997e</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 05:45:34</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

Task-closure gate blocks In Progress to Resolved with the verbatim message">c225a1c9cc36ac254b284caeea84a9ae</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=1259511d217469f43e598d8debaf4041"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>1259511d217469f43e598d8debaf4041</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>920a9f226dfa60926f4e6f2417a7a7b1</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>1259511d217469f43e598d8debaf4041</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>f8e1bc83400dfb41f84f91f867d14c31</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    var gr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    gr.get('8eb58da796d8386b3ecc5493644a5911');
    var v = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
    chk('open child task count is now zero', '0', String(v.getOpenTaskCountForCase('8eb58da796d8386b3ecc5493644a5911')));
    chkTrue('canTransitionToResolved is now allowed', v.canTransitionToResolved(gr).ok);
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('gate reopens once every task is Closed: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'gate reopens once every task is Closed', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>

Form: returning a case to Draft is blocked on the form">058f262dab9141adcb30c3bd61667a78</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=29e00872198b161f721a8f151f71887b"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>29e00872198b161f721a8f151f71887b</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>4190700dfd50eed55feaae80a87d9c7a</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>29e00872198b161f721a8f151f71887b</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>ecdbdb92e59f4c20cb73a5a99f172814</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "open",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "8245a6f0cd348d300927983d87085c9b",
            "prefix": "ATF-UI-16",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-UI-16 open case",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Open",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team"
            }
        }
    ];

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    // GUARD FOR THE CLIENT HANDOFF (step 3, "Open an Existing Record").
    // That step does not read the row itself: the browser calls the platform's own
    // GLOBAL-scope Script Include TestExecutorAjax.validateFormParameters, which
    // resolves it with a plain GlideRecord. If this application's tables refuse
    // cross-scope reads, that lookup returns nothing and the step fails with
    // "Table 'x_casemgmt_case' does not have a record with id '...'" - which reads
    // like a missing fixture but is really a table access-policy problem. The five
    // boolean cross-scope columns on sys_db_object (ws_access, read_access,
    // create_access, update_access, delete_access) must be TRUE; see
    // ../tables/x_casemgmt_case.xml. Asserting the fixture is resolvable HERE turns
    // that misleading downstream failure into a precise one, and it also removes any
    // dependence on a row left behind by an earlier run.
    for (var g = 0; g < FIX.length; g++) {
        var reread = new GlideRecord(FIX[g].table);
        chkTrue('fixture ' + FIX[g].label + ' is resolvable by sys_id after insert (the client form step resolves it the same way)',
            reread.get(FIX[g].sys_id));
    }
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>

server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    var gr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    chkTrue('fixture case readable', gr.get('8eb58da796d8386b3ecc5493644a5911'));
    var v = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
    chk('open child task count', '1', String(v.getOpenTaskCountForCase('8eb58da796d8386b3ecc5493644a5911')));
    var verdict = v.canTransitionToResolved(gr);
    chk('canTransitionToResolved is refused', 'false', String(verdict.ok));
    chk('blocking message is verbatim', 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.', String(verdict.error));
    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends. Emitted separately, the
    // evidence line below was written and then silently discarded, so the run output
    // never showed the value these assertions were made against.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('message: [' + verdict.error + ']');
    notes.push('verbatim task-closure message: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'verbatim task-closure message', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);

RBAC mirror on x_casemgmt_case_task and x_casemgmt_case_party (manager, viewer)">f6256084e214d739604fe63b4bcba018</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=d894cac40bd0a520e296613c6ea4dfab"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>d894cac40bd0a520e296613c6ea4dfab</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>54cb64b2303b7e12c19603ff638f8a55</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>d894cac40bd0a520e296613c6ea4dfab</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>c87f45f1853bc990324c1e835ed1d45f</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    chk('impersonated user', 'x_casemgmt_demo_viewer', gs.getUserName());
    var tk = new GlideRecordSecure('x_casemgmt_case_task');
    chkTrue('viewer canRead task', tk.get('94a0371e5a4444df0b4fecab96375fde'));
    chk('viewer canCreate task', 'false', String(tk.canCreate()));
    chk('viewer canWrite task', 'false', String(tk.canWrite()));
    chk('viewer canDelete task', 'false', String(tk.canDelete()));
    var pt = new GlideRecordSecure('x_casemgmt_case_party');
    chkTrue('viewer canRead party', pt.get('165fe5387948213f9b16f8ade71c0749'));
    chk('viewer canCreate party', 'false', String(pt.canCreate()));
    chk('viewer canWrite party', 'false', String(pt.canWrite()));
    chk('viewer canDelete party', 'false', String(pt.canDelete()));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('viewer capability matrix on the child tables: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'viewer capability matrix on the child tables', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>
