sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_663cfa5f92d4b5208f2a0a4a7bc625ee
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>false</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Field-level ACL granting the query_range operation on x_casemgmt_case.closed_date to x_casemgmt_case_manager, x_casemgmt_case_agent and x_casemgmt_case_viewer. Authored for QA finding F17, which reported every range predicate on this column (>, <, BETWEEN, 'at or after', 'last 30 days') being dropped from the query for non-admin callers - 0 rows plus a server ACL banner naming the query_range operation inside an HTTP 200 list page, and HTTP 403 'Insufficient rights to query records' over the Table API. Retained as an explicit scoped grant rather than a proven repair: re-verification could not reproduce the refusal, and a differential probe measured no difference against columns carrying no such ACL, so this record makes the range filtering implied by AAP Section 0.5.6 'Read - All' independent of the instance's default query_range posture. query_range shapes the query only; which rows are returned remains governed by each role's read ACL, so the agent still sees just its assigned set.</description><local_or_existing>Existing</local_or_existing><name>x_casemgmt_case.closed_date</name><operation display_value="query_range">e66cf897b7300210240b06dd1e11a9fd</operation><script/><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-10 00:21:46</sys_created_on><sys_id>663cfa5f92d4b5208f2a0a4a7bc625ee</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case.closed_date</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_663cfa5f92d4b5208f2a0a4a7bc625ee</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 03:30:24</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_0943b10691d8ae86fd3c2fd6994eb693
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>false</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-update on x_casemgmt_case: when previous.status == 'Pending' AND current.status == 'In Progress', clears current.pending_reason (sets it to empty string). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (Pending->In Progress: clears pending_reason). Order=400 ensures this rule runs after the transition guards (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at order=200, validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) but before set_closed_date (order=500), so it only fires after all guards have approved the transition. Companion to ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml which SETS pending_reason on the In Progress->Pending transition; this rule CLEARS it on the reverse transition. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types since the Pending state is shared. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero GlideRecord lookups.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inpro</name><order>400</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 verbatim:
    //     "Pending -> In Progress: None; clears pending_reason"
    //
    // The pending_reason field is SET by the Flow Designer subflow
    // ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml when the case
    // transitions INTO Pending. When the case transitions OUT of Pending
    // back to In Progress, the previously stored reason is no longer
    // relevant and would be misleading on the form. This rule guarantees
    // the field is empty for any non-Pending case reached via the
    // Pending -> In Progress transition path.
    //
    // This BR has no ArkCase source-side analog. ArkCase did not have
    // a discrete Pending sub-state with a typed reason code; this is
    // target-side-only behavior introduced by the AAP design.
    //
    // Order=400 places this rule after the transition guards
    // (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at
    // order=200, enforce_forward_transitions at order=250,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) and before
    // set_closed_date (order=500), which handles the Resolved -> Closed
    // side-effect.
    //
    // Order alone does NOT skip this rule when an earlier guard rejects the
    // save: setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, and the platform keeps
    // running the rest of the before-update chain, reporting the pending
    // abort through current.isActionAborted(). The explicit guard below is
    // what prevents pending_reason from being cleared on the in-memory record
    // of a transition that is about to be rejected - without it the
    // redisplayed form would show an empty Pending Reason for a case that
    // still holds one in the database.
    //
    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null
    // in certain async/system contexts. If there is no previous state,
    // no transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing. The
    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string
    // for safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string
    // equality can behave inconsistently across releases.
    var prevStatus = previous ? String(previous.status) : '';
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Verbatim Title Case status values per AAP Section 0.5.7 and the
    // sibling choice list ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml. The
    // labels ARE the stored values - ServiceNow Choice fields persist
    // the LABEL string by default, not an integer ID. Note 'In Progress'
    // contains a literal SPACE in the middle (NOT 'In_Progress', NOT
    // 'InProgress', NOT 'in progress'). Misspelled variants would
    // silently never match and the rule would never fire - a critical
    // correctness concern that is encoded by these exact string literals.
    if (prevStatus === 'Pending' && newStatus === 'In Progress') {
        // Do not mutate a rejected save. An earlier before-update rule may
        // have called setAbortAction(true); the platform still runs this rule
        // and only current.isActionAborted() reveals that state. Clearing the
        // field here would leave the redisplayed form contradicting the
        // database.
        if (current.isActionAborted()) {
            return;
        }

        // The empty-string assignment is the canonical ServiceNow pattern
        // for clearing a Choice field's value. Per
        // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_pending_reason.xml the field is
        // non-mandatory (mandatory=false), so clearing it is a legitimate
        // end-state - the row remains valid with an empty pending_reason
        // for any non-Pending status. The next time the case transitions
        // to Pending, the validate_pending_transition subflow will prompt
        // for a fresh reason and populate the field again.
        current.pending_reason = '';
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>0943b10691d8ae86fd3c2fd6994eb693</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=0943b10691d8ae86fd3c2fd6994eb693"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_script_include"><sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>package_private</access><active>true</active><api_name>x_casemgmt.CasePortalService</api_name><caller_access/><client_callable>false</client_callable><description>Server-side helper for the unauthenticated Experience Portal. Provides submitCase(payload) for anonymous case submission and lookupCase(number) for anonymous status lookup. Enforces strict field whitelisting per AAP Section 0.7.4: submission accepts only subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email and forces status=Draft regardless of payload; lookup returns only status, subject, opened_date and never exposes internal fields. submitCase validates its input before inserting - subject, description and requester_name are required and must not exceed 255/4000/100 characters (an over-length value is refused with a named field error, never truncated), requester_email must look like an address when supplied and must not exceed 100 characters, type must be a live choice of x_casemgmt_case.type - an admission ceiling evaluated AFTER the insert bounds the unauthenticated write path (the same caller's rows inside a 60-second window are counted with the inserted row among them, and a count above the global ceiling of 10, or above the per-requester ceiling of 4 taken over the rows sharing its normalised requester_email bucket, deletes the row again and refuses it with throttled=true; counting published rows after the insert bounds the window absolutely - the last caller to count necessarily sees every row that survives - whereas a count taken before the insert bounds nothing and a rank taken after it admits any caller whose query sees only part of the window), and an identical submission received inside a 90-second window is collapsed onto the surviving case (same five values, still Draft, same caller) so a retry or a simultaneous double-post yields one case rather than two - the duplicate row is deleted and its case number is consumed, leaving a gap in the CASE sequence; submitCase returns {number} on success, {error, fields} when validation refuses the payload, {error, throttled} when the admission ceiling refuses it, or {error} when the insert fails; lookupCase normalises and strictly validates the supplied number against ^CASE[0-9]{7}$ before any query, throttles the read path per session in the GlideSession client-data store, and warns under the stable marker X_CASEMGMT_PORTAL_LOOKUP_ABUSE| when a session crosses the soft miss threshold or is throttled; it returns the whitelisted record on match, {throttled} when the session is over its ceiling (the REST operation answers HTTP 429), or null on no-match - which a malformed, empty or absent number produces identically and without a query (the calling scripted REST endpoint translates null into the HTTP 404 not-found response whose verbatim body is specified by AAP Section 0.7.4). The hit-versus-miss distinction is inherent to the single-factor number-only lookup the AAP mandates and is compensated rather than removed; the residual risk is recorded in docs/portal-pages.md. Replaces the persistence and lookup roles of ArkCase SaveCaseService and GetCaseByNumberService for the portal slice. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id reference literals.</description><mobile_callable>false</mobile_callable><name>CasePortalService</name><sandbox_callable>false</sandbox_callable><script><![CDATA[var CasePortalService = Class.create();
CasePortalService.prototype = {
    /**
     * No-arg initializer. The class holds no per-instance state across
     * calls (each request from the scripted REST handler instantiates a
     * fresh CasePortalService), so initialize() is intentionally empty.
     */
    initialize: function() {
    },

    /**
     * Anonymous case submission entry point.
     *
     * Whitelist-only field handling per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *   - Accepted fields: subject, type, description, requester_name,
     *     requester_email
     *   - All other fields are silently dropped (no error returned for
     *     unrecognized keys; this matches the AAP requirement that the
     *     portal not surface internal field names to anonymous callers
     *     even by way of validation error messages).
     *   - status is FORCED to 'Draft' regardless of payload. Even if a
     *     malicious caller sends status='Closed' or any non-Draft value,
     *     the server overwrites to 'Draft' before insert. This is the
     *     single security guarantee that anonymous submissions cannot
     *     bypass the state-machine workflow.
     *   - Returns the auto-generated case number (CASE0000001 format)
     *     on success. The number generator is configured in
     *     ../numbers/sys_number_x_casemgmt_case.xml.
     *   - An identical submission received inside the de-duplication
     *     window is answered with the number of the case that survives
     *     it, and its own row is removed, so a retry or a simultaneous
     *     double-post yields ONE case rather than two. The response shape
     *     is unchanged - { number } either way - so no caller has to know
     *     which of the two happened.
     *
     * Robust input handling per Rule 9 of the agent prompt: gracefully
     * handle null, undefined, and non-object payloads without throwing
     * uncaught exceptions (the unauthenticated REST endpoint can receive
     * any malformed payload from the public Internet).
     *
     * @param {Object} payload - request payload from the scripted REST
     *     endpoint, as parsed from the JSON request body.
     * @return {Object} { number: 'CASE0000001' } on success; or
     *     { error: '<message>', fields: { <field>: '<reason>' } } when the
     *     payload fails validation (the REST operation answers HTTP 400);
     *     or { error: '<message>', throttled: true } when the anonymous
     *     flood guard refuses the request (HTTP 429); or
     *     { error: '<message>' } when the insert itself fails.
     */
    submitCase: function(payload) {
        // Defensive null/type check. The scripted REST endpoint should
        // already have parsed JSON into an object, but a malformed
        // request could yield null/undefined/string/array; guard against
        // all of those without leaking implementation details to the caller.
        if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload)) {
            return { error: 'Invalid payload.' };
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // VALIDATION GATE (AAP Section 0.5.7 constraints, enforced here
        // because nothing else on this write path enforces them).
        //
        // The dictionary marks subject, description and requester_name
        // Mandatory, but a scoped GlideRecord.insert() performed by this
        // Script Include does NOT run the platform's mandatory-field UI
        // validation: mandatory is a form/ACL-time construct, so an insert
        // carrying empty strings succeeds silently. Likewise, ServiceNow
        // backs string columns longer than 255 with a TEXT column that does
        // NOT truncate, so the declared 4000-character description limit is
        // only real if this method enforces it. Both gaps were reproduced
        // against the live endpoint (blank mandatory fields accepted with
        // HTTP 201; a 6006-character description stored in full), so the
        // guard below is the fix for them, and for a `type` value outside
        // the declared choice list.
        //
        // Validation runs BEFORE any GlideRecord is initialized so a
        // rejected submission cannot leave a partial row behind.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var validated = this._validateSubmission(payload);
        if (validated.error) {
            return validated;
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // ANONYMOUS FLOOD GUARD - EVALUATED AFTER THE INSERT, NOT BEFORE IT.
        // The guard used to run here, as a count-then-decide check ahead of
        // the insert. That ordering is unenforceable under concurrency: every
        // parallel caller read the same pre-insert count, every one of them
        // saw it below the ceiling, and every one of them was admitted, so the
        // ceiling bounded nothing at all. The admission decision now happens
        // AFTER the row exists, in _admitAnonymousSubmission - see that method
        // for why coupling the decision to the insert is what makes the
        // ceiling real, and for the per-requester fairness cap that stops one
        // caller consuming the whole allowance.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var caseGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        caseGr.initialize();

        // Whitelisted input fields per AAP Section 0.7.4. The five fields
        // below are EXACTLY the inputs the case submission page exposes
        // to anonymous callers (../portal/pages/sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_submit.xml
        // and the submission widget at
        // ../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget.xml).
        // Any other key in the payload is silently dropped - we do not
        // even acknowledge unrecognized keys via an error response, so a
        // probing client cannot enumerate internal field names.
        //
        // The values written are the VALIDATED, trimmed, length-checked
        // values produced by _validateSubmission(), never the raw payload.
        var WHITELIST = ['subject', 'type', 'description', 'requester_name', 'requester_email'];
        for (var i = 0; i < WHITELIST.length; i++) {
            var fieldName = WHITELIST[i];
            if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(validated.values, fieldName)) {
                caseGr.setValue(fieldName, validated.values[fieldName]);
            }
        }

        // FORCE status='Draft' regardless of payload (security perimeter).
        // Anonymous submissions ALWAYS start in Draft per AAP Sections
        // 0.5.5 and 0.7.4; the state-machine in the Flow Designer flows
        // (../flows/general_inquiry_state_machine.xml,
        // ../flows/complaint_state_machine.xml) advances the case from
        // Draft to subsequent statuses only via authenticated internal
        // user actions. Even if the dictionary's default_value='Draft'
        // already covers most insert paths, an explicit setValue() here
        // defends against a payload that includes status='Closed' (or
        // any other string) attempting to skip the state-machine entirely.
        caseGr.setValue('status', 'Draft');

        // Insert the new row. The insert() return value is the new
        // record's sys_id on success or null on failure. Failure here
        // typically indicates a before-insert business rule rejected the
        // record (e.g., a missing mandatory field that the portal client
        // forgot to send), or a database/platform error.
        var newSysId = caseGr.insert();
        if (!newSysId) {
            // gs.error() emits a diagnostic to the system log. Per Rule 5
            // of the agent prompt, we log getLastErrorMessage() (a
            // system-generated diagnostic) but NOT the raw payload (which
            // could carry PII like a real requester email). The error
            // returned to the caller is intentionally generic ("Submission
            // failed.") so a probing client cannot extract field-level
            // validation hints.
            gs.error('CasePortalService.submitCase: insert failed; lastErrorMessage=' + caseGr.getLastErrorMessage());
            return { error: 'Submission failed.' };
        }

        // Re-query by sys_id to read the auto-generated 'number' field.
        // The number is populated by the platform's Number Maintenance
        // subsystem during the insert pipeline; on most platform releases
        // the number is already visible on the original GlideRecord by
        // the time insert() returns, but a fresh GlideRecord.get(sys_id)
        // is the documented defensive pattern that works across all
        // releases (Yokohama and later per AAP Section 0.6.1).
        //
        // The newSysId used here is the value returned by insert() in the
        // line above - it is NOT a hardcoded sys_id literal, so this
        // GlideRecord.get(newSysId) call complies with the AAP Section
        // 0.7.2 no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
        var savedGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        if (!savedGr.get(newSysId)) {
            gs.error('CasePortalService.submitCase: post-insert lookup failed for sys_id=' + newSysId);
            return { error: 'Submission failed.' };
        }

        // The admission decision. Our row is published, so every concurrent
        // caller now counts a window that already contains it, and the last
        // caller to count cannot miss a row that survives. A
        // refused submission has already removed its own row inside
        // _admitAnonymousSubmission, so nothing is left behind here; the
        // response carries no count, limit or window, only the throttle flag
        // the POST operation answers as HTTP 429.
        if (!this._admitAnonymousSubmission(savedGr, newSysId).allowed) {
            return {
                error: 'Too many submissions were received in a short period. Please try again in a minute.',
                throttled: true
            };
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // ROUND-TRIP VERIFICATION - the value stored must equal the value
        // submitted, or the submission is refused and the row removed.
        //
        // _validateSubmission() refuses anything longer than the declared
        // limit, counted in the units JavaScript counts (str.length, i.e.
        // UTF-16 code units). That is necessary and it is not sufficient,
        // because the column's real capacity is not expressed in those
        // units. Measured on this instance against x_casemgmt_case.subject,
        // declared String(255):
        //     255 ASCII characters                  -> stored 255, exact
        //     one emoji + 253 ASCII (255 units)     -> stored 245 units,
        //                                              ten characters of
        //                                              the tail silently
        //                                              gone
        //     one emoji + 243 ASCII                 -> exact
        // The boundary moves with the number of astral characters present
        // and does not correspond to characters, UTF-16 units or UTF-8
        // bytes in any way that survives being written down as a formula -
        // it is an artefact of how the platform encodes the value on its
        // way to a VARCHAR-backed column. Short values containing the same
        // characters round-trip perfectly, so this is a capacity boundary
        // and not character mangling.
        //
        // Rather than re-derive that boundary and hardcode a formula that a
        // platform upgrade or a different column type would quietly
        // invalidate, this check asks the only question that actually
        // matters and asks it of the platform itself: is what you stored
        // what I gave you? That is exact by construction, needs no model of
        // the encoding, and cannot drift.
        //
        // It costs nothing extra: savedGr is the re-query this method
        // already performs to read the auto-generated number.
        //
        // On mismatch the row is DELETED. A partial case is worse than no
        // case on an anonymous intake path - the requester would be handed
        // a case number for a case whose material content had been
        // shortened, with no way to know, which is the whole defect this
        // check exists to prevent. Deleting and refusing gives them an
        // actionable error and one edit. The case number is consumed either
        // way; the platform allocates numbers on form load as well, so
        // gaps in the CASE sequence are already expected and carry no
        // meaning.
        //
        // Only the four bounded string columns are compared. status is
        // forced by this method, number and the audit columns are the
        // platform's, and type is a choice value resolved against the live
        // choice list before it is written.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var ROUND_TRIP_FIELDS = [
            { name: 'subject',         label: 'Subject' },
            { name: 'description',     label: 'Description' },
            { name: 'requester_name',  label: 'Your name' },
            { name: 'requester_email', label: 'Email' }
        ];
        var mismatches = {};
        var mismatchCount = 0;
        for (var r = 0; r < ROUND_TRIP_FIELDS.length; r++) {
            var rtField = ROUND_TRIP_FIELDS[r];
            if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(validated.values, rtField.name)) {
                continue;
            }
            var submittedValue = String(validated.values[rtField.name]);
            var storedValue = String(savedGr.getValue(rtField.name) || '');
            if (storedValue === submittedValue) {
                continue;
            }
            mismatchCount++;
            // The message quotes both lengths so the caller can act without
            // bisecting the payload, and describes the effect rather than
            // the platform mechanism, which is not the caller's problem.
            // Both numbers describe the caller's own input.
            mismatches[rtField.name] = rtField.label + ' could not be stored exactly as submitted' +
                ' (sent ' + submittedValue.length + ' characters, stored ' + storedValue.length +
                '). Please shorten it and submit again.';
        }

        if (mismatchCount > 0) {
            // Remove the row before returning, so a refused submission
            // leaves nothing behind. deleteRecord() is checked: if the
            // delete itself fails the row would survive as a partial case,
            // which must be logged loudly rather than passed over.
            var cleanupGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
            if (cleanupGr.get(newSysId) && !cleanupGr.deleteRecord()) {
                gs.error('CasePortalService.submitCase: stored value did not match the submitted ' +
                    'value AND the cleanup delete failed for sys_id=' + newSysId +
                    '; a partial case row has been left behind and needs manual removal.');
            } else {
                gs.warn('CasePortalService.submitCase: refused a submission because ' +
                    mismatchCount + ' field(s) did not round-trip exactly; the partial row was ' +
                    'removed. Fields: ' + Object.keys(mismatches).join(', ') + '.');
            }
            return {
                error: 'The submission could not be accepted because one or more fields are invalid.',
                fields: mismatches
            };
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // DOUBLE-SUBMIT COLLAPSE. Two identical anonymous submissions in
        // quick succession are one intake, not two, and this endpoint had
        // no defence against them: QA released two barrier-synchronised
        // POSTs carrying the same body and both were accepted, persisting
        // CASE0000226 and CASE0000227. The flood guard above does not help
        // - ten submissions a minute is exactly what it permits - and the
        // widget's in-flight button lock only covers the single page, not
        // the public API.
        //
        // The collapse runs HERE, after the insert, deliberately. See
        // _collapseDuplicateSubmission for why a post-insert reconcile is
        // the only variant that also settles genuinely simultaneous
        // callers, and for the two honest limits on the guarantee.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var winningNumber = this._collapseDuplicateSubmission(savedGr, validated.values, newSysId);
        if (winningNumber !== null) {
            return { number: winningNumber };
        }

        // Return ONLY the auto-generated number - no other fields, no
        // sys_id, no audit fields. The portal confirmation widget
        // (../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml)
        // displays this number to the requester so they can later look up
        // their case via the status page.
        return { number: String(savedGr.getValue('number')) };
    },

    /**
     * Collapse an identical anonymous submission received inside a short
     * window onto the single case that survives it.
     *
     * WHAT IT GUARANTEES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Stated first, because the
     * value of a de-duplication contract is entirely in its edges:
     *
     *   IT DOES collapse a retry - a requester who presses Submit twice,
     *   a client that repeats a POST after a timeout, a script that loops
     *   - onto the FIRST case, and answers the later caller with that
     *   first case's number, so both callers are told the same truth and
     *   exactly one row survives.
     *
     *   IT DOES collapse two genuinely simultaneous callers, provided
     *   each one's query can see the other's row. Both compute the SAME
     *   winner, because the winner is defined by a total order over the
     *   candidate rows (sys_created_on, then sys_id) rather than by
     *   "whoever noticed first"; the loser removes its own row.
     *
     *   IT DOES NOT collapse two callers whose inserts are both still
     *   invisible to each other's query. Each then sees only its own row,
     *   each declares itself the winner, and TWO cases survive. This is a
     *   real residual window, it is a property of reconciling after the
     *   fact rather than of this implementation, and closing it would
     *   need a uniqueness constraint or a mutex - neither of which exists
     *   for this table, and adding a table, a field or an endpoint to
     *   carry one is refused by the AAP Section 0.7.2 Minimal-Change
     *   Clause. So the guarantee is "duplicates are collapsed, not
     *   prevented", and that is the honest wording.
     *
     *   IT DOES NOT reclaim the case number the discarded row consumed.
     *   The platform allocates a number during the insert, so a collapsed
     *   duplicate leaves a GAP in the CASE sequence. That is already true
     *   of this method's round-trip refusal and of every form load, so
     *   gaps carry no meaning here, but they are visible and a reader
     *   comparing counts should expect them.
     *
     * WHY POST-INSERT RATHER THAN PRE-INSERT. A pre-insert "has an
     * identical case just arrived?" check reads a window in which a
     * simultaneous sibling has not yet written anything, so two callers
     * both see nothing and both insert - it collapses retries only. By
     * inserting first and reconciling after, each caller has already
     * published its candidate before it looks, which is what lets two
     * simultaneous callers converge on one winner. The pattern is not new
     * to this file: the round-trip verification above inserts, asks the
     * platform what it actually stored, and deletes the row when the
     * answer is wrong. This is the same shape with a different question.
     *
     * WHY 90 SECONDS. The window has to be longer than the interval a
     * human or a client will re-press within, and short enough that a
     * requester who deliberately submits the same case again later is not
     * silently refused a second case. Measured behaviour bounds both
     * ends: the submission widget has no client-side timeout at all (see
     * the lookup widget's LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS comment for why the write
     * deliberately differs from the read), so a retry follows a stalled
     * request by whatever the requester's patience is - tens of seconds -
     * while the endpoint's own flood guard already thinks in a 60-second
     * window. 90 seconds sits just above that flood window, so the two
     * mechanisms describe overlapping periods rather than contradicting
     * ones, and well below the minutes it takes to retype a case by hand.
     *
     * THE FINGERPRINT is the five whitelisted values, and nothing else.
     * Two submissions are "identical" when subject, type, description,
     * requester_name and requester_email all match, the row is still in
     * Draft, and it was created by the same caller as ours. status is in
     * the fingerprint because a case that has already been worked -
     * advanced out of Draft by an agent - must never be handed back to an
     * anonymous caller as the answer to a new submission. The creator is
     * read off our own row rather than assumed to be 'guest', so this is
     * correct for whatever user the platform runs an unauthenticated call
     * as, and it keeps an internal user's identically-worded case from
     * ever being returned to the public endpoint.
     *
     * `description` is compared IN SCRIPT rather than in the query. It is
     * declared 4000 characters, so the platform backs it with a TEXT
     * column, and an equality predicate on a TEXT column is the one part
     * of this query that is neither reliably indexed nor portable across
     * the databases the platform runs on. The four narrow columns do the
     * selecting; the wide one does the confirming, on the handful of rows
     * that survive.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_id (AAP Section 0.7.2): the only identifier used
     * is the one insert() returned, passed in. No gs.eventQueue and no
     * notification of any kind (email is disabled per Section 0.7.2). No
     * new table, field or endpoint (Minimal-Change Clause).
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} savedGr - the post-insert re-query of our own
     *     row, already positioned on it.
     * @param {Object} values - the validated whitelisted values that were
     *     written.
     * @param {String} newSysId - the sys_id returned by insert().
     * @return {String|null} the surviving case's number when OUR row was
     *     the duplicate and has been removed, or null when our row is the
     *     one that survives (the caller then returns its own number).
     */
    _collapseDuplicateSubmission: function(savedGr, values, newSysId) {
        var DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS = 90;

        var ourNumber = String(savedGr.getValue('number') || '');
        var creator = String(savedGr.getValue('sys_created_by') || '');
        if (creator === '') {
            // Without a creator there is no safe way to scope the search to
            // this endpoint's own rows, and widening it to every Draft case
            // could hand an anonymous caller a case somebody else created.
            // Fail open: keep our row.
            gs.warn('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: sys_created_by was empty on ' +
                'sys_id=' + newSysId + '; the duplicate check was skipped for this submission.');
            return null;
        }

        if (String(savedGr.getValue('status') || '') !== 'Draft') {
            // Our own row must satisfy the same fingerprint the candidates
            // are selected by, or the winner could be a row that is
            // "identical" to what we submitted while OUR row holds
            // something else - and we would delete the row the requester
            // actually created. submitCase() forces status='Draft' before
            // the insert, so reaching here means something moved it
            // afterwards; that is a state this method has no basis to
            // reconcile, so it declines and keeps our row.
            gs.warn('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: sys_id=' + newSysId +
                ' is no longer in Draft immediately after insert (status=' +
                String(savedGr.getValue('status') || '') + '); the duplicate check was skipped.');
            return null;
        }

        var windowStart = new GlideDateTime();
        windowStart.addSeconds(-DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS);

        var ourDescription = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(values, 'description') ?
            String(values.description) : '';

        var candidates = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        candidates.addQuery('status', 'Draft');
        candidates.addQuery('sys_created_by', creator);
        candidates.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', windowStart);
        candidates.addQuery('subject', this._fingerprintValue(values, 'subject'));
        candidates.addQuery('type', this._fingerprintValue(values, 'type'));
        candidates.addQuery('requester_name', this._fingerprintValue(values, 'requester_name'));
        candidates.addQuery('requester_email', this._fingerprintValue(values, 'requester_email'));
        // The order is the whole mechanism: every caller evaluating this
        // same candidate set picks the same first row. sys_created_on has
        // one-second resolution, so two simultaneous inserts routinely
        // share it - sys_id breaks that tie deterministically, since every
        // caller compares the same 32-character strings.
        candidates.orderBy('sys_created_on');
        candidates.orderBy('sys_id');
        candidates.query();

        var winnerSysId = '';
        var winnerNumber = '';
        while (candidates.next()) {
            if (String(candidates.getValue('description') || '') !== ourDescription) {
                continue;
            }
            winnerSysId = String(candidates.getValue('sys_id') || '');
            winnerNumber = String(candidates.getValue('number') || '');
            break;
        }

        if (winnerSysId === '' || winnerSysId === newSysId) {
            // Either nothing matched (our own row should always match, so
            // this means the query could not see it yet) or we ARE the
            // winner. Both keep our row and return its own number.
            return null;
        }

        if (winnerNumber === '') {
            // A surviving row with no case number is nothing to hand a
            // requester, and deleting ours in favour of it would lose the
            // only number we can quote. Keep ours and say why.
            gs.warn('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: an earlier identical Draft case ' +
                'sys_id=' + winnerSysId + ' carries no case number, so submission sys_id=' + newSysId +
                ' was kept as a separate case rather than collapsed onto it.');
            return null;
        }

        // We are the duplicate. Remove our row and answer with the case
        // that survives. deleteRecord() is checked for the same reason the
        // round-trip cleanup checks it: a failed delete leaves two rows,
        // and the caller must then be told about the row that actually
        // exists under its own number rather than about a row we failed to
        // remove.
        var duplicateGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        if (!duplicateGr.get(newSysId)) {
            gs.warn('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: the duplicate row sys_id=' +
                newSysId + ' could no longer be read for removal; answering with the surviving case.');
            return winnerNumber;
        }
        if (!duplicateGr.deleteRecord()) {
            gs.error('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: submission sys_id=' + newSysId +
                ' duplicates case sys_id=' + winnerSysId + ' but the duplicate could NOT be deleted' +
                ' (lastErrorMessage=' + duplicateGr.getLastErrorMessage() + '); both rows now exist' +
                ' and the duplicate needs manual removal.');
            return null;
        }

        gs.info('CasePortalService._collapseDuplicateSubmission: collapsed an identical anonymous ' +
            'submission received inside ' + DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS + 's onto the surviving case; the ' +
            'duplicate row (number ' + ourNumber + ') was removed and the caller was answered with the ' +
            'earlier case number. The removed row consumed a case number, so the CASE sequence has a gap.');
        return winnerNumber;
    },

    /**
     * One whitelisted value, in the exact form it was written to the row,
     * for use as a query term in the duplicate fingerprint.
     *
     * A field absent from `values` was never written, so the stored column
     * holds the empty string and the query term must be '' - not null,
     * which GlideRecord would treat as an unset condition and silently
     * widen the search with.
     *
     * @param {Object} values - the validated whitelisted values.
     * @param {String} name - the field name.
     * @return {String} the value written, or '' when the field was absent.
     */
    _fingerprintValue: function(values, name) {
        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(values, name)) {
            return '';
        }
        return String(values[name]);
    },

    /**
     * Anonymous case status lookup entry point.
     *
     * Whitelist-only field return per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *   - Looks up by case number (CASE0000001 style; the public-facing
     *     identifier returned by submitCase).
     *   - Returns ONLY: status, subject, opened_date. opened_date is the
     *     DISPLAY value (session timezone and date format), so the instant
     *     an external requester reads matches the instant internal staff
     *     read on the case form; see the block comment at the return
     *     statement for the measurement that made this necessary.
     *   - NEVER returns: assigned_group, assigned_agent, description,
     *     closed_date, requester_name, requester_email, priority, type,
     *     pending_reason, sys_id, sys_created_by, sys_created_on,
     *     sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, or any other field. The
     *     three-field whitelist is the privacy perimeter for anonymous
     *     lookups - returning the full record would expose internal
     *     assignment data and PII that the requester themselves
     *     supplied at submission time.
     *   - Returns null when no case matches, when the supplied value is
     *     not a well-formed case number, and when no value was supplied at
     *     all - the three are ONE outcome here, so nothing in this method
     *     tells a caller which of them happened. The calling scripted REST
     *     endpoint translates null into the HTTP 404 not-found response
     *     whose verbatim body is specified in AAP Section 0.7.4. The
     *     user-facing not-found message is INTENTIONALLY absent from this
     *     Script Include's runtime path - it is the REST endpoint's
     *     responsibility to surface that message.
     *   - Returns { throttled: true } when this session has exceeded the
     *     per-session request ceiling for the trailing window. The REST
     *     operation answers that with HTTP 429, mirroring the submit
     *     endpoint. This is the THIRD return case and the only one that is
     *     neither a hit nor a miss.
     *
     * ENUMERATION EXPOSURE, STATED PLAINLY (review finding F07). The
     * contract AAP Section 0.7.4 fixes is a SINGLE-FACTOR lookup: a case
     * number, on its own, returns that case's status, subject and opened
     * date to an unauthenticated caller. Case numbers are sequential
     * (CASE0000001 upward, per ../numbers/sys_number_x_casemgmt_case.xml),
     * so "200 for a real number, 404 for an unused one" is inherently a
     * hit/miss oracle: a script that walks the sequence learns which
     * numbers exist and reads three fields of each. That is a property of
     * the mandated contract, NOT of this implementation, and it cannot be
     * removed without a second factor the AAP does not define and the
     * Section 0.7.2 Minimal-Change Clause forbids inventing.
     *
     * What this method therefore does is RAISE THE COST and MAKE THE SWEEP
     * VISIBLE, rather than claim the oracle away:
     *
     *   1. STRICT FORMAT VALIDATION BEFORE ANY QUERY. The value is trimmed,
     *      upper-cased and matched against ^CASE[0-9]{7}$. Anything else
     *      returns the not-found result WITHOUT touching the database, so a
     *      malformed sweep costs the instance nothing and gains the caller
     *      nothing - and the response is identical to a genuine miss, so
     *      the shape of the accepted input is not disclosed either.
     *   2. PER-SESSION SLIDING-WINDOW THROTTLE. Requests are counted in the
     *      session's own client-data store (no new table, field or
     *      property - Section 0.7.2), pruned to the window on every call.
     *      Beyond the ceiling the answer is { throttled: true } / HTTP 429.
     *   3. ABUSE MONITORING. Crossing the soft miss threshold, or being
     *      throttled, emits a gs.warn under a STABLE MARKER prefix carrying
     *      the client IP and the miss/total counts, so an operator can
     *      alert on the prefix alone and see a sweep in progress.
     *   4. A PLATFORM-NATIVE PER-HOUR CEILING on the guest user for this
     *      resource ships beside the endpoint
     *      (../portal/rest/sys_rate_limit_rules_x_casemgmt_case_status_lookup.xml),
     *      as defence in depth behind the in-script controls.
     *
     * RESIDUAL RISK, NOT DENIED: a distributed caller that discards its
     * session cookie between requests gets a fresh session each time and so
     * a fresh window, which is what the native per-hour rule on the guest
     * user exists to bound; and a caller inside the ceiling can still walk
     * the sequence slowly. The three fields exposed are the three the AAP
     * mandates, and they are the whole of the exposure. This is recorded in
     * ../docs/portal-pages.md rather than described as closed.
     *
     * Robust input handling: gracefully handles empty strings,
     * whitespace-only strings, non-string inputs and lower-case input
     * without throwing.
     *
     * @param {String} number - case number (e.g., 'CASE0000001'). Trimmed
     *     and upper-cased, then required to match ^CASE[0-9]{7}$.
     * @return {Object|null} { status, subject, opened_date } when a case
     *     with the given number is found; { throttled: true } when this
     *     session is over its request ceiling; or null when no case matches
     *     (including when the number argument is null, undefined, empty,
     *     non-string, whitespace-only or not a well-formed case number).
     */
    lookupCase: function(number) {
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 1. PER-SESSION THROTTLE, EVALUATED FIRST so that EVERY request is
        //    counted - including the ones that will be refused for their
        //    format and the ones that carry no value at all. A sweep that
        //    varies its input must not be able to buy free attempts by
        //    sending values this method rejects early.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        if (!this._admitAnonymousLookup().allowed) {
            // The third return case. Deliberately carries no counts, no
            // ceiling and no window: the REST operation turns the flag into
            // HTTP 429 and its own hardcoded message.
            return { throttled: true };
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 2. NORMALISE, THEN VALIDATE STRICTLY - BEFORE ANY QUERY.
        //
        //    The scripted REST endpoint passes through whatever the caller
        //    supplied as the 'number' query parameter: a missing parameter
        //    yields undefined, an empty one yields '', and the platform may
        //    coerce a numeric-looking value into a Number. All of those, and
        //    anything that is not shaped like a case number, produce the
        //    SAME not-found result as a genuine miss and issue NO query.
        //
        //    Two reasons the check lives here rather than in the query:
        //      - Cost. A malformed sweep is answered from memory, so it
        //        cannot be used to make the database do work.
        //      - Disclosure. A distinct "malformed input" answer would tell
        //        an anonymous caller the accepted shape of the identifier.
        //        One answer for both keeps that to what the widget source
        //        already shows.
        //
        //    The pattern is the auto-number format from
        //    ../numbers/sys_number_x_casemgmt_case.xml: the CASE prefix and
        //    exactly seven digits. Upper-casing first accepts a requester
        //    who types their number in lower case, which is a usability
        //    concession and not a widening: the stored values are upper case.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var candidate = (number === null || number === undefined) ? '' : String(number).trim().toUpperCase();
        if (!/^CASE[0-9]{7}$/.test(candidate)) {
            this._recordAnonymousLookupMiss();
            return null;
        }

        var caseGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        // Query by the public-facing 'number' field, NOT by sys_id. The
        // case number is the stable human-readable identifier shown to
        // the requester on the submission confirmation; it is the only
        // identifier the requester ever sees, so it is the only key the
        // lookup endpoint accepts. This compliance with the AAP Section
        // 0.7.2 no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint is also a privacy win:
        // anonymous callers cannot probe the system by guessing
        // 32-character hex sys_id values.
        caseGr.addQuery('number', candidate);
        // setLimit(1) is a defensive optimization - the case number is
        // a unique field per the auto-numbering generator, so at most
        // one row can match. Setting the limit eliminates any potential
        // for a misconfiguration to return multiple rows and tells the
        // database engine to stop after the first hit.
        caseGr.setLimit(1);
        caseGr.query();

        if (!caseGr.next()) {
            // A well-formed number that matched nothing. This is the miss
            // the abuse monitor counts: a sweep of the sequential number
            // space produces a run of them from one session, which is what
            // the soft threshold in _recordAnonymousLookupMiss detects and
            // reports. Counting it changes nothing the caller can observe -
            // the response below is identical either way.
            this._recordAnonymousLookupMiss();
            // No case with the given number was found. Return null; the
            // caller (the scripted REST operation script) translates
            // null into the HTTP 404 response whose verbatim body is
            // specified in AAP Section 0.7.4. We deliberately do NOT
            // include that verbatim text in this Script Include - the
            // REST endpoint owns the user-facing message, and embedding
            // the literal here would create a maintenance hazard if the
            // message ever needed to be reworded (which would then
            // require a schema/Update-Set re-export rather than just a
            // REST endpoint update).
            return null;
        }

        // Whitelisted output fields per AAP Section 0.7.4. EXACTLY three
        // fields are exposed to anonymous lookup callers:
        //
        //   - status: lets the requester see if their case is still
        //     Draft, has progressed to Open / In Progress / Pending /
        //     Resolved, or has been Closed.
        //   - subject: lets the requester confirm they're looking up the
        //     correct case (the requester chose this string at
        //     submission time, so echoing it back confirms identity
        //     without exposing other-party content).
        //   - opened_date: lets the requester compute how long the case
        //     has been open. Note: opened_date is auto-set on insert
        //     by the before-insert business rule
        //     ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_opened_date.xml.
        //
        // The String() coercion normalizes the GlideElement primitive
        // values into plain strings (so JSON.stringify on the result
        // produces clean JSON without any GlideElement object metadata).
        // The `|| ''` defaults handle the rare edge case where a column
        // is unexpectedly null-valued at runtime (e.g., a partially-
        // initialized seed-data row); empty strings are safer than null
        // in JSON responses to widget code that may not handle null
        // gracefully.
        //
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // opened_date IS EMITTED AS THE DISPLAY VALUE, NOT THE RAW COLUMN
        // VALUE.
        //
        // A GlideDateTime column is stored in UTC and getValue() returns
        // exactly those stored characters. getDisplayValue() renders the
        // same instant in the session's timezone and date format - which is
        // what every internal surface (the case form, the case list, the
        // reports) shows. Reading the column with getValue() therefore made
        // this endpoint the ONLY surface in the application quoting UTC:
        // measured on CASE9000003, /api/now/table/x_casemgmt_case with
        // sysparm_display_value=false returned '2026-09-03 17:39:40', with
        // sysparm_display_value=true returned '2026-09-03 10:39:40', and
        // this endpoint returned the 17:39:40 form while the internal form
        // showed 10:39:40 - a seven-hour discrepancy on one record, because
        // the instance default timezone resolves to US/Pacific and neither
        // the admin nor the guest user carries a personal timezone.
        //
        // An external requester reading 17:39:40 concludes their case was
        // opened seven hours in the future relative to what the staff
        // handling it can see, and there is no way for them to reconcile the
        // two. AAP Section 0.7.3 Gate 5 requires the CORRECT opened_date be
        // returned for a valid case number, so the display value is the
        // correct emission and the raw value is not.
        //
        // The RESPONSE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED: exactly three keys - status,
        // subject, opened_date - per AAP Section 0.7.4's whitelist. The
        // timezone that qualifies the instant is surfaced as a LABEL on the
        // lookup panel by
        //   ../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget.xml
        // (which reads it from its own widget data, not from this response),
        // deliberately NOT as a fourth key here: adding one would widen a
        // whitelist the AAP fixes at three fields.
        //
        // getDisplayValue() is called on the GlideElement (caseGr.opened_date)
        // rather than on the GlideRecord, because the no-argument
        // GlideRecord.getDisplayValue() returns the record's DISPLAY FIELD
        // (the case number), not this column.
        //
        // The fallback below covers only the abnormal case where the element
        // is unavailable or renders empty while the column holds data - a
        // partially-initialized row or a platform-level formatting failure.
        // It cannot reintroduce the UTC value for a normal populated row,
        // because getDisplayValue() on a populated GlideDateTime always
        // renders; and when opened_date is genuinely empty both calls yield
        // '' so the emitted value is '' either way (the empty opened_date
        // seen on some seeded rows is a separate, upstream seed-data
        // concern, not a formatting one).
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var openedDateDisplay = '';
        var openedDateElement = caseGr.opened_date;
        if (openedDateElement) {
            openedDateDisplay = String(openedDateElement.getDisplayValue() || '');
        }
        if (openedDateDisplay === '') {
            openedDateDisplay = String(caseGr.getValue('opened_date') || '');
        }

        return {
            status:      String(caseGr.getValue('status') || ''),
            subject:     String(caseGr.getValue('subject') || ''),
            opened_date: openedDateDisplay
        };
    },

    /**
     * The one place the anonymous-lookup guard's tuning lives.
     *
     * Kept in a single method rather than duplicated across the three
     * methods that need it, so the window used to PRUNE the stored
     * timestamps can never drift from the window used to JUDGE them - a
     * drift that would silently widen or narrow the ceiling.
     *
     * key                 the single GlideSession client-data key the guard
     *                     stores its compact JSON under. One key, so the
     *                     guard adds no storage anywhere else (AAP Section
     *                     0.7.2 Minimal-Change Clause: no new table, field
     *                     or property).
     * marker              the STABLE log-marker prefix an operator alerts
     *                     on. Changing it breaks existing alerts, so it is
     *                     treated as a published interface and is recorded
     *                     in ../docs/portal-pages.md.
     * windowSeconds       the sliding window, in seconds.
     * requestLimit        requests allowed per session per window. Sized
     *                     well above real use of the lookup page - a
     *                     requester checking one case makes one request,
     *                     the confirmation link's prefill makes one, and a
     *                     retry after a mistyped number makes another - and
     *                     far below the rate a sweep needs to be useful.
     * missThreshold       misses per session per window that trip the soft
     *                     abuse warning. A requester mistyping their own
     *                     number a few times stays under it; walking the
     *                     number space does not.
     * logIntervalSeconds  minimum spacing between warnings from ONE
     *                     session, so a sustained flood cannot turn the
     *                     monitor into a log-flood amplifier.
     * maxEntries          hard cap on stored timestamps per list. Only the
     *                     most recent entries can change a decision, and an
     *                     uncapped list would let a caller grow its own
     *                     session record without limit.
     *
     * @return {Object} the guard's settings.
     */
    _lookupGuardSettings: function() {
        return {
            key: 'x_casemgmt_portal_lookup_guard',
            marker: 'X_CASEMGMT_PORTAL_LOOKUP_ABUSE|',
            windowSeconds: 60,
            requestLimit: 12,
            missThreshold: 5,
            logIntervalSeconds: 60,
            maxEntries: 64
        };
    },

    /**
     * Read this session's lookup-guard state and prune it to the window.
     *
     * The state is a compact JSON document under ONE client-data key:
     *     { "t": [<request epoch ms>...],
     *       "m": [<miss epoch ms>...],
     *       "w": <epoch ms of the last warning emitted for this session> }
     * Timestamps outside the window are dropped on every call, which is
     * what makes the window slide without a scheduled job.
     *
     * The session store is used because it is the only per-caller state the
     * platform offers this path without adding an artifact the AAP does not
     * define. It is in-memory and per-session, so it is cheap, it expires
     * with the session, and it stores NO PII - only integers.
     *
     * FAILS OPEN, AND SILENTLY, BY DESIGN. When there is no session, or the
     * client-data store cannot be read, this returns null and the caller
     * admits the request. Refusing instead would take the public lookup
     * page down on a platform condition the requester cannot influence.
     * The branch deliberately does NOT log: it is reachable on every
     * request if it is reachable at all, so logging it would hand an
     * attacker a log-flood amplifier. The condition is documented as a
     * residual risk in ../docs/portal-pages.md and is covered by the native
     * per-hour rate-limit rule on the guest user instead.
     *
     * A stored value that is not the JSON this guard wrote - truncated,
     * replaced, or from an older shape - is treated as ABSENT rather than
     * trusted, so a corrupt value costs one window of throttling and never
     * an exception on the public path.
     *
     * @param {Object} settings - the object returned by
     *     _lookupGuardSettings().
     * @return {Object|null} { t: Array, m: Array, w: Number,
     *     session: GlideSession } pruned to the window, or null when no
     *     session state is available.
     */
    _readLookupGuardState: function(settings) {
        var session = null;
        try {
            session = gs.getSession();
        } catch (sessionError) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!session) {
            return null;
        }

        var raw = '';
        try {
            raw = String(session.getClientData(settings.key) || '');
        } catch (readError) {
            raw = '';
        }

        var requests = [];
        var misses = [];
        var lastWarned = 0;
        if (raw !== '') {
            try {
                var parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
                if (parsed && typeof parsed === 'object') {
                    requests = parsed.t;
                    misses = parsed.m;
                    var parsedWarned = Number(parsed.w);
                    if (!isNaN(parsedWarned) && isFinite(parsedWarned)) {
                        lastWarned = parsedWarned;
                    }
                }
            } catch (parseError) {
                requests = [];
                misses = [];
                lastWarned = 0;
            }
        }

        var cutoff = new GlideDateTime().getNumericValue() - (settings.windowSeconds * 1000);
        return {
            t: this._pruneGuardTimestamps(requests, cutoff, settings.maxEntries),
            m: this._pruneGuardTimestamps(misses, cutoff, settings.maxEntries),
            w: lastWarned,
            session: session
        };
    },

    /**
     * Keep only the timestamps inside the window, and only the most recent
     * maxEntries of them.
     *
     * Every entry is coerced and checked, because the input is whatever was
     * parsed out of the session store: a non-array, a sparse array, strings,
     * nulls and NaN are all possible and none of them may reach the
     * arithmetic that follows.
     *
     * @param {Array} value - the raw parsed list (may be any type).
     * @param {Number} cutoff - epoch ms; entries older than this are
     *     dropped.
     * @param {Number} maxEntries - hard cap on the returned length.
     * @return {Array} a clean array of numeric timestamps.
     */
    _pruneGuardTimestamps: function(value, cutoff, maxEntries) {
        var kept = [];
        if (!value || !Array.isArray(value)) {
            return kept;
        }
        for (var i = 0; i < value.length; i++) {
            var entry = Number(value[i]);
            if (!isNaN(entry) && isFinite(entry) && entry >= cutoff) {
                kept.push(entry);
            }
        }
        if (kept.length > maxEntries) {
            kept = kept.slice(kept.length - maxEntries);
        }
        return kept;
    },

    /**
     * Persist the pruned lookup-guard state back onto the session.
     *
     * A write failure is not fatal and is not logged, for the same reason
     * the read failure is not: it would be reachable on every request and
     * would amplify a flood into the log. The consequence of a failed write
     * is that this request is not counted, which the native per-hour
     * rate-limit rule bounds.
     *
     * @param {Object} settings - the object returned by
     *     _lookupGuardSettings().
     * @param {Object} state - the state object from
     *     _readLookupGuardState().
     * @return {Boolean} true when the state was stored.
     */
    _writeLookupGuardState: function(settings, state) {
        try {
            state.session.putClientData(settings.key, JSON.stringify({
                t: state.t,
                m: state.m,
                w: state.w
            }));
            return true;
        } catch (writeError) {
            return false;
        }
    },

    /**
     * Admission control for one anonymous lookup request.
     *
     * Counts THIS request in the session's sliding window and answers
     * whether it may proceed. Refused requests are counted too: a caller
     * that keeps hammering keeps its own window full and has to go quiet
     * for a whole window to recover, which is the point of a throttle.
     *
     * Crossing the ceiling emits ONE warning per logIntervalSeconds per
     * session under the stable marker, carrying the client IP and the
     * miss/total counts so an operator can see a sweep and its source. The
     * IP comes from GlideSession.getClientIP(); it is abuse telemetry about
     * an unauthenticated caller and is not requester data - no submitted
     * field value, name or address is ever logged (AAP Section 0.7.2
     * no-PII).
     *
     * WHAT THIS GUARD IS AND IS NOT. The window lives in the session's
     * client-data store, which this method READS, appends to and WRITES
     * BACK - three steps with no lock around them. Two requests of the same
     * session that interleave inside those steps can both read the same
     * array, and the later write then drops the earlier increment, so a
     * caller issuing its lookups in parallel can get more of them through
     * than the ceiling names. A caller that discards its session cookie is
     * not slowed at all, because the next request arrives with a fresh
     * session and therefore an empty window (recorded on lookupCase under
     * ENUMERATION EXPOSURE).
     *
     * This guard is therefore defence-in-depth against a naive sequential
     * sweep, plus the telemetry an operator needs - it is NOT the
     * enumeration perimeter. The perimeter is the platform-native per-hour
     * ceiling shipped beside this endpoint
     * (../portal/rest/sys_rate_limit_rules_x_casemgmt_case_status_lookup.xml),
     * whose binding to a scoped resource for an unauthenticated caller is
     * unverified on this release and is recorded as a capability gap in
     * ../docs/PDI_LIMITATIONS_AND_KNOWN_ISSUES.md, together with the
     * miss-threshold warning below. Closing either hole inside this file
     * would need an atomic counter in a new table or system property, or a
     * control at the edge in front of the instance: AAP Section 0.7.2's
     * Minimal-Change Clause refuses the first and a PDI does not offer the
     * second, so the residue is reported rather than worked around.
     *
     * @return {Object} { allowed: Boolean } - and nothing else, so no
     *     count, ceiling or window can escape into a response.
     */
    _admitAnonymousLookup: function() {
        var settings = this._lookupGuardSettings();
        var state = this._readLookupGuardState(settings);
        if (state === null) {
            return { allowed: true };
        }

        var nowMs = new GlideDateTime().getNumericValue();
        state.t.push(nowMs);
        var requests = state.t.length;
        var allowed = requests <= settings.requestLimit;

        if (!allowed && (nowMs - state.w) >= (settings.logIntervalSeconds * 1000)) {
            state.w = nowMs;
            gs.warn(settings.marker + 'event=throttled ip=' + this._clientIpForLog() +
                ' requests=' + requests + ' misses=' + state.m.length +
                ' request_limit=' + settings.requestLimit +
                ' window_seconds=' + settings.windowSeconds);
        }

        this._writeLookupGuardState(settings, state);
        return { allowed: allowed };
    },

    /**
     * Record one anonymous lookup that returned nothing - a malformed
     * value, an absent value, or a well-formed number that matched no case.
     *
     * A run of misses from a single session is the signature of a sweep of
     * the sequential number space, and it is the only signal available on
     * an endpoint whose mandated contract makes hit-versus-miss inherently
     * observable (see the ENUMERATION EXPOSURE note on lookupCase). Once
     * the soft threshold is crossed the guard emits ONE warning per
     * logIntervalSeconds per session under the stable marker, carrying the
     * client IP and both counts, so an admin can alert on the prefix and
     * act - block the address at the edge, or tighten the shipped
     * sys_rate_limit_rules ceiling.
     *
     * Recording a miss changes NOTHING a caller can observe: the response
     * that follows is byte-identical whether or not this method ran, so the
     * monitor itself introduces no new oracle.
     *
     * @return {undefined} nothing; monitoring never alters the answer.
     */
    _recordAnonymousLookupMiss: function() {
        var settings = this._lookupGuardSettings();
        var state = this._readLookupGuardState(settings);
        if (state === null) {
            return;
        }

        var nowMs = new GlideDateTime().getNumericValue();
        state.m.push(nowMs);
        var misses = state.m.length;

        if (misses >= settings.missThreshold && (nowMs - state.w) >= (settings.logIntervalSeconds * 1000)) {
            state.w = nowMs;
            gs.warn(settings.marker + 'event=miss_threshold ip=' + this._clientIpForLog() +
                ' misses=' + misses + ' requests=' + state.t.length +
                ' miss_threshold=' + settings.missThreshold +
                ' window_seconds=' + settings.windowSeconds);
        }

        this._writeLookupGuardState(settings, state);
    },

    /**
     * The calling client's IP address, in a form that is always safe to
     * concatenate into a log line.
     *
     * Returns the literal 'unavailable' rather than an empty string when
     * the platform cannot supply an address, so a log line always has a
     * value in the ip= field and an alert parsing those lines never has to
     * handle a missing token.
     *
     * @return {String} the client IP, or 'unavailable'.
     */
    _clientIpForLog: function() {
        var ip = '';
        try {
            var session = gs.getSession();
            if (session) {
                ip = String(session.getClientIP() || '');
            }
        } catch (ipError) {
            ip = '';
        }
        return ip === '' ? 'unavailable' : ip;
    },

    /**
     * Validate an anonymous submission payload against the AAP Section 0.5.7
     * constraints for the five whitelisted input fields, returning the
     * cleaned values to write.
     *
     * Contract per field:
     *   subject         MANDATORY. Rejected when absent, null or
     *                   whitespace-only. Trimmed, then REJECTED when it
     *                   exceeds 255 characters (the declared String(255)
     *                   length) - never truncated to fit.
     *   description     MANDATORY. Rejected when absent, null or
     *                   whitespace-only. Trimmed, then REJECTED when it
     *                   exceeds 4000 characters. The check MUST live here:
     *                   the platform stores >255-character string columns
     *                   in a TEXT column that does not truncate, so the
     *                   database alone does not enforce the declared limit.
     *   requester_name  MANDATORY. Rejected when absent, null or
     *                   whitespace-only. Trimmed, then REJECTED above 100
     *                   characters.
     *   requester_email OPTIONAL (AAP Section 0.5.7 marks it optional).
     *                   When supplied non-empty it must look like an
     *                   address - one '@', no whitespace, a dot-bearing
     *                   domain - and is REJECTED above 100 characters. An
     *                   empty or absent value is accepted and stored as an
     *                   empty string.
     *
     *   type            OPTIONAL at the dictionary level (choice=3, the
     *                   platform's "Dropdown with -- None --"), so an
     *                   absent value is legal and stored empty. A SUPPLIED
     *                   value must match one of the live choices for
     *                   x_casemgmt_case.type, resolved case-insensitively
     *                   and normalised to the canonical stored value, so a
     *                   value outside the choice list can never be stored.
     *
     * NO field is ever silently shortened. Every length violation becomes a
     * named field error, which the calling REST operation answers as HTTP
     * 400 with the { error, fields } body - see the block comment at the
     * length checks for why truncation was the wrong behaviour on an
     * anonymous intake path.
     *
     * The error response names the offending fields. Those five names are
     * already public - the portal form posts them - so naming them leaks
     * nothing an anonymous caller cannot read in the widget source, while
     * making the endpoint usable by any client. No INTERNAL field name
     * (status, assigned_group, assigned_agent, closed_date, ...) ever
     * appears in a validation response.
     *
     * @param {Object} payload - the parsed request body (already checked
     *     to be a non-array object by the caller).
     * @return {Object} { values: { <field>: <cleaned string> } } when the
     *     payload is valid, or { error: '<message>', fields: { <field>:
     *     '<reason>' } } when it is not.
     */
    _validateSubmission: function(payload) {
        var MANDATORY_TEXT_FIELDS = [
            { name: 'subject',        label: 'Subject',    maxLength: 255 },
            { name: 'description',    label: 'Description', maxLength: 4000 },
            { name: 'requester_name', label: 'Your name',  maxLength: 100 }
        ];
        var values = {};
        var fieldErrors = {};
        var i;

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // OVER-LENGTH IS REFUSED, NEVER TRUNCATED.
        //
        // Each of these fields previously did
        //     values[spec.name] = raw.length > spec.maxLength ?
        //         raw.substring(0, spec.maxLength) : raw;
        // which answered HTTP 201 and stored a SILENTLY SHORTENED value.
        // Measured against the live endpoint, a 4001-character description
        // was accepted and stored as 4000 characters, a 256-character
        // subject as 255 and a 101-character requester_name as 100, with
        // nothing in the response distinguishing that from a submission
        // stored in full.
        //
        // For an anonymous intake form that is the worst available
        // behaviour. The requester is handed a case number and told the
        // case was submitted, so they have no reason to check, while the
        // material sentence of a complaint - the one at the end of a long
        // description - is gone, and neither they nor the agent who later
        // reads the case has any way to know that anything was dropped.
        // Refusing the write and naming the field costs the requester one
        // edit and loses nothing.
        //
        // The public form makes this refusal rare rather than routine: the
        // submission widget's inputs carry maxlength=255/4000/100 plus a
        // role="status" notice that fires once a limit is reached
        // (../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget.xml),
        // so a requester using the page cannot normally reach this branch.
        // It is the guard for every OTHER caller of a public endpoint,
        // which is the population that matters on an unauthenticated write
        // path.
        //
        // The message quotes the limit and the length received so a caller
        // can fix the payload in one attempt instead of bisecting it. Both
        // numbers describe the caller's OWN input against a limit the
        // portal form already publishes as an HTML attribute, so nothing
        // internal is disclosed.
        //
        // The equivalent gap on the INTERNAL form is closed separately and
        // server-side by
        //   ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_case_text_lengths.xml
        // which aborts any insert or update whose subject, description,
        // requester_name or requester_email exceeds the declared length,
        // whatever the write path.
        //
        // That rule backstops THIS method for description and only for
        // description, and the reason is worth stating here so the two
        // files are not read as saying the same thing. Measured on this
        // instance: a column declared <= 255 characters is VARCHAR-backed
        // and the platform coerces the value to fit BEFORE before-rules
        // run, so no business rule can observe that subject,
        // requester_name or requester_email arrived over-length (a
        // 300-character subject is answered HTTP 200 and stored at 255).
        // description is declared 4000, is TEXT-backed, is not coerced,
        // and IS refused there (4001 characters is answered HTTP 403 with
        // the stored value unchanged). So for those three fields THIS
        // method is not merely the first line of defence on the anonymous
        // path - it is the only layer that can report the violation at
        // all, which is another reason it must refuse rather than
