        // truncate.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        for (i = 0; i < MANDATORY_TEXT_FIELDS.length; i++) {
            var spec = MANDATORY_TEXT_FIELDS[i];
            var raw = this._readString(payload, spec.name);
            if (raw === '') {
                fieldErrors[spec.name] = spec.label + ' is required.';
                continue;
            }
            if (raw.length > spec.maxLength) {
                fieldErrors[spec.name] = spec.label + ' must be ' + spec.maxLength +
                    ' characters or fewer (received ' + raw.length + ').';
                continue;
            }
            values[spec.name] = raw;
        }

        // requester_email - optional, but validated when present so the
        // stored value is always either empty or plausibly deliverable.
        // Over-length is refused here for the same reason as above: an
        // address truncated to fit is not the requester's address, and
        // storing it would make the case unanswerable while reporting
        // success. The format test runs first so a caller who sends
        // something that is not an address at all is told that, rather
        // than being told about its length.
        var email = this._readString(payload, 'requester_email');
        if (email === '') {
            values.requester_email = '';
        } else if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@.]+(\.[^\s@.]+)+$/.test(email)) {
            fieldErrors.requester_email = 'Email must be a valid address.';
        } else if (email.length > 100) {
            fieldErrors.requester_email = 'Email must be 100 characters or fewer (received ' +
                email.length + ').';
        } else {
            values.requester_email = email;
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // type - REQUIRED on this path, and constrained to the choice list.
        //
        // It is required here even though the DICTIONARY leaves it optional
        // (choice=3, the platform's "Dropdown with -- None --"), and the
        // difference is deliberate rather than an oversight. Two reasons,
        // and the first is decisive.
        //
        // 1. A typeless case cannot be worked. AAP Sections 0.4.1 and 0.5.5
        //    implement the case lifecycle as TWO Flow Designer flows, one
        //    per case type - ../flows/general_inquiry_state_machine.xml
        //    triggered on type = General Inquiry and
        //    ../flows/complaint_state_machine.xml on type = Complaint. A row
        //    whose type is empty matches NEITHER trigger filter, so it can
        //    never be advanced out of Draft by the mechanism the AAP
        //    specifies for advancing it. Storing one produces a case that is
        //    permanently stuck at birth: it counts in every aggregate, it
        //    appears in the internal list, and no flow will ever pick it up.
        //    Measured before this check: three anonymous submissions with
        //    `type` omitted, empty and null each answered HTTP 201 and
        //    created a guest-owned Draft case with type = ''.
        //
        // 2. The public form already states the requirement. The submission
        //    widget renders the control as "Type *" with `required` and
        //    aria-required=true, and its helper text reads "Every field
        //    marked * is required. Complete all four before submitting."
        //    (../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget.xml).
        //    An endpoint that accepts what its own form declares mandatory
        //    is contradicting the contract it publishes, and every
        //    non-browser caller sees the endpoint, not the form.
        //
        // The dictionary is deliberately NOT changed to mandatory: doing so
        // would impose the constraint on every internal write path too,
        // where AAP Section 0.5.7 declares only subject, description and
        // requester_name Mandatory, and the AAP is authoritative on that
        // table's constraints. So the requirement is applied exactly where
        // the contradiction lives - the anonymous intake path this class
        // owns - and nowhere else.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        var type = this._readString(payload, 'type');
        if (type === '') {
            fieldErrors.type = 'Type is required.';
        } else {
            var canonical = this._resolveCaseTypeChoice(type);
            if (canonical === null) {
                fieldErrors.type = 'Type must be one of: ' + this._caseTypeChoices().join(', ') + '.';
            } else {
                values.type = canonical;
            }
        }

        for (var key in fieldErrors) {
            if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(fieldErrors, key)) {
                return {
                    error: 'The submission could not be accepted because one or more fields are invalid.',
                    fields: fieldErrors
                };
            }
        }
        return { values: values };
    },

    /**
     * Read one payload key as a trimmed string.
     *
     * Absent keys, null, undefined, objects and arrays all collapse to the
     * empty string so the caller can treat "not usable" uniformly; scalar
     * non-strings (a JSON number or boolean) are coerced, matching the
     * String() coercion this class has always applied before writing to a
     * string column.
     *
     * @param {Object} payload - the parsed request body.
     * @param {String} key - the field name to read.
     * @return {String} the trimmed value, or '' when unusable.
     */
    _readString: function(payload, key) {
        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(payload, key)) {
            return '';
        }
        var value = payload[key];
        if (value === null || value === undefined) {
            return '';
        }
        if (typeof value === 'object') {
            // An object or array where a scalar belongs is not a usable
            // value; treating it as empty makes it fail the mandatory
            // check rather than storing "[object Object]".
            return '';
        }
        return String(value).trim();
    },

    /**
     * The live choice values for x_casemgmt_case.type, in the order the
     * platform presents them.
     *
     * Read from sys_choice rather than hardcoded so the "extensible" part
     * of the AAP Section 0.5.7 contract ("General Inquiry, Complaint -
     * extensible") keeps working: an administrator who adds a choice does
     * not have to touch this Script Include for the endpoint to accept it.
     * Inactive choices are excluded - an inactive choice must not be
     * storable through the public endpoint.
     *
     * @return {Array} array of choice value strings (possibly empty when
     *     the choice list has not been created yet).
     */
    _caseTypeChoices: function() {
        var choices = [];
        var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        gr.addQuery('name', 'x_casemgmt_case');
        gr.addQuery('element', 'type');
        gr.addQuery('inactive', false);
        gr.orderBy('sequence');
        gr.query();
        while (gr.next()) {
            var value = String(gr.getValue('value') || '');
            if (value !== '' && choices.indexOf(value) === -1) {
                choices.push(value);
            }
        }
        return choices;
    },

    /**
     * Resolve a caller-supplied case type to its canonical stored value.
     *
     * Matching is exact first, then case-insensitive, so 'general inquiry'
     * is accepted and stored as 'General Inquiry' while 'NOT_A_REAL_TYPE'
     * is refused. When the choice list cannot be read at all (it has not
     * been created on this instance yet) the value is refused rather than
     * stored unchecked: refusing is the fail-closed answer, and the choice
     * list is a Gate 1 requirement, so its absence is an installation
     * fault rather than a reason to relax the contract.
     *
     * @param {String} supplied - a non-empty trimmed candidate value.
     * @return {String|null} the canonical choice value, or null when the
     *     candidate is not a live choice.
     */
    _resolveCaseTypeChoice: function(supplied) {
        var choices = this._caseTypeChoices();
        var i;
        for (i = 0; i < choices.length; i++) {
            if (choices[i] === supplied) {
                return choices[i];
            }
        }
        var lowered = supplied.toLowerCase();
        for (i = 0; i < choices.length; i++) {
            if (choices[i].toLowerCase() === lowered) {
                return choices[i];
            }
        }
        return null;
    },

    /**
     * Admission control for the unauthenticated submit path, decided AFTER
     * the row has been inserted.
     *
     * WHY THE DECISION FOLLOWS THE INSERT. This method used to count the
     * rows the endpoint had created inside the trailing window and answer
     * "allowed" while the insert happened afterwards, in submitCase(). That
     * is a check-then-act race (CWE-367) and it bounded nothing under the
     * one condition a flood guard exists for: parallel callers each read the
     * same pre-insert count, each saw it below the ceiling, and each was
     * admitted - so ten simultaneous requests produced ten cases whatever
     * the ceiling said.
     *
     * The decision is now taken from the row itself. submitCase() inserts
     * first and calls this method with the persisted row, and what decides
     * is a COUNT of the rows the same caller created inside the trailing
     * window, taken with our own row already among them. A count above
     * GLOBAL_LIMIT deletes our row and answers its caller with the
     * throttle.
     *
     * WHY COUNTING AFTER THE INSERT BOUNDS THE WINDOW ABSOLUTELY. Take any
     * set of rows that survive this guard and consider the one whose count
     * query ran LAST. Every other survivor had already inserted when that
     * query ran: a survivor's insert commits before that survivor's own
     * query, and its query ran before the last one. So the last caller's
     * query saw every other survivor, and its own row besides. Had more
     * than GLOBAL_LIMIT rows survived, that caller would have counted more
     * than GLOBAL_LIMIT and refused itself - a contradiction. At most
     * GLOBAL_LIMIT rows therefore survive a window, with no lock, no
     * counter table and no serialization, and the bound holds whatever the
     * interleaving.
     *
     * WHY THE TWO OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVES DO NOT. A count taken BEFORE the
     * insert bounds nothing, because nothing bound the insert that followed
     * it: every parallel caller read the same below-ceiling number and
     * every one of them was admitted (CWE-367). A RANK taken after the
     * insert - our row's position among the window's rows under a total
     * order - fails differently and less visibly: rank can only be computed
     * over the rows a query can SEE, so a caller whose query sees only part
     * of the window ranks itself near the front and admits, and a run of
     * inserts arriving in descending sys_id order admits every one of them
     * however far past the ceiling it goes. Counting has no such hole,
     * because a partial view can only UNDER-count, and an under-count is
     * exactly what the last caller's complete view corrects.
     *
     * THE ONE COST, AND IT IS THE SAFE DIRECTION. A caller can be
     * over-REJECTED and can never be over-ADMITTED. Under a burst that is
     * genuinely simultaneous - every request inserting before any of them
     * counts - each caller sees a window already past the ceiling, and how
     * many are refused depends only on how much of the withdrawal each
     * caller's query can already see: the range runs from JUST THE EXCESS,
     * when refusals are visible to the callers that follow, to THE WHOLE
     * BURST, when every caller queried before any withdrawal committed.
     * Both ends are inside the ceiling and both were measured (see the
     * offline harness cited under VERIFICATION below). That is deliberate:
     * the answer is a retryable throttle, the next window admits normally,
     * legitimate traffic on this endpoint never approaches ten submissions
     * in sixty seconds, and an abuser gains nothing by racing. The same
     * insert-then-reconcile shape is already how this file verifies the
     * round trip and collapses duplicate submissions.
     *
     * VERIFICATION. The bound above is a claim about interleavings, which
     * no single-threaded reading of this file can settle, so it was
     * exercised offline against this exact method body with a stubbed
     * GlideRecord that models what each caller's query may see: 3,000
     * randomly generated schedules (arbitrary interleavings of insert and
     * count, under both delete-visibility models), the prefix-visibility
     * run in descending sys_id order that the earlier RANK implementation
     * admitted in full, and the simultaneous burst at both ends of the
     * range above. No schedule left more than GLOBAL_LIMIT rows in the
     * window or more than PER_REQUESTER_LIMIT in one bucket. What that
     * cannot establish is the platform's own commit visibility, which only
     * a deployed instance shows; the mandatory pre-release gate recorded in
     * ../docs/validation-gates.md is where that is settled.
     *
     * WHAT THIS CEILING IS NOT. It is a rate control on one endpoint, not
     * an identity check and not the security perimeter: it cannot tell two
     * anonymous callers apart (see PER-REQUESTER FAIRNESS below), and a
     * caller that keeps its traffic under the ceiling is not slowed at all.
     * The platform-native per-hour ceiling shipped beside this endpoint
     * (../portal/rest/sys_rate_limit_rules_x_casemgmt_case_submit.xml) is
     * the defence-in-depth layer for that residue, and its own file records
     * that its binding and effectiveness are unverified on this release.
     *
     * PER-REQUESTER FAIRNESS. One global allowance is a denial-of-service
     * lever in its own right: a single abuser consuming all ten submissions
     * leaves nothing for any legitimate requester until the window rolls. A
     * second, tighter ceiling therefore applies to the rows in the window
     * that share this submission's requester_email bucket, normalised
     * case-insensitively, with an absent or empty address forming its OWN
     * bucket so it cannot dilute anybody else's. PER_REQUESTER_LIMIT is
     * strictly below GLOBAL_LIMIT, so no single bucket can consume the
     * endpoint's whole allowance.
     *
     * requester_email is used because it is the only caller-identifying
     * value the AAP Section 0.5.7 data model puts on this path, and no new
     * table, field or property may be added to carry a better one (Section
     * 0.7.2 Minimal-Change Clause; Section 0.5.7 is verbatim). HONEST LIMIT:
     * an abuser who varies the address defeats the bucket - it is a fairness
     * dimension, not an identity. What still bounds that abuser is the
     * global ceiling above, the native per-hour rate-limit rule on the guest
     * user, and the refusal log below, which names the ceiling that fired so
     * an operator can alert on a sustained flood.
     *
     * WHOSE ROWS ARE COUNTED. The window is scoped to OUR OWN row's
     * sys_created_by rather than to the literal 'guest', so it is correct
     * for whatever user the platform runs an unauthenticated call as, and an
     * internal user's cases are never ranked against an anonymous caller's:
     * a flood through this endpoint cannot throttle case creation on the
     * native form, and case creation on the native form cannot throttle this
     * endpoint.
     *
     * A REFUSED SUBMISSION CONSUMES A CASE NUMBER. The platform allocates
     * the number during the insert, so a withdrawn row leaves a gap in the
     * CASE sequence - already true of this file's round-trip refusal, of a
     * collapsed duplicate and of every form load, so gaps carry no meaning
     * here, but a reader comparing counts should expect them.
     *
     * NO PII IS LOGGED. The refusal log carries the marker, the count, the
     * ceilings and our own row's sys_id - never the address that formed the
     * bucket, never any submitted field value (AAP Section 0.7.2 no-PII).
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} savedGr - the post-insert re-query of our own
     *     row, already positioned on it.
     * @param {String} newSysId - the sys_id returned by insert().
     * @return {Object} { allowed: Boolean } - true when our row is inside
     *     both ceilings and survives; false when the window count exceeded
     *     one of them, in which case the row has ALREADY been removed. No count,
     *     limit or window is returned, so no caller can leak one to an
     *     anonymous requester.
     */
    _admitAnonymousSubmission: function(savedGr, newSysId) {
        var SUBMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS = 60;
        var GLOBAL_LIMIT = 10;
        var PER_REQUESTER_LIMIT = 4;
        var LOG_MARKER = 'X_CASEMGMT_PORTAL_SUBMIT_ABUSE|';

        var creator = String(savedGr.getValue('sys_created_by') || '');
        if (creator === '') {
            // Without a creator the window cannot be scoped to this
            // endpoint's own rows, and widening it to every recent case
            // would let internal case creation throttle the public endpoint.
            // The guard declines rather than guesses, and says so: this
            // ceiling is a rate control, not the security perimeter, and the
            // native per-hour rule on the guest user still applies.
            gs.warn(LOG_MARKER + 'guard_skipped reason=empty_sys_created_by sys_id=' + newSysId);
            return { allowed: true };
        }

        var windowStart = new GlideDateTime();
        windowStart.addSeconds(-SUBMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS);

        var ourBucket = this._requesterEmailBucket(savedGr.getValue('requester_email'));

        // GLOBAL_LIMIT + 1 rows are enough to decide and reading no more
        // keeps this query bounded during a flood: a window already holding
        // that many rows is past the ceiling whatever else it holds. The
        // order does not enter the decision - a count does not depend on it
        // - and is kept only so the rows read during a flood are the
        // window's oldest, which makes a refusal reproducible from the log.
        var rows = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        rows.addQuery('sys_created_by', creator);
        rows.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', windowStart);
        rows.orderBy('sys_created_on');
        rows.orderBy('sys_id');
        rows.setLimit(GLOBAL_LIMIT + 1);
        rows.query();

        var windowCount = 0;
        var bucketCount = 0;
        var sawOurRow = false;
        while (rows.next()) {
            windowCount++;
            if (String(rows.getValue('sys_id') || '') === newSysId) {
                sawOurRow = true;
            }
            if (this._requesterEmailBucket(rows.getValue('requester_email')) === ourBucket) {
                bucketCount++;
            }
        }

        if (!sawOurRow) {
            // Our row exists - this method only runs after an insert that
            // succeeded and a re-query that found it - so it counts even
            // when this query could not return it, which is what happens
            // when the window already held GLOBAL_LIMIT + 1 older rows and
            // the limit truncated ours away. Counting it keeps the decision
            // on the safe side in that case instead of guessing.
            windowCount++;
            bucketCount++;
        }

        if (windowCount > GLOBAL_LIMIT) {
            return this._discardOverflowSubmission(newSysId, LOG_MARKER, 'global_window_ceiling',
                'count=' + windowCount + ' limit=' + GLOBAL_LIMIT +
                ' window_seconds=' + SUBMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS);
        }

        // The bucket count is exact whenever the global count is inside its
        // ceiling, because the query then returned every row of the window
        // rather than a truncated prefix of it.
        if (bucketCount > PER_REQUESTER_LIMIT) {
            return this._discardOverflowSubmission(newSysId, LOG_MARKER, 'per_requester_ceiling',
                'count=' + bucketCount + ' limit=' + PER_REQUESTER_LIMIT +
                ' window_seconds=' + SUBMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS);
        }

        return { allowed: true };
    },

    /**
     * Normalise a requester_email value into the bucket key the
     * per-requester fairness ceiling counts by.
     *
     * Case and surrounding whitespace are not identity, so both are removed.
     * An absent, empty or whitespace-only address collapses to the empty
     * bucket. That empty value is a BUCKET, not a wildcard: an address-less
     * submission is never counted against one that carries an address, so a
     * flood of address-less requests cannot push a requester who supplied
     * one over the per-requester ceiling. All address-less submissions DO
     * share that single bucket, which is the honest consequence of having no
     * better caller dimension on this path - what bounds that case is the
     * global ceiling and the native per-hour rule, not this bucket.
     *
     * The value is used ONLY as an in-memory grouping key: it is never
     * logged, never stored anywhere new and never returned to a caller, so
     * no address leaves the row it was submitted on (AAP Section 0.7.2
     * no-PII).
     *
     * @param {String} value - a row's requester_email, as read with
     *     GlideRecord.getValue() (may be null, undefined or empty).
     * @return {String} the bucket key; '' when there is no address.
     */
    _requesterEmailBucket: function(value) {
        if (value === null || value === undefined) {
            return '';
        }
        return String(value).trim().toLowerCase();
    },

    /**
     * Withdraw the row this request inserted because the window count
     * exceeded one of the admission ceilings, and report the refusal.
     *
     * The row is removed rather than left in place because an admitted
     * submission and a refused one must not both persist a case: the caller
     * is being told, with HTTP 429, that nothing was accepted, so nothing
     * may remain. A failed delete is the one branch that leaves a case
     * behind the requester was never told about, so it is logged with
     * gs.error and names the sys_id an administrator has to remove by hand.
     *
     * Every line starts with the caller-supplied STABLE MARKER so an
     * operator can alert on the prefix alone. The lines carry counts,
     * ceilings and our own row's sys_id, and no submitted value, no address
     * and no client identifier, so the log stays free of PII.
     *
     * @param {String} newSysId - the sys_id returned by insert().
     * @param {String} marker - the stable log-marker prefix.
     * @param {String} reason - which ceiling refused the row.
     * @param {String} detail - space-separated key=value diagnostics.
     * @return {Object} { allowed: false } - always, so the caller returns
     *     the throttled response whether or not the cleanup succeeded.
     */
    _discardOverflowSubmission: function(newSysId, marker, reason, detail) {
        var cleanupGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        if (!cleanupGr.get(newSysId)) {
            gs.warn(marker + 'refused reason=' + reason + ' ' + detail +
                ' cleanup=row_already_gone sys_id=' + newSysId);
            return { allowed: false };
        }
        if (!cleanupGr.deleteRecord()) {
            gs.error(marker + 'refused reason=' + reason + ' ' + detail +
                ' cleanup=FAILED sys_id=' + newSysId +
                ' lastErrorMessage=' + cleanupGr.getLastErrorMessage() +
                '; the refused case row still exists and needs manual removal.');
            return { allowed: false };
        }
        gs.warn(marker + 'refused reason=' + reason + ' ' + detail +
            ' cleanup=ok sys_id=' + newSysId);
        return { allowed: false };
    },

    /**
     * Class-name marker. ServiceNow's Class.create() pattern conventionally
     * exposes a `type` property whose value matches the class name (without
     * the scope prefix). This is used by the platform's introspection
     * tooling and by some debug logging. It MUST be 'CasePortalService'
     * (NOT 'x_casemgmt_CasePortalService') - the scope prefix lives only in
     * the <api_name> element above, not in the class name itself.
     */
    type: 'CasePortalService'
};
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>95e90fa18471e42875f5f956ec7949d1</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>CasePortalService</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_include_95e90fa18471e42875f5f956ec7949d1</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 05:45:34</sys_updated_on></sys_script_include></record_update>

x_casemgmt_case_resumetruefalseUI Action that resumes a Pending case back to In Progress status, clearing pending_reason. Visible to x_casemgmt_case_manager (always) and x_casemgmt_case_agent (only when assigned to the case via assigned_agent or member of assigned_group, per AAP Section 0.5.6 Assigned-only rule). Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 4 verbatim: "Pending -> In Progress: None; clears pending_reason". Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role, status, and assignment. Explicitly clears pending_reason in addition to the companion business rule ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress.xml (order=400) which also clears it during the same database update transaction; together they form a belt-and-suspenders defense-in-depth pair. sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_46b2e4e627993d8b706ade6c788dc2a1
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>true</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-insert and before-update on x_casemgmt_case: refuses any write that would store an empty or whitespace-only subject, description or requester_name, naming the offending field via gs.addErrorMessage() and cancelling the write via current.setAbortAction(true). Closes QA finding F15 for the parent table: dictionary mandatory flags are form-time only, so POST /api/now/table/x_casemgmt_case {} previously returned HTTP 201 and stored a blank-shell case. Enforces AAP Section 0.5.7 (subject/description/requester_name Mandatory) and Section 0.7.3 Gate 1 (Zero missing mandatory fields) on every server-side write path - Table API, background script, Import Set, scoped Script Include. Order=50 is the lowest in the chain so a structurally invalid row is refused before the state-machine rules at 100-500 evaluate; orders 70 and 80 are reserved. Returns early on current.isActionAborted() so it never stacks a message onto an already-rejected save, and reproduces none of the four verbatim messages Section 0.7.4 fixes. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_validate_case_mandatory_field</name><order>50</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Server-side backstop for AAP Section 0.5.7's MANDATORY contract on
    // x_casemgmt_case, and for Section 0.7.3 Gate 1 ("Zero missing
    // mandatory fields").
    //
    // A sys_dictionary mandatory flag is enforced by the FORM engine, not by
    // the insert/update pipeline, so every non-form write path bypassed it.
    // Measured before this rule existed:
    //     POST /api/now/table/x_casemgmt_case {}  ->  HTTP 201
    // which stored a case with no subject, no description and no requester
    // name. This rule is the one hook that all of the Table API, background
    // scripts, Import Set transforms and scoped Script Includes run through.

    // Stop if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    //
    // setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, not the remaining before
    // rules - the platform keeps running them and reports the pending abort
    // through current.isActionAborted(). This rule is currently first at
    // order 50, so the flag is normally false here; the guard is retained
    // because orders 70 and 80 are RESERVED for future guards that would
    // run ahead of nothing but could be renumbered below 50, and because it
    // is the discipline every other rule in this chain follows. Returning
    // here keeps an already-refused save from collecting a second,
    // unrelated message on top of the one the caller needs to read.
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // Data-driven declaration of the three MANDATORY columns from AAP
    // Section 0.5.7. `label` is the column_label the dictionary carries
    // (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_subject.xml, _description.xml,
    // _requester_name.xml), so the message names the field exactly as the
    // caller sees it on the form and in the list header.
    //
    // Deliberately NOT included:
    //   - `status`   : dictionary-mandatory with default_value='Draft', so it
    //                  can never be empty on insert, and the state machine
    //                  (orders 100-500) owns every subsequent value.
    //   - `number`   : issued by the platform's Number Maintenance subsystem
    //                  during the insert pipeline and read-only thereafter.
    //   - `type`, `priority`, `requester_email`, `opened_date`,
    //     `closed_date`, `assigned_group`, `assigned_agent`,
    //     `pending_reason` : Section 0.5.7 marks none of them Mandatory.
    //     assigned_group is required only ON the Draft -> Open transition,
    //     which is the validate_open_transition subflow's contract reached
    //     through x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions at order 250 - not
    //     a column-level invariant, and not this rule's concern.
    var MANDATORY_FIELDS = [
        { element: 'subject', label: 'Subject' },
        { element: 'description', label: 'Description' },
        { element: 'requester_name', label: 'Requester Name' }
    ];

    for (var i = 0; i < MANDATORY_FIELDS.length; i++) {
        var element = MANDATORY_FIELDS[i].element;

        // getValue() returns the underlying String, or null when the column
        // was never set. It is used in preference to property access
        // (current.subject) because it has one documented return contract
        // across field types and releases, whereas a GlideElement wrapper
        // coerces to '' in some contexts and to the literal 'null' in
        // others. The value read is the value the row WOULD CARRY AFTER
        // this write: on update, a PATCH that touches only `priority`
        // reads the stored, populated subject and passes untouched, so no
        // unrelated update is made harder than it was.
        var value = current.getValue(element);

        // Whitespace is empty. Section 0.5.7's "Mandatory" is a statement
        // about content: a space-only subject renders as a blank cell in
        // the case list and as a blank line in the anonymous portal
        // lookup, so it is refused alongside '' and null. The same trimming
        // is applied to these three fields on the portal path by
        // x_casemgmt.CasePortalService._validateSubmission().
        if (value === null || value === undefined || String(value).trim() === '') {
            // gs.addErrorMessage() surfaces the message as a blocking
            // banner at the top of the case form for a UI save, and is
            // recorded in the session message list for a Table API call
            // (whose own 403 body names this rule). Per AAP Section 0.7.1:
            // "Surface all blocking errors on the form. Invalid transition
            // attempts MUST produce a blocking error message visible on the
            // form - silent failures or post-save error logs are
            // unacceptable."
            //
            // The wording is target-side authored: AAP Section 0.7.4 fixes
            // exactly four verbatim strings and none of them is a
            // mandatory-field message, so no other rule's message is
            // reproduced here. Naming the field is what makes the refusal
            // actionable for a caller who cannot see the form.
            gs.addErrorMessage(MANDATORY_FIELDS[i].label +
                ' is mandatory and cannot be empty.');

            // setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both calls
            // are required: without the message the write is refused with no
            // visible diagnosis, and without the abort the message appears
            // while the invalid row is still persisted.
            current.setAbortAction(true);

            // Return on the FIRST violation rather than reporting all
            // three. One actionable message is what the form banner and the
            // Table API response can each carry legibly, and the caller
            // re-submits after fixing it, at which point the next violation
            // - if any - is reported the same way.
            return;
        }
    }
})(current, previous);

sys_update_xml.name: sys_ui_policy_e13c3e9e50df1b846271700b571c5a82
sys_update_xml.payload:
truestatus=ClosedTerminal-state read-only UI Policy on x_casemgmt_case. Implements the form-layer half of AAP Section 0.5.5's transition matrix row 8 ("Closed -> * PROHIBITED - terminal state", verbatim failure message "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified."), closing QA finding Issue 17: a Closed case rendered all ten of its writable fields as live inputs, so correctness rested entirely on the before-update Business Rule x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed aborting the save after the gesture. When status=Closed the ten sys_ui_policy_action children present type, status, priority, subject, description, requester_name, requester_email, assigned_group, assigned_agent and pending_reason as read-only (the action column `disabled`), so the form states the terminal restriction before the operator acts. The other four fields the form renders - number, opened_date, closed_date, duration_to_close - already carry read_only=true in sys_dictionary and need no action. This policy is PRESENTATION ONLY: it enforces nothing and replaces nothing. x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed remains the enforcement layer for every write path a browser is not involved in (Table API, scripts, list inline edit) and keeps surfacing the verbatim message; because no control can now be dirtied on a Closed form, pressing Update is the genuine no-op save that guard explicitly still allows. mandatory=ignore on every action so the four dictionary-mandatory fields keep their constraint untouched; visible=ignore so a Closed case stays fully readable for audit, reporting and the read-only viewer role; cleared=false and value_action=ignore so no field value is ever read, written or cleared. reverse_if_false is deliberately FALSE, unlike the companion party policies: the reverse of disabled=true is an explicit "make writable" that would be applied to all ten fields on every non-Closed case form, including the two fields whose write access AAP Section 0.5.6 restricts through field-level ACLs (assigned_group, assigned_agent), which would recreate this same defect pointed at the ACL matrix. Nothing is lost, because a Closed row can never legally leave Closed and its status control is itself read-only here. run_scripts=false with empty script bodies - there is no imperative logic. The six transition UI Actions need no change: each is evaluated server-side against current and requires an exact non-Closed source status, so none renders on a Closed case. The form's Update and Delete buttons are out-of-the-box global sys_ui_action records that AAP Section 0.3.2 puts out of bounds for this package.truefalsefalsetrue100falsefalseCase Closed Terminal State - Read Only: present every writable field of a Closed case as read-only, so the form states AAP 0.5.5's terminal restriction instead of inviting an edit the server guard then refuses.sys_ui_policyadmin2025-01-01 00:00:00global/e13c3e9e50df1b846271700b571c5a820Case Closed Terminal State - Read Only: present every writable field of a Closed case as read-only, so the form states AAP 0.5.5's terminal restriction instead of inviting an edit the server guard then refuses.82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_ui_policy_e13c3e9e50df1b846271700b571c5a82admin2025-01-01 00:00:00x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>true</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>false</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-insert on x_casemgmt_case: sets current.opened_date = gs.nowDateTime() when not already populated. Replaces ArkCase CaseFile.@PrePersist beforeInsert() audit hook from acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java. Per AAP Section 0.5.7 (opened_date Auto-set on creation). Defensive: respects pre-set values from seed data and other authoritative callers via current.opened_date.nil() guard. Fires in all contexts (form, Table API, scripted REST, seed scripts) because is_rest=false. Order=100 ensures the field is populated early in the before-insert phase. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_set_opened_date</name><order>100</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase CaseFile.@PrePersist beforeInsert()
    // (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    //  armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java, lines 307-316).
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7: opened_date is "DateTime, Auto-set on creation".
    //
    // Defensive .nil() guard: respect pre-set values from authoritative callers.
    // This is critical for the seed-data demos in
    // ../seed-data/cases/x_casemgmt_case_demo_*.xml which explicitly set
    // synthetic timestamps spanning the past 30 days so the "Cases opened
    // (30 days)" single-score widget on the Manager View dashboard
    // (../reports/x_casemgmt_cases_opened_30d.xml) has non-zero data on a
    // freshly-imported PDI. Without this guard, the seeded timestamps would
    // be overwritten with gs.nowDateTime() at import time and every demo
    // case would appear to be opened on import day.
    //
    // For organic inserts (form submissions, Table API calls, portal scripted
    // REST submissions, ad-hoc admin scripts) where opened_date is not
    // pre-populated, the script populates the field with the current platform
    // time so downstream reports and the portal status lookup never see a
    // null opened_date.
    if (current.opened_date.nil()) {
        current.opened_date = new GlideDateTime();
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>c56aeecd4086f111be2867faae9e55ad</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_set_opened_date</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_set_opened_date</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=c56aeecd4086f111be2867faae9e55ad"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_44c5a728c4f234c957a8218eb121f643
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>true</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Table-level ACL: x_casemgmt_case_agent can write x_casemgmt_case records ONLY when assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current user (per AAP Section 0.5.6 'Assigned only'). Field-level ACLs on assigned_group/assigned_agent further restrict those specific fields.</description><local_or_existing/><name>x_casemgmt_case</name><operation display_value="write">write</operation><script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();

    // INSERT PATH - closes QA finding F4 (HIGH).
    //
    // On an insert the platform evaluates this table-level WRITE ACL once
    // per column being set, BEFORE the row exists. At that moment
    // current.assigned_agent and current.assigned_group are empty (an agent
    // cannot populate either: assigned_group is manager-only per
    // ../acl/x_casemgmt_case_assigned_group_field_acl.xml, and the case is
    // not yet assigned to anyone), so the "Assigned only" predicate below
    // could never be satisfied and EVERY field value the agent supplied was
    // silently discarded - the create ACL
    // (../acl/x_casemgmt_case_create_agent.xml) still admitted the row, so
    // the insert returned success and stored a blank-shell case. Measured
    // before this limb existed: an agent-created case landed with subject,
    // description, requester_name and type all empty.
    //
    // "Assigned only" is a statement about which EXISTING records an agent
    // may reach (AAP Section 0.5.6, and Section 0.7.3 Gate 3 "case_agent
    // cannot access unassigned cases"). It is logically inapplicable to a
    // record that does not exist yet - the same reasoning the create ACL
    // records in its own header for running with advanced=false. Admitting
    // the insert path here is therefore what makes the Create cell the AAP
    // grants an actually working grant rather than a row-shaped hole.
    //
    // This limb widens nothing on the update path: isNewRecord() is true
    // only while the row is being inserted. Nor does it let the agent set
    // privileged columns during that insert - the two field-level ACLs on
    // assigned_group and assigned_agent are evaluated in ADDITION to this
    // record and still refuse assigned_group outright for a non-manager.
    // Mandatory-field content is enforced independently of any ACL by
    // ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_case_mandatory_fields.xml
    // (order 50), so an agent insert that carries no subject/description/
    // requester_name is refused with a named field error rather than
    // stored blank.
    if (current.isNewRecord()) {
        return true;
    }

    // UPDATE PATH - AAP Section 0.5.6 "Assigned only", unchanged.
    if (current.assigned_agent == currentUserId) {
        return true;
    }
    if (current.assigned_group && !current.assigned_group.nil()) {
        var groupId = current.assigned_group.toString();
        if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
})();]]></script><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>44c5a728c4f234c957a8218eb121f643</sys_id><sys_mod_count>2</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_44c5a728c4f234c957a8218eb121f643</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 05:45:34</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_atf_step"><sys_atf_step action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><callable_outputs/><copied_from/><description>Run Server Side Validation Script</description><display_name>Run Server Side Script</display_name><inputs/><mugshots_cache_json/><notes>One assigned and one unassigned synthetic case</notes><order>1</order><step_config display_value="Run Server Side Script">41de4a935332120028bc29cac2dc349a</step_config><sys_class_name>sys_atf_step</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>Run Server Side Script</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_atf_step_0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><table/><test display_value="ATF 02 - RBAC: x_casemgmt_case_manager has full CRUD (AAP 0.5.6)">64dd92fb6ce07b6b62d2978edd0231f2</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>8250d1fdd592d6879163cb99e58c239d</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>0c49d5628dca1cfa5a6de8db29fabe6e</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>e609efad5a803801bd39d9050436ae96</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "mine",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "6fab7dd278e415c8e5bdea665c89d8a5",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-02",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-02 manager fixture",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "unassigned",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "93eeda729062207211ec3270cbf1545e",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-02",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-02 unassigned fixture",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium"
            }
        }
    ];

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);

server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "closed",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "3ed0fd4998aa5a461d089e574c504954",
            "prefix": "ATF-SM-14",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-SM-14 closed case",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Closed",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        }
    ];

    // CLEANUP IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED.
    //
    // This step used to end with a "cleanup ran" check that compared the literal
    // string true against itself - a tautology. It therefore passed even when every
    // delete had
    // silently failed, so fixtures could survive and contaminate later steps, later
    // tests in the suite, and later runs (a stale pinned sys_id or a stale prefix row
    // makes another test assert against the wrong record). What follows checks the
    // outcome of each delete and then RE-QUERIES for residue, so a surviving row fails
    // this step and is named in the failure message.
    //
    // Note on coverage: a fixture carrying no `prefix` (case_party rows, which have no
    // `subject` column to match on) is swept by pinned sys_id only - the same guard the
    // delete loop uses - because that is the only key such a row is ever created with.
    var removed = 0, failedDeletes = [];
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) {
            old.setWorkflow(false);
            if (old.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[d].table + ':' + FIX[d].sys_id);
        }
    }
    for (var p = 0; p < FIX.length; p++) {
        if (!FIX[p].prefix) continue;
        var extra = new GlideRecord(FIX[p].table);
        extra.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[p].prefix);
        extra.query();
        while (extra.next()) {
            var extraId = extra.getUniqueValue();
            extra.setWorkflow(false);
            if (extra.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[p].table + ':' + extraId);
        }
    }
    chk('every delete reported success', '', failedDeletes.join(' | '));

    // Residue re-query: by pinned sys_id for every fixture, and by prefix for every
    // fixture that has one. Any row still present here is a real leak.
    var residue = [];
    for (var q = 0; q < FIX.length; q++) {
        var byId = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        if (byId.get(FIX[q].sys_id))
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' sys_id ' + FIX[q].sys_id + ' survived');
        if (!FIX[q].prefix) continue;
        var byPrefix = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        byPrefix.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[q].prefix);
        byPrefix.query();
        while (byPrefix.next())
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' ' + byPrefix.getUniqueValue() +
                ' [' + byPrefix.getValue('subject') + '] survived');
    }
    chk('no fixture residue remains after cleanup', '', residue.join(' | '));

    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends, so every reported
    // line is accumulated and emitted once, at the end of the step.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('fixtures removed=' + removed +
        ' | deletes reporting failure=' + failedDeletes.length +
        ' | residue rows=' + residue.length);
    notes.push('fixture cleanup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture cleanup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);

Form: returning a case to Draft is blocked on the form">058f262dab9141adcb30c3bd61667a78</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=9ab82b16bf0d4bc4ab9cd7ff9dcd6aa7"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>9ab82b16bf0d4bc4ab9cd7ff9dcd6aa7</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>2c61748d993b89fd9374e97b37fd8e3b</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "open",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "8245a6f0cd348d300927983d87085c9b",
            "prefix": "ATF-UI-16",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-UI-16 open case",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Open",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team"
            }
        }
    ];

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // VERBATIM MESSAGE, asserted before the fixtures are removed.
    //
    // WHAT ATF CAN AND CANNOT SEE HERE. The submit in step 5 is refused by the
    // server and step 6 proves the stored row did not change, but ATF ships no step
    // type that can read the classic form's error banner: the only text-on-page
    // assertion in the framework is "Assert Text on Page (Custom UI)", which targets
    // the Custom UI DOM and not the platform form these tests drive, and the
    // "Submit a Form" step exposes only `form_ui` and `assert_type` inputs. So the
    // fact that the message is RENDERED is a MANUAL observation - see the runner's
    // step-5 screenshot and docs/ATF_MANUAL_TEST_PLAN.md - and is not claimed as
    // automated coverage anywhere.
    //
    // What IS automated is the string itself. Without the block below this test could
    // pass while the message was missing or reworded, because nothing it asserted
    // depended on the wording. Asserting the exact string here, in the same
    // transaction and against the same fixture the form just submitted, means a
    // missing or altered message turns this test RED.
    var gate = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    chkTrue('the fixture case is still present for the message assertion',
        gate.get('8245a6f0cd348d300927983d87085c9b'));
    chk('the case is still Open, so the refused submit changed nothing',
        'Open', gate.getValue('status'));
    var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
    var verdict = validator.validateNoBacktransition(gate.getValue('status'), 'Draft');
    chk('the backtransition to Draft is refused', 'false', String(verdict.ok));
    chk('the blocking message is verbatim (AAP 0.7.4)',
        'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.', String(verdict.error));
    // stepResult.setOutputMessage OVERWRITES the step's output on every call - it does
    // NOT append. Measured in the client runner: this step called it three times and
    // only the last line survived, so the message-assertion evidence below was written
    // and then silently discarded. Every line is therefore accumulated here and emitted
    // exactly once, at the end of the step.
    var notes = ['message asserted server-side: [' + verdict.error + ']'];

    // CLEANUP IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED.
    //
    // This step used to end with a "cleanup ran" check that compared the literal
    // string true against itself - a tautology. It therefore passed even when every
    // delete had
    // silently failed, so fixtures could survive and contaminate later steps, later
    // tests in the suite, and later runs (a stale pinned sys_id or a stale prefix row
    // makes another test assert against the wrong record). What follows checks the
    // outcome of each delete and then RE-QUERIES for residue, so a surviving row fails
    // this step and is named in the failure message.
    //
    // Note on coverage: a fixture carrying no `prefix` (case_party rows, which have no
    // `subject` column to match on) is swept by pinned sys_id only - the same guard the
    // delete loop uses - because that is the only key such a row is ever created with.
    var removed = 0, failedDeletes = [];
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) {
            old.setWorkflow(false);
            if (old.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[d].table + ':' + FIX[d].sys_id);
        }
    }
    for (var p = 0; p < FIX.length; p++) {
        if (!FIX[p].prefix) continue;
        var extra = new GlideRecord(FIX[p].table);
        extra.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[p].prefix);
        extra.query();
        while (extra.next()) {
            var extraId = extra.getUniqueValue();
            extra.setWorkflow(false);
            if (extra.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[p].table + ':' + extraId);
        }
    }
    chk('every delete reported success', '', failedDeletes.join(' | '));

    // Residue re-query: by pinned sys_id for every fixture, and by prefix for every
    // fixture that has one. Any row still present here is a real leak.
    var residue = [];
    for (var q = 0; q < FIX.length; q++) {
        var byId = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        if (byId.get(FIX[q].sys_id))
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' sys_id ' + FIX[q].sys_id + ' survived');
        if (!FIX[q].prefix) continue;
        var byPrefix = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        byPrefix.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[q].prefix);
        byPrefix.query();
        while (byPrefix.next())
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' ' + byPrefix.getUniqueValue() +
                ' [' + byPrefix.getValue('subject') + '] survived');
    }
    chk('no fixture residue remains after cleanup', '', residue.join(' | '));
    notes.push('fixtures removed=' + removed +
        ' | deletes reporting failure=' + failedDeletes.length +
        ' | residue rows=' + residue.length);
    notes.push('fixture cleanup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture cleanup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);

both-branch, direct-only, group-only, unassigned and nonmember-group - each with one child task and one child party</notes><order>1</order><step_config display_value="Run Server Side Script">41de4a935332120028bc29cac2dc349a</step_config><sys_class_name>sys_atf_step</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>d3b39dda41536d859e5d65633e0af619</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>Run Server Side Script</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_atf_step_d3b39dda41536d859e5d65633e0af619</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><table/><test display_value="ATF 07 - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    // A group the demo agent is definitively NOT a member of, resolved at run time by
    // elimination rather than by name, so the test needs no second seeded group and no
    // hardcoded group name. AAP 0.5.6 defines "Assigned only" as
    //     assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current user
    // and proving the "only" half requires a parent whose group does NOT contain the
    // agent. The chosen group is asserted below to be a genuine non-membership.
    function nonMemberGroupId(userName) {
        var uid = userId(userName);
        var mine = {}, m = new GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember');
        m.addQuery('user', uid);
        m.query();
        while (m.next()) { mine[m.getValue('group')] = 1; }
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('active', true);
        g.orderBy('name');
        g.query();
        while (g.next()) {
            if (!mine[g.getUniqueValue()]) { return g.getUniqueValue(); }
        }
        return '';
    }
    var OTHER_GRP_ID = nonMemberGroupId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');

    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "parent-both",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "ee66fab2aae0daab57a18a04fa5fc3bd",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 parent case",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "task",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_task",
            "sys_id": "ed02fff340bf0037625492f0cb259810",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "case": "ee66fab2aae0daab57a18a04fa5fc3bd",
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 task",
                "type": "Review",
                "status": "Open",
                "assigned_to": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "due_date": "2026-12-31"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "party",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_party",
            "sys_id": "41b752e01dd8d0f75ef3230a70b55d2c",
            "prefix": null,
            "fields": {
                "case": "ee66fab2aae0daab57a18a04fa5fc3bd",
                "party_type": "Person",
                "person": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "role_label": "Witness"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "parent-direct",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "bad75eb1c21c932236a5cd1a275fc83f",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 parent assigned DIRECTLY to the agent, no group",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "task-direct",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_task",
            "sys_id": "74896b49d2174d3fbf07b0f3c0e13cfb",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "case": "bad75eb1c21c932236a5cd1a275fc83f",
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 task on the direct parent",
                "type": "Review",

                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 parent assigned to the agent GROUP only, no agent",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "task-group",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_task",
            "sys_id": "f3573645a8f769471a11daeeb63a75b1",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "case": "f7fb08a92f84b635e1118fbf871a97c5",
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 task on the group parent",
                "type": "Review",
                "status": "Open",
                "assigned_to": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "due_date": "2026-12-31"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "party-group",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_party",
            "sys_id": "d97f9690087d07b7e9a2633a357fbd28",
            "prefix": null,
            "fields": {
                "case": "f7fb08a92f84b635e1118fbf871a97c5",
                "party_type": "Person",
                "person": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "role_label": "Witness"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "parent-unassigned",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "c12db6ba96650309f874e2245ad94102",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 parent assigned to NOBODY",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "task-unassigned",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_task",
            "sys_id": "255261c44d7e569393eb5b378f093cf5",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "case": "c12db6ba96650309f874e2245ad94102",
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 task on the unassigned parent",
                "type": "Review",
                "status": "Open",
                "assigned_to": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "due_date": "2026-12-31"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "party-unassigned",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_party",
            "sys_id": "84d0b2cec80ea74f5d3b34003cfb2629",
            "prefix": null,
            "fields": {
                "case": "c12db6ba96650309f874e2245ad94102",
                "party_type": "Person",
                "person": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "role_label": "Witness"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "parent-othergroup",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "8e8ba999d36f28846a3a63a1889b0794",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 parent assigned to a group the agent is NOT in",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@nonmembergroup:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "task-othergroup",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_task",
            "sys_id": "d0d522c65c706fd4e973124487d5a306",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-07",
            "fields": {
                "case": "8e8ba999d36f28846a3a63a1889b0794",
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-07 task on the othergroup parent",
                "type": "Review",
                "status": "Open",
                "assigned_to": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "due_date": "2026-12-31"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "party-othergroup",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case_party",
            "sys_id": "1549f71e383e795314639032274605b9",
            "prefix": null,
            "fields": {
                "case": "8e8ba999d36f28846a3a63a1889b0794",
                "party_type": "Person",
                "person": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent",
                "role_label": "Witness"
            }
        }
    ];

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        if (kind === 'nonmembergroup') { return nonMemberGroupId(key); }
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    chkTrue('a group the demo agent is NOT a member of was found for the negative branch',
        String(OTHER_GRP_ID).length === 32);
    var memberProbe = new GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember');
    memberProbe.addQuery('user', userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent'));
    memberProbe.addQuery('group', OTHER_GRP_ID);
    memberProbe.query();
    chk('the agent really is NOT a member of that group', '0', String(memberProbe.getRowCount()));
    var teamProbe = new GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember');
    teamProbe.addQuery('user', userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent'));
    teamProbe.addQuery('group', GRP_ID);
    teamProbe.query();
    chk('the demo agent IS a member of x_casemgmt_demo_team, so the positive group branch is real',
        '1', String(teamProbe.getRowCount()));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
