Queried by the "all tasks closed" guard subflow for the In Progress -> Resolved transition (../flows/sub_flows/validate_resolved_transition.xml, which delegates to ../script_includes/x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator.xml) via addQuery('case', current.sys_id).addQuery('status', '!=', 'Closed') - if any rows are returned the subflow returns a not-ok verdict carrying the literal text "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case." (AAP Section 0.7.4 verbatim), and the order-250 before-update business rule business_rules/x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions.xml turns that verdict into gs.addErrorMessage() + setAbortAction(true) so the message appears on the form and the save is blocked. Replaces ArkCase AcmTask.attachedToObjectId/attachedToObjectType polymorphic parent linkage; in this POC the parent is always a x_casemgmt_case row, so the polymorphism is collapsed into a single fixed-target reference. Used by case_agent "Assigned only" ACL conditions on x_casemgmt_case_task via the accessor current.getElement('case') to reach the parent case's assigned_agent / assigned_group (a literal current.case dot-walk cannot compile - 'case' is a JavaScript reserved word). Cascade rule is "none" - deleting a parent case does NOT auto-cascade-delete its child tasks (POC-safe default; manual cleanup Portal contract: lookup of an unknown number returns 404 with the verbatim message">7ab5876adb5664a2e51acd22c663ab76</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=06ce956d311e524e0606f3c64ccb499f"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>06ce956d311e524e0606f3c64ccb499f</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>9eee5d0d3059742f6742916bb023f3a7</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>06ce956d311e524e0606f3c64ccb499f</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>deaa9222b64d4d9c39a4c0c963a2a0a2</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }

    function anonCall(method, path, body) {
        var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2();
        r.setHttpMethod(method);
        r.setEndpoint(String(gs.getProperty('glide.servlet.uri')).replace(/\/$/, '') + path);
        r.setRequestHeader('Accept', 'application/json');
        if (body) {
            r.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
            r.setRequestBody(body);
        }
        var resp = r.execute();
        return { status: String(resp.getStatusCode()), body: String(resp.getBody() || '') };
    }

    var res = anonCall('get', '/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup?number=CASE9999999', null);
    chk('anonymous lookup status', '404', res.status);
    var body = JSON.parse(res.body).result;
    chk('the error message is verbatim', 'No case found with that number.', String(body.error));
    chk('the 404 body carries only the error key', 'error', Object.keys(body).sort().join(','));
    var empty = anonCall('get', '/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup', null);
    chk('a missing number parameter also answers 404', '404', empty.status);
    chk('the empty-parameter message is verbatim', 'No case found with that number.', String(JSON.parse(empty.body).result.error));
    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends. Emitted separately, the
    // evidence line below was written and then silently discarded, so the run output
    // never showed the value these assertions were made against.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('anonymous 404 body: ' + res.body);
    notes.push('genuinely anonymous 404 with no credentials: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'genuinely anonymous 404 with no credentials', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>

Transition Open to In Progress requires an assigned_agent in the assigned_group">02867a68434b5b09351e8a5d43b67223</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=681476b69b9d5938e51c0907f0a58411"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>681476b69b9d5938e51c0907f0a58411</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>6179ea5dc0958df2ca2d56826c0abc2e</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>681476b69b9d5938e51c0907f0a58411</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>b486b6c1463016c6143cad910efe72e5</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');

    var gr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    gr.get('d2b5064109ff252741f8c4c4d370b398');
    var v = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
    chkTrue('canTransitionToInProgress is true for a member agent', v.canTransitionToInProgress(gr).ok);
    chkTrue('isAgentInGroup is true for the demo agent', v.isAgentInGroup(AGT_ID, GRP_ID));
    chk('isAgentInGroup is false for the demo viewer', 'false', String(v.isAgentInGroup(VWR_ID, GRP_ID)));
    gr.setValue('assigned_agent', '');
    var none = v.canTransitionToInProgress(gr);
    chk('canTransitionToInProgress is false with no agent', 'false', String(none.ok));
    chkTrue('a blocking message is supplied', String(none.error || '').length > 0);
    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends. Emitted separately, the
    // evidence line below was written and then silently discarded, so the run output
    // never showed the value these assertions were made against.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('validator message: [' + none.error + ']');
    notes.push('validator verdict and group-membership helper: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'validator verdict and group-membership helper', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_atf_step"><sys_atf_step action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><callable_outputs/><copied_from/><description>Run Server Side Validation Script</description><display_name>Run Server Side Script</display_name><inputs/><mugshots_cache_json/><notes>A synthetic case the viewer has no relationship to</notes><order>1</order><step_config display_value="Run Server Side Script">41de4a935332120028bc29cac2dc349a</step_config><sys_class_name>sys_atf_step</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>7e054b9e0778b4cff2b63d15cec671db</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>Run Server Side Script</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_atf_step_7e054b9e0778b4cff2b63d15cec671db</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><table/><test display_value="ATF 04 - RBAC: x_casemgmt_case_viewer is read-only across all cases">be4d720d4d1f4225fb87e1ec63314d00</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=7e054b9e0778b4cff2b63d15cec671db"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>7e054b9e0778b4cff2b63d15cec671db</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>055d9ff25e1be02487673e0a533b742a</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    // Identities are resolved by user_name / name - never by sys_id literal.
    function userId(userName) {
        var u = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        u.addQuery('user_name', userName); u.setLimit(1); u.query();
        return u.next() ? u.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    function groupId(groupName) {
        var g = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
        g.addQuery('name', groupName); g.setLimit(1); g.query();
        return g.next() ? g.getUniqueValue() : '';
    }
    var MGR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_manager');
    var AGT_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_agent');
    var VWR_ID = userId('x_casemgmt_demo_viewer');
    var GRP_ID = groupId('x_casemgmt_demo_team');
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "other",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "cd17696587e11cb376a2964c217ff87f",
            "prefix": "ATF-RBAC-04",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-RBAC-04 assigned elsewhere",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        }
    ];

    // A field value written as "@user:<user_name>" or "@group:<name>" is resolved
    // here, at run time, so no identity sys_id is baked into the test definition.
    function resolveToken(v) {
        if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.charAt(0) !== '@') { return v; }
        var sep = v.indexOf(':');
        var kind = v.substring(1, sep), key = v.substring(sep + 1);
        return kind === 'user' ? userId(key) : groupId(key);
    }
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) { old.setWorkflow(false); old.deleteRecord(); }
    }
    for (var f = 0; f < FIX.length; f++) {
        var gr = new GlideRecord(FIX[f].table);
        gr.initialize();
        gr.setNewGuidValue(FIX[f].sys_id);
        for (var fld in FIX[f].fields) gr.setValue(fld, resolveToken(FIX[f].fields[fld]));
        var newId = gr.insert();
        chk('fixture ' + FIX[f].label + ' created', FIX[f].sys_id, newId);
    }
    stepResult.setOutputMessage('fixture setup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture setup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>7e054b9e0778b4cff2b63d15cec671db</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>c84405a43225c753f7801d4e08150002</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>

Field-level ACLs on assigned_group and assigned_agent">3fd9e4a1d92dad9b1aed0b58ca382bb5</test><timeout/><warning_message/></sys_atf_step><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=a762634f65908637d7752f1c22d4d8c2"/><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>a762634f65908637d7752f1c22d4d8c2</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>aa66b812e882261b1e6e7a5d96a74e6a</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>3.1</value><variable display_value="Jasmine version">42f2564b73031300440211d8faf6a777</variable></sys_variable_value><sys_variable_value action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><document>sys_atf_step</document><document_key>a762634f65908637d7752f1c22d4d8c2</document_key><order/><sys_class_name>sys_variable_value</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>f4f04dabc7fe8fee43f6616de0782f59</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><value>// x_casemgmt ATF - server-side assertion block.
// Aggregates every individual check and reports them through ONE assertion so
// that a failure message names precisely which expectation broke.
(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var fails = [], checks = 0;
    function chk(name, expected, actual) {
        checks++;
        if (String(expected) !== String(actual))
            fails.push(name + ' expected[' + expected + '] actual[' + actual + ']');
    }
    function chkTrue(name, actual) { chk(name, 'true', String(actual)); }
    function dict(table, element) {
        var d = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        d.addQuery('name', table); d.addQuery('element', element); d.setLimit(1); d.query();
        return d.next() ? d : null;
    }
    function choices(table, element) {
        var out = [], c = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
        c.addQuery('name', table); c.addQuery('element', element); c.orderBy('sequence'); c.query();
        while (c.next()) out.push(c.getValue('value'));
        return out;
    }
    var FIX = [
        {
            "label": "acl",
            "table": "x_casemgmt_case",
            "sys_id": "174bb5a31631f5fb4f95c14083aa1afd",
            "prefix": "ATF-ACL-05",
            "fields": {
                "subject": "ATF-ACL-05 field level acl",
                "description": "Synthetic ATF fixture record. No PII.",
                "requester_name": "ATF Synthetic Requester",
                "requester_email": "atf-fixture@example.invalid",
                "type": "General Inquiry",
                "status": "Draft",
                "priority": "Medium",
                "assigned_group": "@group:x_casemgmt_demo_team",
                "assigned_agent": "@user:x_casemgmt_demo_agent"
            }
        }
    ];

    // CLEANUP IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED.
    //
    // This step used to end with a "cleanup ran" check that compared the literal
    // string true against itself - a tautology. It therefore passed even when every
    // delete had
    // silently failed, so fixtures could survive and contaminate later steps, later
    // tests in the suite, and later runs (a stale pinned sys_id or a stale prefix row
    // makes another test assert against the wrong record). What follows checks the
    // outcome of each delete and then RE-QUERIES for residue, so a surviving row fails
    // this step and is named in the failure message.
    //
    // Note on coverage: a fixture carrying no `prefix` (case_party rows, which have no
    // `subject` column to match on) is swept by pinned sys_id only - the same guard the
    // delete loop uses - because that is the only key such a row is ever created with.
    var removed = 0, failedDeletes = [];
    for (var d = FIX.length - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
        var old = new GlideRecord(FIX[d].table);
        if (old.get(FIX[d].sys_id)) {
            old.setWorkflow(false);
            if (old.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[d].table + ':' + FIX[d].sys_id);
        }
    }
    for (var p = 0; p < FIX.length; p++) {
        if (!FIX[p].prefix) continue;
        var extra = new GlideRecord(FIX[p].table);
        extra.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[p].prefix);
        extra.query();
        while (extra.next()) {
            var extraId = extra.getUniqueValue();
            extra.setWorkflow(false);
            if (extra.deleteRecord()) removed++;
            else failedDeletes.push(FIX[p].table + ':' + extraId);
        }
    }
    chk('every delete reported success', '', failedDeletes.join(' | '));

    // Residue re-query: by pinned sys_id for every fixture, and by prefix for every
    // fixture that has one. Any row still present here is a real leak.
    var residue = [];
    for (var q = 0; q < FIX.length; q++) {
        var byId = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        if (byId.get(FIX[q].sys_id))
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' sys_id ' + FIX[q].sys_id + ' survived');
        if (!FIX[q].prefix) continue;
        var byPrefix = new GlideRecord(FIX[q].table);
        byPrefix.addQuery('subject', 'STARTSWITH', FIX[q].prefix);
        byPrefix.query();
        while (byPrefix.next())
            residue.push(FIX[q].table + ' ' + byPrefix.getUniqueValue() +
                ' [' + byPrefix.getValue('subject') + '] survived');
    }
    chk('no fixture residue remains after cleanup', '', residue.join(' | '));

    // setOutputMessage OVERWRITES rather than appends, so every reported
    // line is accumulated and emitted once, at the end of the step.
    var notes = [];
    notes.push('fixtures removed=' + removed +
        ' | deletes reporting failure=' + failedDeletes.length +
        ' | residue rows=' + residue.length);
    notes.push('fixture cleanup: checks=' + checks + ' failures=' + fails.length +
        (fails.length ? ' :: ' + fails.join(' | ') : ''));
    stepResult.setOutputMessage(notes.join('\n'));
    return assertEqual({ name: 'fixture cleanup', shouldbe: '', value: fails.join(' | ') });
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
</value><variable display_value="Test script">989d9e235324220002c6435723dc3484</variable></sys_variable_value></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_atf_test_afd33eebe6f49b746316b620f3886027
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_atf_test"><sys_atf_test action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><copied_from/><description>Agent row of the ACL matrix (AAP 0.5.6): create YES, read/write ASSIGNED ONLY, delete NO. "Assigned only" is exercised both ways - assigned_agent is the agent, and assigned_group contains the agent - plus the negative case of a case assigned to nobody. The negative WRITE is a genuine attempted write, not a query: step 8 attempts the update through GlideRecordSecure - the only scoped API that applies the write ACL - and asserts the stored row is unchanged. It is a script step rather than a native Record Update step because ATF's Record Update must first LOCATE the row, and the assigned-only read ACL already hides it from the agent, so that step aborts with "Unable to find record" instead of reaching an update-refused outcome. For this role read scope and write scope are the same set, so a case the agent can read but not write does not exist by design; the readable-row-with-forbidden-field case is covered by ATF 05.</description><enable_parameterized_testing>false</enable_parameterized_testing><fail_on_server_error>false</fail_on_server_error><name>ATF 03 - RBAC: x_casemgmt_case_agent create, ASSIGNED-ONLY read/write, no delete</name><parameters/><remember/><sn_atf_tg_generated>false</sn_atf_tg_generated><sys_class_name>sys_atf_test</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_id>afd33eebe6f49b746316b620f3886027</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>ATF 03 - RBAC: x_casemgmt_case_agent create, ASSIGNED-ONLY read/write, no delete</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_atf_test_afd33eebe6f49b746316b620f3886027</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><test_origin>manual</test_origin></sys_atf_test><sys_variable_value action="delete_multiple" query="document_key=afd33eebe6f49b746316b620f3886027"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>true</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case_task</collection><condition/><description>Before-insert and before-update on x_casemgmt_case_task: refuses any write that would store an empty mandatory case/subject/assigned_to/due_date, or a `case` reference that does not resolve to a live x_casemgmt_case row. Closes QA finding F15 for the task table, which carried NO business rule at all - all seven shipped rules are on x_casemgmt_case - so its mandatory and referential constraints existed only at the form layer. Measured before this rule: POST with case=deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef returned 201 (dangling mandatory reference) and POST with an empty case returned 201 (parentless task). Enforces AAP Section 0.5.7 (case/subject/assigned_to/due_date Mandatory) and Section 0.5.2 (case references resolve by key). The parent is resolved with plain GlideRecord, not GlideRecordSecure, so the rule tests EXISTENCE only and leaves authorization to the scoped ACLs of Section 0.5.6. Order=100; returns early on current.isActionAborted(); reproduces none of the four verbatim messages Section 0.7.4 fixes. Does not fire on delete, so the cascade rule on the case reference and the manager Delete grant are both untouched. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_validate_case_task_integrity</name><order>100</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Server-side backstop for AAP Section 0.5.7's MANDATORY contract and
    // AAP Section 0.5.2's resolvable-parent contract on
    // x_casemgmt_case_task.
    //
    // Before this rule the table carried NO business rule at all, so both
    // contracts lived only at the form layer. Measured as admin:
    //     POST {"case":"deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef", ...} -> HTTP 201
    //     POST {"case":"", ...}                                 -> HTTP 201
    // The first stored a dangling mandatory reference, the second a task
    // with no parent. Both are invisible to the "all tasks closed" gate in
    // x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator (which counts children by `case`)
    // and to the case form's Tasks related list, while still counting in
    // every task-table aggregate.

    // Stop if an earlier rule in the chain has already rejected this save.
    // setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, not the remaining before
    // rules; the platform keeps running them and reports the pending abort
    // through current.isActionAborted(). This is the only rule on this table
    // at authoring time, so the flag is normally false here; the guard is
    // the discipline every rule in this application follows and it keeps a
    // save refused by any future lower-ordered rule from collecting a
    // second, unrelated message.
    if (current.isActionAborted()) {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1 + 2. THE MANDATORY PARENT REFERENCE.
    //
    // Checked first because it is the constraint whose violation does the
    // most damage: the "In Progress -> Resolved" task-closure gate, the
    // Agent Workspace "My overdue tasks" report and the case form's Tasks
    // related list all reach this row THROUGH this column, so a row that
    // fails here is simultaneously invalid and unreachable from the
    // surfaces meant to police it.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var parentId = current.getValue('case');

    // getValue() returns the underlying sys_id String, or null when the
    // reference was never set. It is used in preference to property access
    // for two reasons: it has one documented return contract across
    // releases, and `case` is a reserved word in JavaScript, so
    // current.getValue('case') avoids relying on the ES5 allowance for
    // reserved words as property names.
    if (parentId === null || parentId === undefined || String(parentId).trim() === '') {
        // Target-side authored wording. AAP Section 0.7.4 fixes four
        // verbatim strings and none of them is a mandatory-field message,
        // so no other artifact's message is reproduced here. The field is
        // named by its dictionary column_label ('Case') so the refusal is
        // actionable for a caller who cannot see the form.
        gs.addErrorMessage('Case is mandatory: a task must reference the case it belongs to.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // EXISTENCE, NOT ACCESS. Plain GlideRecord is used deliberately in
    // place of GlideRecordSecure: the question is whether the parent row
    // exists, never whether the caller may read it. Access control on this
    // table is owned by the scoped ACLs of AAP Section 0.5.6 under ../acl/,
    // and AAP Section 0.7.3 Gate 3 is measured against those ACLs. A
    // read-ACL-aware lookup here would tell an x_casemgmt_case_agent
    // creating a task against a case outside their "Assigned only" read
    // scope that the CASE DOES NOT EXIST, masking the ACL that actually
    // governs the operation.
    //
    // The argument is the sys_id the CALLER supplied on the row being
    // written, read at run time - not a literal, so the AAP Section 0.7.2
    // no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint holds.
    var parentGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
    if (!parentGr.get(parentId)) {
        // A stored reference that resolves to nothing is the defect QA
        // finding F18 produced from the parent side and finding F15 from
        // this side. Such a row can never be saved from its own form,
        // because a mandatory reference cannot be re-filled from a value
        // that displays as blank.
        //
        // The wording deliberately differs from the anonymous portal
        // lookup's "No case found with that number." (owned by
        // x_casemgmt.CasePortalService, fixed verbatim by AAP Section
        // 0.7.4): that message answers an external requester searching by
        // case NUMBER, this one answers an internal caller who supplied an
        // unresolvable sys_id. Reusing it here would put a portal-facing
        // string on an internal write path and duplicate another
        // artifact's message.
        gs.addErrorMessage('The case this task references does not exist.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3 + 4 + 5. THE REMAINING MANDATORY COLUMNS from AAP Section 0.5.7.
    //
    // `label` is the column_label the dictionary carries
    // (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_task_subject.xml, _assigned_to.xml,
    // _due_date.xml), so the message names the field exactly as the caller
    // sees it on the form and in the list header.
    //
    // Deliberately NOT included: `type` and `status`. Section 0.5.7 marks
    // neither Mandatory, and `status` carries default_value='Open'
    // (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_task_status.xml) so it can never be
    // empty on insert. `number` is issued by the platform's Number
    // Maintenance subsystem during the insert pipeline and is read-only
    // thereafter.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var MANDATORY_FIELDS = [
        { element: 'subject', label: 'Subject' },
        { element: 'assigned_to', label: 'Assigned To' },
        { element: 'due_date', label: 'Due Date' }
    ];

    for (var i = 0; i < MANDATORY_FIELDS.length; i++) {
        // The value read is the value the row WOULD CARRY AFTER this write,
        // so a PATCH that touches only `status` on a conformant task reads
        // the stored subject, assigned_to and due_date and passes
        // untouched. Whitespace counts as empty for the same reason it does
        // on the case table: "Mandatory" is a statement about content, and
        // a space-only subject renders as a blank cell in the task list and
        // in the case form's Tasks related list.
        var value = current.getValue(MANDATORY_FIELDS[i].element);
        if (value === null || value === undefined || String(value).trim() === '') {
            gs.addErrorMessage(MANDATORY_FIELDS[i].label +
                ' is mandatory and cannot be empty.');
            current.setAbortAction(true);

            // Return on the FIRST violation: one actionable message is what
            // the form banner and the Table API response can each carry
            // legibly, and the caller re-submits after fixing it.
            return;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 6. THE ASSIGNEE REFERENCE MUST RESOLVE.
    //
    // The loop above proves assigned_to is non-empty; it does not prove it
    // points at a user who exists. Those are different contracts and the
    // second one was missing. Measured on this instance before this block:
    //     POST {"case":"<valid>", "subject":"x", "due_date":"2026-05-01",
    //           "assigned_to":"deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef"}  -> 201
    //     PATCH {"assigned_to":"deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef"}  -> 200
    // Both stored the unresolvable sys_id. The row then reads as an
    // assigned task everywhere it is counted - the task-table aggregates,
    // the case form's Tasks related list, the "all tasks closed" gate -
    // while its Assigned To cell renders blank and the Agent Workspace
    // "My overdue tasks" report can never match it for anybody, because
    // that report keys on assigned_to = gs.getUserID(). It is a task
    // nobody owns that still blocks case resolution.
    //
    // This closes the "referential" clause of AAP Section 0.5.7's contract
    // for this table. The parent `case` reference was already checked
    // above; this is the same check applied to the other reference column,
    // which is the half QA re-testing found still open.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!_referenceResolves('sys_user', current.getValue('assigned_to'))) {
        gs.addErrorMessage('Assigned To must reference a user that exists.');
        current.setAbortAction(true);
        return;
    }

    /**
     * Reports whether a supplied reference value points at a row that
     * exists, and does so WITHOUT ever converting "I am not allowed to
     * look" into "it is not there".
     *
     * The distinction is the whole point of this helper. A scoped script
     * reading a table outside its own scope depends on that table's
     * cross-scope access setting, and this application genuinely does
     * reference an out-of-box global table from scope
     * (x_casemgmt_case_party.organization -> core_company). If a
     * cross-scope restriction made the target table unreadable here, a
     * naive `if (!gr.get(id))` would read that as "the row is missing" and
     * would refuse EVERY write that carries a perfectly valid reference -
     * turning a validation improvement into a total outage of the
     * Organization party branch. So the helper only reports a missing row
     * when it can first demonstrate that it can read the table at all.
     *
     * Plain GlideRecord is deliberate, exactly as it is for the parent
     * `case` lookup above: the question is EXISTENCE, never ACCESS.
     * GlideRecordSecure would apply the caller's read ACLs and would tell
     * an x_casemgmt_case_agent that a user or company they are not
     * permitted to read "does not exist" - a false statement, and one that
     * would mask the ACL actually governing the operation. Access control
     * belongs to the scoped ACLs of AAP Section 0.5.6 under ../acl/.
     *
     * The sys_id argument is always the value the CALLER supplied on the
     * row being written, read at run time, so the AAP Section 0.7.2
     * no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint holds.
     *
     * @param {string} table - the reference target table name.
     * @param {string} sysId - the supplied reference value.
     * @return {boolean} true when the value is empty (presence is a
     *     separate contract, checked by the callers) or resolves, or when
     *     resolvability cannot be judged; false only when the table is
     *     demonstrably readable and the row is demonstrably absent.
     */
    function _referenceResolves(table, sysId) {
        var value = (sysId === null || sysId === undefined) ? '' : String(sysId).trim();
        if (value === '') {
            // Empty is not this check's business. Whether empty is legal is
            // a mandatory-field question and is answered by the callers.
            return true;
        }

        var probe = new GlideRecord(table);
        if (!probe.isValid()) {
            // The table is not addressable from this scope at all. Nothing
            // can be concluded about the row, so do not refuse the write.
            gs.info('x_casemgmt_validate_case_task_integrity: cannot address ' +
                table + ' from this scope; skipped the resolvability check ' +
                'for reference value ' + value + '.');
            return true;
        }
        if (probe.get(value)) {
            return true;
        }

        // The row did not come back. Before calling it absent, prove this
        // scope can read the table at all - otherwise an access restriction
        // masquerades as a missing row.
        var readable = new GlideRecord(table);
        readable.setLimit(1);
        readable.query();
        if (!readable.hasNext()) {
            gs.info('x_casemgmt_validate_case_task_integrity: ' + table +
                ' returned no rows at all, so the absence of ' + value +
                ' could not be distinguished from a read restriction; ' +
                'skipped the resolvability check.');
            return true;
        }

        return false;
    }
})(current, previous);

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_client_c6e53b45c50d4b9325f281b7876590bb
sys_update_xml.payload:
truefalseTwo behaviours for x_casemgmt_case, both from QA Issue 17. FIRST, it puts the form back in step with the database after an aborted submit: the platform re-renders an aborted save with the POSTED values, so setting Status to Draft on an Open case and pressing Update leaves the form showing Draft even though the write was refused with the verbatim "Cases cannot be returned to Draft." and nothing was persisted. The block reads the stored status published on g_scratchpad by the display Business Rule ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_case_display_stored_state.xml, which obtains it by re-reading the row from the database by its own sys_id, and calls g_form.setValue('status', stored) only when the rendered value and the stored value disagree. Fail-safe: no scratchpad, an empty or unrecognised value, status absent from the form, values already equal or any exception are all silent no-ops that change nothing. It clears no message and does not reload: AAP Section 0.5.5 requires the blocking error to stay on the form, and g_form.setValue does not touch the message area. It runs before the lockdown below so the terminal-status test is made against the stored status and so the control is corrected before it is made inert. SECOND, the terminal-state form lockdown: on load, when status is Closed, disables the ten writable fields (subject, type, status, priority, description, requester_name, requester_email, assigned_group, assigned_agent, pending_reason) through g_form.setDisabled, and additionally sets the DOM disabled property on Choice controls because the platform's client-side read-only treatment sets only the inert HTML readonly attribute on a select. Backs up ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_closed_readonly.xml, whose description action has no runtime effect on this release: measured on CASE9000006, g_form.isDisabled('description') returned false and the textarea was editable while the other nine fields were protected, correlating with the platform's repeated "renderNACMFieldLevel is not defined" text-area exception in runBeforeRender. Does not touch a non-Closed form (early return) and does not remove the Update verb, because AAP Section 0.5.5 requires the blocking message "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified." to be surfaced on an attempt. Enforcement of the rule itself remains server-side in ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed.xml; this record governs only what the form presents. Per AAP Sections 0.4.4, 0.5.5 and 0.7.2.truefalsex_casemgmt_case_closed_readonly_enforce200sys_script_clientadmin2025-01-01 00:00:00global/c6e53b45c50d4b9325f281b7876590bb0x_casemgmt_case_closed_readonly_enforce82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_script_client_c6e53b45c50d4b9325f281b7876590bbadmin2025-01-01 00:00:00x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_opentruefalseUI Action that transitions a Draft case to Open status. Visible only to x_casemgmt_case_manager users on cases with status=Draft. Delegates the assigned_group-populated check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToOpen() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_open_transition.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 1 verbatim: "Draft -> Open: assigned_group populated - Surface form-level error". Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the assigned_group field that the operator should have populated on the form before clicking. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role and status. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if assigned_group is empty (verbatim message "Required field assigned_group is empty." returned by the Script Include). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII.new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().canShowManagerAction(current, 'Draft')truetruefalsefalsefalsefalseprimaryfalseOpen this case (assigned_group must be populated; case_manager role required).truefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalseOpen100falsefalsefalsetruesys_ui_actionsystem2025-01-01 00:00:00global/2d897ab4b680731b3da534c9a667c6581Open82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_ui_action_2d897ab4b680731b3da534c9a667c658admin2026-09-10 05:45:34x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_0ee339c18d12366737a3637b952fe75b
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>false</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-update guard on x_casemgmt_case: blocks ANY transition out of the Closed terminal status. When previous.status === 'Closed', delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition(previousStatus, newStatus) and surfaces the verbatim error message 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true) when the validator returns {ok: false}. Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 8: 'Closed -> *: PROHIBITED -- terminal state') and 0.7.4 (verbatim error message - non-negotiable). Order=100 is the HIGHEST priority before-update rule in this scoped application; it runs FIRST so that its verbatim message is the one surfaced when the case is already Closed. setAbortAction(true) cancels the write but not the chain - the later rules (block_draft_backtransition at 200, enforce_forward_transitions at 250, validate_assigned_agent_membership at 300, clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at 400, set_closed_date at 500) still run and each returns early on current.isActionAborted(). The Script Include is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the verbatim error message; this BR contains zero inline error strings. action_insert=false because new cases always start at Draft (per dictionary default_value); only updates on already-Closed rows trigger this guard. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. When the status itself is unchanged, the rule then calls x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateClosedRecordUnchanged(current, previous), which compares the case's own columns and surfaces the same verbatim message when any of them changed - so a Closed row is immutable in fact and not only in wording, while a genuine no-op save (nothing edited) still succeeds. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types. Defense in depth: the per-type Flow Designer flows do NOT enforce this rule, so this BR is the only enforcer for direct DB modifications via Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, and bulk imports. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed</name><order>100</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 8):
    //     "Closed -> *: PROHIBITED -- terminal state"
    //     Failure surface: "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified."
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.7.4: the literal text "Closed cases are terminal and
    // cannot be modified." is the VERBATIM, NON-NEGOTIABLE error message
    // surfaced when this guard fires. Character-for-character: capital "C",
    // trailing period, exact wording. The message lives ONCE in the Script
    // Include's validateNoBacktransition() return; this BR reads it from
    // result.error and never inlines it.
    //
    // Order=100 makes this the FIRST/HIGHEST-PRIORITY before-update rule
    // in this scoped application, so its verbatim message is the first one
    // the user reads. It does not stop the rest of the chain:
    // setAbortAction(true) cancels the WRITE, and the platform keeps running
    // the remaining before-update rules (enforce_forward_transitions at 250,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at 300,
    // clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at 400, set_closed_date at 500),
    // each of which checks current.isActionAborted() itself and returns.
    // Running first is still intentional: it is the cheapest path to reject
    // an invalid update.
    //
    // Delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition()
    // which returns { ok: true } when the transition is allowed, or
    // { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' }
    // when transitioning OUT of Closed (i.e., prev === 'Closed' &&
    // next !== 'Closed' && next !== ''). The Script Include is the single
    // source of truth for the verbatim message and the prohibited-transition
    // matrix; this BR consumes its return shape and surfaces the error.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: ChangeCaseFileStateService at
    // acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    // armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java
    // handled state changes via changeCaseState() (line 95: setStatus,
    // line 99: setClosed for CLOSED transitions) but did NOT enforce a
    // "Closed is terminal" rule - the ArkCase service would happily transition
    // a Closed case to any other status. Terminal-state behavior was implicit
    // in Activiti BPMN process definitions and queue handlers. This BR makes
    // the rule EXPLICIT at the data layer, hardening the state-machine contract
    // per AAP Section 0.5.5.

    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts (scheduled jobs invoking
    // GlideRecord.update(), some bulk import scenarios, server-side script
    // paths that call GlideRecord.updateMultiple()). If there is no previous
    // state, no terminal state can be detected, and the rule does nothing.
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string for
    // safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases. The Title Case literal
    // 'Closed' (6 chars, single word) is the verbatim choice value from
    // ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml per AAP Section 0.5.7. Variants
    // like 'CLOSED' (uppercase, ArkCase Java legacy), 'closed' (lowercase),
    // or 'Close' (no trailing 'd') would silently never match.
    var prevStatus = String(previous.status);
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Only fire when previous.status is Closed - a row that is not in the
    // terminal state is none of this rule's business.
    //
    // TWO QUESTIONS ARE ASKED, IN ORDER, because AAP Section 0.5.5 row 8
    // makes two promises and this rule used to keep only the first:
    //
    //   1) validateNoBacktransition(prev, next) - is the STATUS being moved
    //      out of Closed? Returns { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are
    //      terminal and cannot be modified.' } when prev === 'Closed' &&
    //      next !== 'Closed' && next !== '', and { ok: true } for the
    //      no-op Closed -> Closed case.
    //
    //   2) validateClosedRecordUnchanged(current, previous) - if the status
    //      is unchanged, is any OTHER column of the case being rewritten?
    //      Until this call existed, the answer did not matter: a save that
    //      left `status` alone and changed `priority`, `subject`, or that
    //      cleared `assigned_agent`, committed silently on a Closed case,
    //      which contradicted the very message this rule surfaces and the
    //      four in-scope documents that quote it. The record the platform
    //      told the user "cannot be modified" was in fact freely editable.
    //      The method compares only the application's own columns, so a
    //      genuine no-op save (Update pressed with nothing edited) still
    //      succeeds - sys_mod_count and sys_updated_on are deliberately not
    //      compared.
    //
    // The two calls are chained rather than combined so that a status move
    // out of Closed keeps producing the message it always produced, and so
    // that each method keeps a single, testable responsibility.
    if (prevStatus === 'Closed') {
        // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
        // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
        // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the `CaseTransitionValidator`
        // portion is the api_name of the Script Include. NO sys_id literal -
        // the resolution is by scoped class name only.
        var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
        var result = validator.validateNoBacktransition(prevStatus, newStatus);
        if (result.ok) {
            // The status itself is not moving. The row is still terminal, so
            // reject any change to the case's own fields. Both methods return
            // the same verbatim string for a rejection, so the user sees one
            // consistent sentence whichever half of the promise was broken.
            result = validator.validateClosedRecordUnchanged(current, previous);
        }
        if (!result.ok) {
            // gs.addErrorMessage(result.error) surfaces the verbatim message
            // at the top of the form when the user attempts the save through
            // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
            // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. The string is read from
            // result.error - never inlined here - so the verbatim wording
            // contract is enforced by the Script Include alone.
            gs.addErrorMessage(result.error);
            // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
            // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
            // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
            // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
            // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
            // would still update; without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write
            // would be silently rejected with no visible failure.
            current.setAbortAction(true);
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>0ee339c18d12366737a3637b952fe75b</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=0ee339c18d12366737a3637b952fe75b"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_start_progresstruefalseUI Action that transitions an Open case to In Progress status. Visible to x_casemgmt_case_manager (always) and x_casemgmt_case_agent (only when they are assigned to the case via assigned_agent or member of assigned_group, per AAP Section 0.5.6 Assigned-only rule). Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the assigned_agent and assigned_group fields that the operator should have populated on the form before clicking. Delegates the assigned_agent-populated AND member-of-assigned_group check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToInProgress() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_inprogress_transition.xml and ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 2 verbatim: "Open -> In Progress: assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group - Surface form-level error". Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role, status, and "Assigned only" assignment. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if any guard fails (verbatim message returned by the Script Include). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII.new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().canShowAction(current, 'Open')truetruefalsefalsefalsefalseprimaryfalseStart working on this case (assigned_agent must be populated and a member of assigned_group).truefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalsefalseStart Progress200falsefalsefalsetruesys_ui_actionsystem2025-01-01 00:00:00global/e77dc24317a301765a60a3673ec7d1640x_casemgmt_case_start_progress82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5afsys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_start_progresssystem2025-01-01 00:00:00x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.name: sys_script_6396a298689f7e5a5b41ff6afcece502
sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><abort_action>false</abort_action><access>package_private</access><action_delete>false</action_delete><action_insert>false</action_insert><action_query>false</action_query><action_update>true</action_update><active>true</active><add_message>false</add_message><advanced>true</advanced><change_fields>false</change_fields><client_callable>false</client_callable><collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection><condition/><description>Before-update guard on x_casemgmt_case: blocks any transition from a non-Draft status back to Draft. When current.status === 'Draft' AND previous.status !== 'Draft' AND previous.status !== '', delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition(previousStatus, newStatus) and surfaces the verbatim error message 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true) when the validator returns {ok: false}. Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 7: 'Any -> Draft: PROHIBITED') and 0.7.4 (verbatim error message - non-negotiable). Order=200 is the SECOND-HIGHEST priority before-update rule in this scoped application; it runs AFTER block_terminal_closed (order=100), whose message wins for an already-Closed case, and BEFORE enforce_forward_transitions (250), validate_assigned_agent_membership (300), clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress (400) and set_closed_date (500). Those later rules still execute after an abort - setAbortAction(true) cancels the write, not the chain - and each returns early on current.isActionAborted(). The Script Include is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the verbatim error message; this BR contains zero inline error strings. action_insert=false because Draft is the legitimate initial status (per dictionary default_value); only the BACK-transition from a non-Draft state is forbidden. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Skip-if-no-change guard (prevStatus === newStatus) avoids unnecessary Script Include instantiation on non-status-changing updates. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types. Defense in depth: the per-type Flow Designer flows do NOT enforce this rule, so this BR is the only enforcer for direct DB modifications via Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, and bulk imports. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals.</description><execute_function>false</execute_function><filter_condition/><is_rest>false</is_rest><message/><name>x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition</name><order>200</order><priority>100</priority><rest_method/><rest_method_text/><rest_service/><rest_service_text/><rest_variables/><role_conditions/><script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 7):
    //     "Any -> Draft: PROHIBITED"
    //     Failure surface: "Cases cannot be returned to Draft."
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.7.4: the literal text "Cases cannot be returned to
    // Draft." is the VERBATIM, NON-NEGOTIABLE error message surfaced when
    // this guard fires. Character-for-character: capital "C", capital "D",
    // trailing period, exact wording. The message lives ONCE in the Script
    // Include's validateNoBacktransition() return; this BR reads it from
    // result.error and never inlines it.
    //
    // Order=200 makes this the SECOND before-update rule in this scoped
    // application. Order=100 (block_terminal_closed) runs first to catch
    // the more aggressive Closed-terminal prohibition; once that rule has
    // confirmed the case is not Closed, this rule fires at order=200 to
    // catch the more specific Any->Draft case. Subsequent rules
    // (enforce_forward_transitions at 250,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at 300,
    // clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at 400, set_closed_date at 500)
    // still RUN when this rule aborts - setAbortAction(true) cancels the
    // WRITE, not the chain - and each of them returns early on
    // current.isActionAborted(), so only this rule's message is surfaced.
    //
    // Delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition()
    // which returns { ok: true } when the transition is allowed, or
    // { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' } when
    // transitioning TO Draft from a non-Draft state (prev !== '' &&
    // prev !== 'Draft' && next === 'Draft'). The Script Include is the
    // single source of truth for the verbatim message and the prohibited
    // -transition matrix; this BR consumes its return shape and surfaces
    // the error.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: ChangeCaseFileStateService at
    // acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    // armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java
    // handled state changes via changeCaseState() (line 95: setStatus)
    // without enforcing a Draft-backtransition rule. Backtransition behavior
    // was implicit in Activiti BPMN process definitions and queue handlers
    // (e.g., CaseFileQueueHandler.java set status to ACTIVE pre-save). This
    // BR makes the rule EXPLICIT at the data layer, hardening the
    // state-machine contract per AAP Section 0.5.5.

    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts (scheduled jobs invoking
    // GlideRecord.update(), some bulk import scenarios, server-side script
    // paths that call GlideRecord.updateMultiple()). If there is no previous
    // state, no transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing.
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string for
    // safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases. The Title Case literal
    // 'Draft' (5 chars, single word) is the verbatim choice value from
    // ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml per AAP Section 0.5.7. Variants
    // like 'DRAFT' (uppercase, ArkCase Java legacy from CaseFile.java
    // @PrePersist hook), 'draft' (lowercase), or 'Drafting' (extended)
    // would silently never match.
    var prevStatus = String(previous.status);
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Skip if status didn't change - this rule only cares about transitions.
    // Avoids unnecessary Script Include instantiation on the vast majority
    // of UPDATE operations (those that don't change the status field).
    if (prevStatus === newStatus) {
        return;
    }

    // Only fire when transitioning TO Draft from a non-Draft non-empty state.
    // Three conditions, all required:
    //   (1) newStatus === 'Draft'           - we're transitioning toward Draft
    //   (2) prevStatus !== 'Draft'          - we're moving FROM a non-Draft state
    //   (3) prevStatus !== ''               - defensive: empty previousStatus
    //                                         on a brand-new record can't reach
    //                                         this BR because action_insert is
    //                                         false; this guard is belt-and-
    //                                         suspenders for unusual contexts
    //                                         where the platform might emit an
    //                                         empty-string previous.status on a
    //                                         pseudo-update.
    // This BR's pre-check is redundant with the Script Include's authoritative
    // matrix but acts as a fast-path filter to avoid Script Include
    // instantiation cost on the vast majority of updates. Defense in depth:
    // if this pre-check were ever loosened, the Script Include's matrix
    // would still produce the correct result.
    if (newStatus === 'Draft' && prevStatus !== 'Draft' && prevStatus !== '') {
        // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
        // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
        // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the
        // `CaseTransitionValidator` portion is the api_name of the Script
        // Include. NO sys_id literal - the resolution is by scoped class
        // name only.
        var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
        var result = validator.validateNoBacktransition(prevStatus, newStatus);
        if (!result.ok) {
            // gs.addErrorMessage(result.error) surfaces the verbatim message
            // at the top of the form when the user attempts the save through
            // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
            // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. The string is read from
            // result.error - never inlined here - so the verbatim wording
            // contract is enforced by the Script Include alone.
            gs.addErrorMessage(result.error);
            // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
            // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
            // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
            // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
            // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
            // would still update; without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write
            // would be silently rejected with no visible failure.
            current.setAbortAction(true);
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>system</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on><sys_domain>global</sys_domain><sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path><sys_id>6396a298689f7e5a5b41ff6afcece502</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition</sys_name><sys_overrides/><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>system</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on><template/><when>before</when></sys_script><sys_translated_text action="delete_multiple" query="documentkey=6396a298689f7e5a5b41ff6afcece502"/></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: sys_security_acl_a76cdd65e47612e82ec81a0ba19bc7c8
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_security_acl"><sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides><advanced>false</advanced><applies_to/><condition/><controlled_by_refs/><decision_type>allow</decision_type><description>Field-level ACL granting the query_range operation on x_casemgmt_case.opened_date to x_casemgmt_case_manager, x_casemgmt_case_agent and x_casemgmt_case_viewer. Authored for QA finding F17, which reported every range predicate on this column (>, <, BETWEEN, 'at or after', 'last 30 days') being dropped from the query for non-admin callers - 0 rows plus a server ACL banner naming the query_range operation inside an HTTP 200 list page, and HTTP 403 'Insufficient rights to query records' over the Table API. Retained as an explicit scoped grant rather than a proven repair: re-verification could not reproduce the refusal, and a differential probe measured no difference against columns carrying no such ACL, so this record makes the range filtering implied by AAP Section 0.5.6 'Read - All' independent of the instance's default query_range posture. query_range shapes the query only; which rows are returned remains governed by each role's read ACL, so the agent still sees just its assigned set.</description><local_or_existing>Existing</local_or_existing><name>x_casemgmt_case.opened_date</name><operation display_value="query_range">e66cf897b7300210240b06dd1e11a9fd</operation><script/><security_attribute/><sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-10 00:21:46</sys_created_on><sys_id>a76cdd65e47612e82ec81a0ba19bc7c8</sys_id><sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_casemgmt_case.opened_date</sys_name><sys_package display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="x_casemgmt Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_a76cdd65e47612e82ec81a0ba19bc7c8</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-10 03:30:24</sys_updated_on><type display_value="record">record</type></sys_security_acl></record_update>
